meat-01.title: Boiled Meats & Poultry with Golden Aromatic Broth
meat-01.culturalNotes: Dr. Fatma emphasizes starting with a light sear of aromatics in baladi ghee before adding boiling water, resulting in an exceptionally rich, clear golden broth without cloudiness.

mp1-1.name: Fresh beef cuts or whole chicken
mp1-1.standardAmount: 1 kg meat cuts or 1 whole chicken

mp1-6.name: Aromatic spices (cardamom, salt, black pepper)
mp1-6.standardAmount: Sea salt, cracked black pepper & crushed cardamom

instructions.1: Wash the meat or chicken thoroughly. A quick rinse with a splash of white vinegar ensures pristine cleanliness and tenderizes the meat fibers.
instructions.2: Heat baladi ghee in a deep heavy pot. Lightly sauté the onion, tomato, garlic clove, and cracked cardamom until fragrant without browning.
instructions.3: Add the meat or poultry pieces to the hot aromatics, turning to sear and seal in natural juices for richer flavor.
instructions.4: Pour boiling water over the seared meat. Bring to a vigorous boil and skim off any surface foam (zeem) to keep the broth crystal clear.
instructions.5: Lower the heat, cover the pot, and simmer gently until meat is fork-tender. Season with salt only toward the final minutes to preserve tenderness.

meat-02.title: Egyptian Rabbit (Boiled, Kabab Halla, or Tomato Stew)
meat-02.culturalNotes: Rabbit broth is historically celebrated as the finest companion for authentic Egyptian Molokhia. Dr. Fatma documents three traditional variations: clear broth boiling, caramelized onion braising, and rich tomato reduction.

mp2-6.name: Vinegar, cardamom & spices
mp2-6.standardAmount: 1 tbsp vinegar, sea salt, black pepper, cardamom

instructions.1: Thoroughly rinse rabbit pieces in cold water with vinegar and lemon. Drain and pat dry completely.
instructions.2: Method 1 (Boiling for Molokhia): Sauté onions with cardamom in ghee, sear rabbit pieces lightly, then add boiling water and simmer gently for clear broth.
instructions.3: Method 2 (Kabab Halla style): Sauté rabbit with generous caramelized onions and garlic over low heat, adding warm water in small increments until tender.
instructions.4: Method 3 (Tomato Stew - Bil Dam'a): Sauté garlic in ghee, pour strained tomato juice, simmer until reduced, then add cooked rabbit to absorb the tangy sauce.

meat-03.title: Kabab Halla (Egyptian Beef Stew with Potatoes)
meat-03.culturalNotes: The secret to authentic Kabab Halla lies in using an equal weight of onions to meat, cooked patiently until deeply caramelized into a velvety mahogany gravy.

mp3-6.name: Traditional Kabab spices & salt
mp3-6.standardAmount: Black pepper, allspice, cardamom, sea salt

instructions.1: Melt baladi ghee in a heavy pot. Add onions with a pinch of black pepper, cooking over medium heat until deep golden brown.
instructions.2: Add beef cubes to the caramelized onions, searing on high heat until browned on all sides.
instructions.3: Progressive braising (Shaqshaq): Add boiling water 1/4 cup at a time. Cover and cook over low heat, adding water each time the liquid is absorbed.
instructions.4: When meat is three-quarters cooked, add potato cubes and minced garlic so they cook in the rich onion gravy.
instructions.5: Add salt and allspice. Simmer until sauce is thick and velvety, coating the back of a spoon.

meat-04.title: Classic Minced Meat Filling (Assag)
meat-04.culturalNotes: Assag is the cornerstone savory filling of Egyptian home cooking, used inside Macaroni Béchamel, Goulash pastries, stuffed vegetables, and potato bakes.

mp4-4.name: Traditional Assag spices
mp4-4.standardAmount: Salt, black pepper, pinch of cinnamon & nutmeg

instructions.1: Melt ghee in a wide skillet, soften onions until translucent, then add minced meat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon.
instructions.2: Add black pepper, salt, and spices. Cook over medium-low heat until moisture evaporates and meat is cooked and fragrant.

meat-05.title: Burghul Meat Kofta with Charcoal Aroma
meat-05.culturalNotes: Fine cracked burghul gives Egyptian kofta its signature tender bite and moisture, while the final drop of ghee on glowing charcoal delivers genuine bazaar barbecue fragrance.

mp5-2.name: Fine wheat burghul
mp5-2.standardAmount: 1/2 cup fine burghul, washed and drained

mp5-5.name: Traditional kofta spice blend
mp5-5.standardAmount: Salt, black pepper, 7-spices, pinch of cinnamon

instructions.1: Rinse fine burghul in warm water, drain completely, and let rest 15 minutes to soften without soaking in excess liquid.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, mix minced meat, burghul, grated onion pulp, garlic, spices, and baking powder. Knead vigorously for 5 minutes until sticky and homogenous.
instructions.3: Shape onto skewers or into fingers, moistening hands with the reserved onion juice to produce a smooth, glossy surface.
instructions.4: Grill over hot coals or bake on a greased tray under the oven broiler, turning until nicely browned on all sides.
instructions.5: Place glowing charcoal on foil in the baking dish, drizzle a drop of ghee, cover immediately for 5 minutes to infuse charcoal aroma.

meat-06.title: Alexandrian Style Spiced Liver (Kebda Eskandarani)
meat-06.culturalNotes: Alexandrian liver requires a blazing hot skillet and lightning-fast cooking. Overcooking toughens liver, whereas high heat seals in sweetness alongside garlic, cumin, and fiery green peppers.

mp6-1.name: Beef liver sliced in thin strips

mp6-5.name: Fresh lemon juice and white vinegar

mp6-6.name: Spices (cumin, coriander, salt, pepper)
mp6-6.standardAmount: Ground cumin, dry coriander, salt, black pepper

instructions.1: Toss sliced liver with half the minced garlic, vinegar, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Do not wash liver with water.
instructions.2: Heat oil in a wide skillet until smoking hot. Add remaining garlic and green peppers, tossing for 30 seconds.
instructions.3: Add liver in a single layer over high heat. Stir quickly for 3 to 5 minutes only to maintain tender texture.
instructions.4: Remove immediately from heat, squeeze extra lemon juice over the top, and serve piping hot in baladi bread or fino rolls with tahini.

meat-07.title: Stuffed Pigeon with Rice or Freekeh (Hamam Mahshi)
meat-07.culturalNotes: Stuffed pigeon is considered the crown jewel of Egyptian hospitality. The skin is separated with surgical precision, stuffed with spiced rice or green freekeh, and crisped in baladi ghee.

mp7-6.name: Aromatic spices
mp7-6.standardAmount: Cracked black pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, salt

instructions.1: Sauté onion and chopped giblets in ghee, add washed rice or freekeh with spices, cook halfway with a splash of water, then cool completely.
instructions.2: Gently loosen pigeon skin from breast, stuff cavity and under skin without overfilling to prevent bursting during cooking.
instructions.3: Poach stuffed pigeons in simmering water with aromatics (onion, cardamom, bay leaf) on low heat for 35-40 minutes.
instructions.4: Remove, pat dry completely, and fry in hot baladi ghee until skin is crisp and deep mahogany golden.

sea-01.title: Egyptian Fried Fish (Flour Dusted or Breaded)
sea-01.culturalNotes: Alexandria's fishmongers season the fish with fresh garlic, cumin, and vinegar, then dredge in flour and starch for a blisteringly crisp exterior and tender, juicy flesh.

sf1-2.name: Alexandrian garlic Daqqa marinade
sf1-2.standardAmount: Garlic, cumin, coriander, lemon, vinegar, chili, salt

instructions.1: Score thick fish diagonally on both sides for even cooking and spice absorption.
instructions.2: Rub the garlic, cumin, lemon, vinegar, and chili paste deep inside cavity and scores. Rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Mix flour with cornstarch, salt, and cumin. Coat fish evenly, shaking off excess flour.
instructions.4: Quickly dip floured fish in cold water for a split second before placing in hot oil for shatteringly crisp skin without burning oil.
instructions.5: Fry in clean hot oil over medium-high heat until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.

sea-02.title: Egyptian Grilled Mullet (Samak Mashwi with Radda & Garlic Doffa)
sea-02.culturalNotes: Egypt's iconic street fish preparation: scaled mullet coated generously in wheat bran (Radda), grilled over intense heat, and plunged sizzling hot into an aromatic vinegar-lemon-garlic bath.

sf2-1.name: Fresh whole grey mullet with scales

sf2-3.name: Aromatic stuffing herbs & vegetables
sf2-3.standardAmount: Onion, parsley, celery, garlic, tomato, chili

sf2-4.name: Alexandrian boiling Doffa bath
sf2-4.standardAmount: Garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, water, cumin, salt

instructions.1: Clean fish cavity while keeping scales intact on skin to protect flesh during fierce dry grilling.
instructions.2: Stuff cavity with chopped onion, parsley, celery, garlic, tomato, and spices.
instructions.3: Coat the whole fish completely in fine wheat bran until no moist skin is visible.
instructions.4: Grill on a searing cast-iron griddle or open coals, flipping once when bran is blackened and charred.
instructions.5: As soon as fish leaves grill piping hot, immerse for 15 seconds in the fragrant lemon-garlic-vinegar bath, then lift onto platter.

sea-03.title: Shrimp Sayadia with Spiced Brown Rice
sea-03.culturalNotes: Originating from Suez and Port Said, Sayadia achieves its mahogany color from deeply caramelized onions boiled down into a rich, fragrant cumin broth that infuses the short-grain rice and tender shrimp.

sf3-6.name: Sayadia spices (cumin, cinnamon, salt)
sf3-6.standardAmount: Ground cumin, black pepper, salt, pinch of cinnamon

instructions.1: Fry onions in oil over medium heat, stirring continuously until dark reddish-brown (mahogany), taking care not to burn.
instructions.2: Pour boiling water or broth over caramelized onions. Boil for 5 minutes until liquid turns deep amber-brown.
instructions.3: In a separate pan, quickly sauté shrimp with garlic and cumin for 2 minutes.
instructions.4: Add washed rice to the boiling brown onion stock. Season with cumin, salt, and pepper.
instructions.5: When rice absorbs liquid, fold in sautéed shrimp, reduce heat to lowest setting, cover and steam for 15 minutes.

sea-04.title: Crispy Fried Calamari (Squid Rings / Strips)
sea-04.culturalNotes: Dr. Fatma's rule for perfect calamari: flash-frying for 2 to 3 minutes in hot oil. Any longer will make the squid tough and rubbery.

sf4-2.name: Garlic, lemon & cumin marinade
sf4-2.standardAmount: Minced garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, salt

instructions.1: Toss cleaned squid rings with garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and salt for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Combine flour, cornstarch, and baking powder in a shallow bowl.
instructions.3: Toss squid in flour mixture, shaking vigorously in a colander to remove excess.
instructions.4: Drop in hot oil in small batches. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes only until crisp and pale golden. Overcooking makes squid rubbery.
instructions.5: Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with sea salt, and serve with fresh lemon and tahini.

soup-01.title: Vegetable Soup (Clear Broth or Creamy Milk & Dill)
soup-01.culturalNotes: A nourishing Egyptian staple. The aromatic mastic and cardamom pods provide an irreplaceable floral depth to the vegetable broth.

ss1-1.name: Assorted fresh seasonal vegetables
ss1-1.standardAmount: 3 cups diced zucchini, carrots, potatoes, celery & peas

ss1-5.name: Mastic tears, cardamom & salt
ss1-5.standardAmount: 2 mastic tears, cardamom pods, salt, white pepper

ss1-6.name: Fresh whole milk and chopped dill
ss1-6.standardAmount: 1 cup milk + 2 tbsp dill (for creamy variation)

instructions.1: Melt butter or ghee in pot. Sauté onion with mastic and cardamom until fragrant.
instructions.2: Add carrots and potatoes first (firmer vegetables), sauté for 3 minutes, then add zucchini, peas, and celery.
instructions.3: Pour boiling broth over vegetables, cover, and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender.
instructions.4: Creamy milk variation (Optional): Whisk in fresh milk and a spoonful of flour, simmer for 3 minutes, and stir in chopped fresh dill before serving.
instructions.5: Serve hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

soup-02.title: Egyptian Yellow Lentil Soup with Crispy Croutons
soup-02.culturalNotes: The quintessential winter warmer of Egypt. Slow-cooked lentils pureed with carrots, garlic, and cumin, enriched with golden toasted vermicelli and crispy baladi bread.

ss2-6.name: Lentil spices (cumin, black pepper, salt, turmeric)
ss2-6.standardAmount: 1 tbsp ground cumin, salt, pepper, pinch of turmeric

instructions.1: Combine rinsed lentils, carrots, tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a pot with broth or water. Boil until lentils and carrots are completely soft.
instructions.2: Blend soup until silky smooth using an immersion blender or countertop blender. Return to pot.
instructions.3: In a small pan, brown vermicelli in ghee until golden, then pour into simmering soup.
instructions.4: Add cumin, salt, black pepper, and turmeric. Simmer on low heat for 7-10 minutes until vermicelli is cooked.
instructions.5: Sauté minced garlic in ghee with dry coriander, pour over soup with a sizzle.
instructions.6: Serve in deep bowls accompanied by crispy toasted baladi bread croutons and fresh lemon wedges.

salad-01.title: Egyptian Tahini Salad (Classic Garlic & Pickled Onion)
salad-01.culturalNotes: Tahini is the universal Egyptian table condiment. Gradual whisking with warm water and vinegar transforms raw sesame paste into a light, velvety dip.

ss3-5.name: Spices (cumin, sea salt, chili)
ss3-5.standardAmount: Ground cumin, salt, pinch of red pepper

ss3-6.name: Finely diced onion marinated in vinegar

instructions.1: Place tahini in a glass bowl. Gradually whisk in warm water; tahini will thicken first, then turn into a smooth, creamy light emulsion.
instructions.2: Pour in vinegar and lemon juice while whisking until silky and pale ivory.
instructions.3: Stir in minced garlic, ground cumin, salt, and red chili powder.
instructions.4: Fold in finely diced red onion that has been macerated in vinegar for 5 minutes for a tangy crunch.

salad-02.title: Baba Ghanoush (Smoked Roasted Eggplant with Tahini)
salad-02.culturalNotes: Direct open flame charring collapses the eggplant and imparts the inimitable smoky aroma essential to true Egyptian Baba Ghanoush.

ss4-6.name: Spices (cumin, salt, paprika, parsley)
ss4-6.standardAmount: Ground cumin, salt, paprika, fresh parsley

instructions.1: Roast eggplants directly over open gas flame or hot coals, turning until skin is completely charred and flesh is collapsed and smoky.
instructions.2: Cool in a covered bowl, then peel charred skin. Drain excess bitter water.
instructions.3: Mash eggplant flesh with a fork or mortar for rustic texture (avoid food processor to preserve texture).
instructions.4: Mix tahini with lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, and salt, then fold into mashed eggplant. Drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika.

veg-01.title: Classic Egyptian Molokhia with Garlic-Coriander Taqlia
veg-01.culturalNotes: The national culinary soul of Egypt. Minced fresh jute leaves gently whisked into rich poultry broth and crowned with the legendary sizzling Taqlia.

vl1-1.name: Fresh finely chopped jute mallow leaves
vl1-1.standardAmount: 500g fresh leaves, finely chopped with Makhrata

vl1-2.name: Rich chicken, duck, or rabbit broth

instructions.1: Bring seasoned, strained rich broth to a boil in a medium pot.
instructions.2: Lower heat, add minced molokhia, and whisk briskly until completely dispersed and smooth. Do not let molokhia boil vigorously or it will separate.
instructions.3: In a small skillet, melt baladi ghee. Sauté minced garlic until pale golden, then add ground dry coriander and sauté until fragrant and golden.
instructions.4: Pour sizzling garlic-coriander Taqlia over the pot of molokhia with a theatrical gasp, swirling a ladle of soup in the skillet to capture every drop of garlic ghee.
instructions.5: Simmer for 1 minute on low heat.
instructions.6: Never cover the pot after cooking, which keeps the bright emerald green color and prevents leaves from falling to the bottom.

veg-02.title: Taro with Swiss Chard (Qolqas bil Salq & Coriander)
veg-02.culturalNotes: Dr. Fatma's golden rule for taro: Never wash peeled taro in water. Wiping it meticulously with a clean towel preserves its firm texture and prevents slimy starch.

instructions.1: Wipe taro thoroughly with dry clean cloth before and after peeling without washing in water to preserve crisp texture and prevent slimy starch release.
instructions.2: Simmer diced taro in hot broth with salt and pepper until tender (about 20 minutes).
instructions.3: Chop Swiss chard leaves and coriander, sauté in ghee until darkened and crisp, then crush into a dark green paste.
instructions.4: Sauté garlic in ghee with dry coriander, then combine with the chard paste.
instructions.5: Pour green chard mixture into simmering taro pot, cooking for 5 minutes until broth turns rich deep green.

leg-01.title: Traditional Egyptian Koshari with Tangy Tomato Sauce
leg-01.culturalNotes: Egypt's most legendary street food: layers of brown lentils, rice, pasta, and crispy fried onions, united by spicy tomato sauce and garlic-vinegar Daqqa.

vl3-4.name: Sliced yellow onions for crispy topping (Ward)

vl3-5.name: Tangy Koshari tomato sauce
vl3-5.standardAmount: Tomato sauce, vinegar, garlic, cumin, chili

vl3-6.name: Garlic & vinegar Daqqa
vl3-6.standardAmount: Garlic, vinegar, lemon, cumin, chili water

instructions.1: Fry sliced onions in generous oil until crispy dark golden brown. Drain on paper towels. Reserve onion-infused oil for all other steps.
instructions.2: Cook lentils halfway in water. In onion oil, toast vermicelli, add rice and lentils with cooking liquid, and cook until fluffy.
instructions.3: Boil macaroni and spaghetti in salted water until al dente. Toss with a spoonful of hot onion oil.
instructions.4: Sauté garlic in onion oil, add vinegar, then tomato sauce, cumin, and salt. Simmer until thickened.
instructions.5: Layer rice and lentils in wide bowls, top with pasta, spoon hot tomato sauce, garnish with crispy onions and chickpeas, and serve with cold garlic-vinegar Daqqa and Shatta.

leg-02.title: Authentic Egyptian Taameya (Fava Bean Falafel with Sesame)
leg-02.culturalNotes: Unlike Levantine falafel made with chickpeas, genuine Egyptian Taameya is made exclusively with soaked split fava beans (Foul Madshoush), leeks, and coriander, creating an airy, brilliant emerald interior.

vl4-1.name: Split peeled dried fava beans (Foul Madshoush)

vl4-2.name: Fresh green herbs (Egyptian leek, coriander, dill)

vl4-4.name: Taameya spices (coriander, cumin, salt)
vl4-4.standardAmount: Dry coriander, ground cumin, salt, pinch of soda

instructions.1: Soak fava beans in cold water for 12 hours. Drain completely so paste won't be too wet.
instructions.2: Grind fava beans, greens, onion, and garlic in a meat grinder or food processor until smooth and fluffy.
instructions.3: Whisk or beat dough with hand for 3 minutes to incorporate air, ensuring light, fluffy taameya that does not absorb excess oil.
instructions.4: With wet hands, shape small flat patties, coat one or both sides in sesame seeds and cracked coriander.
instructions.5: Fry in medium-hot oil until deep golden and crunchy on the outside, moist and emerald green on the inside.
instructions.6: Serve hot inside warm baladi flatbread with tahini, tomatoes, and pickled turnip.

pasta-01.title: Classic Baked Macaroni Béchamel with Minced Meat
pasta-01.culturalNotes: The undisputed star of Egyptian festive banquets. Penne tossed with rich white sauce, layered with spiced beef filling, and crowned with a golden, bubbling béchamel crust.

pb1-2.name: Cooked classic Assag minced meat filling

instructions.1: Boil penne pasta in salted water until just al dente (about 8 minutes). Drain without rinsing.
instructions.2: Melt ghee in saucepan, whisk in flour for 2 minutes until golden. Gradually pour milk and warm broth while whisking continuously until smooth and thick. Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.
instructions.3: Mix one-third of the hot béchamel sauce into the cooked pasta.
instructions.4: Spread half the pasta in a buttered baking dish, distribute the savory minced meat filling evenly, then cover with remaining pasta.
instructions.5: Pour remaining béchamel smoothly over top. Whisk an egg into the top layer or sprinkle with grated Rumi cheese.
instructions.6: Bake in 200°C (400°F) oven for 30 minutes, then brown under broiler until surface is bubbling and golden-crusted. Rest 15 minutes before slicing.

pasta-02.title: Egyptian Fatta with Garlic-Vinegar Sauce & Crispy Flatbread
pasta-02.culturalNotes: The celebratory feast dish of Eid and major milestones: ghee-toasted baladi bread squares, gleaming white rice, tender boiled meat, and the unmistakable aroma of garlic quenched with white vinegar.

pb2-1.name: Boiled veal or beef shank with rich broth

pb2-3.name: Egyptian baladi flatbread toasted in ghee

pb2-8.name: Spices (black pepper, salt, dry coriander)
pb2-8.standardAmount: Ground black pepper, salt, dry coriander

instructions.1: Cut baladi bread into bite-sized squares, toss with baladi ghee and garlic, bake until deeply crisp and aromatic.
instructions.2: Cook short-grain white rice using rich meat broth until tender and gleaming.
instructions.3: Sauté minced garlic in ghee with dry coriander until pale golden, quench with white vinegar, then add a ladle of rich broth.
instructions.4: Divide garlic-vinegar sauce in half. To one half, add strained tomato sauce and simmer until rich and tangy.
instructions.5: Place crispy bread in serving platter, moisten with a few ladles of hot broth and clear vinegar-garlic sauce (bread should stay slightly crunchy), cover with hot white rice.
instructions.6: Crown with the tangy tomato sauce, drizzle remaining garlic-vinegar sauce, and arrange browned pieces of meat on top.

bake-01.title: Baked Goulash Pastry with Pastirma & Melted Cheese
bake-01.culturalNotes: Crisp paper-thin phyllo layers infused with warm ghee, enclosing seasoned Egyptian pastirma and sharp aged Rumi cheese, soaked in seasoned egg and milk before baking.

pb3-4.name: Melted baladi ghee, milk & egg wash

instructions.1: Brush baking dish with melted ghee. Layer half the phyllo pastry sheets, brushing each sheet with melted ghee.
instructions.2: Distribute deseeded pastirma, diced bell peppers, tomatoes, and grated Rumi & mozzarella cheeses evenly.
instructions.3: Cover with remaining phyllo sheets, brushing each layer with ghee.
instructions.4: Slice goulash into squares with a sharp knife before baking.
instructions.5: Whisk egg with milk, salt, and black pepper, and pour evenly over the sliced pastry. Let soak for 5 minutes.
instructions.6: Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 25 minutes until puffed, crisp, and golden brown.

des-01.title: Egyptian Semolina Basbousa with Aromatic Syrup
des-01.culturalNotes: The secret to authentic melt-in-the-mouth Basbousa (Murammala) is 'bassing' coarse semolina with warm ghee between your fingertips before gently folding in warm milk and honey without kneading.

db1-7.name: Hot aromatic sugar syrup (Shira)
db1-7.standardAmount: 2 cups sugar, 1.5 cups water, lemon juice, 1 tbsp ghee

instructions.1: Rub coarse semolina with warm melted ghee with your fingertips until every grain is thoroughly coated in fat (this prevents gluten formation and ensures the melt-in-the-mouth crumb).
instructions.2: Warm milk with sugar and honey until sugar dissolves. Pour into semolina and stir gently with a spatula just until combined (do not overwork dough).
instructions.3: Spread mixture evenly into a greased shallow round baking tray (depth 1 cm). Decorate with peeled almonds.
instructions.4: Bake in preheated 200°C (400°F) oven for 25-30 minutes until edges and top are rich golden amber.
instructions.5: While basbousa is baking, boil sugar and water with lemon juice for 5 minutes, finish with a spoonful of ghee.
instructions.6: Pour hot syrup over piping hot basbousa as soon as it leaves the oven. Cover tray for 10 minutes to lock in moisture and yield signature velvety crumb.

des-02.title: Luqmat Al-Qadi (Crispy Egyptian Zalabia with Syrup)
des-02.culturalNotes: Double-frying is Dr. Fatma's infallible technique: fry once until pale blonde, rest, then fry a second time before dropping into cold rosewater syrup for a shatteringly crisp exterior and pillowy center.

db2-5.name: Pinch of salt & vanilla
db2-5.standardAmount: Pinch of salt and pure vanilla

db2-6.name: Heavy cold sugar syrup with rosewater
db2-6.standardAmount: 2.5 cups sugar, 1 cup water, lemon, rosewater

instructions.1: Whisk flour, cornstarch, yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water together until you have a smooth, sticky, elastic batter.
instructions.2: Cover bowl and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled and bubbly. Deflate gently before frying.
instructions.3: Squeeze batter through your closed fist and cut small round balls with an oiled teaspoon, dropping them directly into medium-hot oil.
instructions.4: Fry dumplings halfway until pale blonde. Remove and drain. Just before serving, fry a second time in hot oil until deeply golden and shatteringly crisp.
instructions.5: Lift hot crispy dumplings straight from oil and plunge into heavy cold sugar syrup for 1 minute.
instructions.6: Drain and serve piled high on a platter, or dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon.

bev-01.title: Traditional Egyptian Carob Drink (Kharroub)
bev-01.culturalNotes: Carob is the timeless refreshing beverage of Egyptian streets and Ramadan tables. Caramelizing the sugar directly with crushed carob pieces yields its unmistakable amber hue and deeply smoky, aromatic flavor.

db3-1.name: Crushed carob pods in small pieces

instructions.1: Place crushed carob pieces and sugar in a deep saucepan over low-medium heat. Stir continuously until sugar melts and turns deep golden-amber (caramelizes) without burning, imparting its signature smoky aroma and rich color.
instructions.2: Pour in water and cover pot over low heat until hardened sugar dissolves completely. Bring to a gentle boil for 4 minutes.
instructions.3: Remove from heat and let rest covered until completely cooled to extract maximum flavor. Strain through a fine mesh sieve, refrigerate until ice-cold, and serve chilled over ice cubes.

add-001.title: Smoked Chicken Mandi
add-001.culturalNotes: Mandi is originally from Yemen, where it is cooked in a pit dug in the ground. Smoking with an ember inside the pot recreates its signature flavour at home. It is usually served with dakkous or sahawiq sauce.

add-001-i6.name: Saffron soaked in orange-blossom water (or turmeric)

add-001-i7.name: Mandi spice (ground cardamom, white pepper, garlic powder)

add-001-i8.name: Whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, dried lime, bay leaf)
add-001-i8.standardAmount: 2 cinnamon sticks + 4 cardamom pods + 4 cloves + 1 dried lime + 1 bay leaf

add-001-i11.name: Toasted nuts, raisins and crispy onions to garnish

instructions.1: Boil the chicken in water with the whole spices and salt for 25-30 minutes until mostly cooked, then lift it out, strain the stock and keep it.
instructions.2: Mix half the soaked saffron with a spoonful of ghee, the mandi spice and salt, and brush it all over the chicken.
instructions.3: Arrange the chicken on a tray and grill under the oven broiler for about 10 minutes until the skin is browned and crisp.
instructions.4: Sauté the onion in the rest of the ghee until soft but not coloured, add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until every grain is coated.
instructions.5: Pour the boiling stock over the rice to about 1.5 cm above it, cook on high heat until most of it is absorbed, then lower the heat, cover and leave 15 minutes.
instructions.6: Sprinkle the remaining saffron over part of the rice to colour it, and lay the chicken on top inside the pot.
instructions.7: To smoke: set a small piece of foil with a spoon of oil in the middle of the rice, put the glowing ember on it, seal the pot tightly for 10 minutes, then remove the ember.
instructions.8: Serve the mandi on a large platter garnished with the nuts, raisins and crispy onions.

add-002.title: Chicken Kabsa
add-002.culturalNotes: Kabsa is the national dish of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf. Loomi (dried black lime) gives it its tang and aroma, and the same method works with lamb or shrimp.

add-002-i11.name: Dried lime (loomi), cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves
add-002-i11.standardAmount: 2 dried limes + 4 cardamom + 1 cinnamon stick + 2 bay leaves

add-002-i14.name: Toasted almonds and raisins to garnish

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a wide pot and sauté the onion until golden, then add the garlic and chilli.
instructions.2: Add the chicken pieces and turn them with the onion until they change colour on all sides.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, carrot, kabsa spice and whole spices, and stir until the tomatoes cook down.
instructions.4: Pour in the hot water, adjust the salt and simmer the chicken on medium heat for 30 minutes until cooked.
instructions.5: Lift out the chicken and brown it in the oven or a pan until golden; measure the remaining stock to about 4 cups.
instructions.6: Add the drained rice to the boiling stock, cook on high heat until most of the water is absorbed, then cover on very low heat for 20 minutes.
instructions.7: Gently fluff the rice onto a serving platter, arrange the chicken on top and garnish with almonds and raisins.

add-003.title: Coconut & Yogurt Basbousa
add-003.culturalNotes: This basbousa has no eggs, and the coconut makes it both crumbly and moist. Warm syrup on hot basbousa is absorbed without turning it doughy.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar and water over medium heat, add the lemon, simmer 5 minutes and set aside to cool.
instructions.2: Mix the dry ingredients: semolina, flour, coconut, sugar, baking powder, vanilla and salt.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt and milk with the butter and oil, then add to the dry mix and fold gently without kneading until smooth.
instructions.4: Pour into a greased tray, level it and cut into squares before baking.
instructions.5: Bake on the middle rack at 180°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat until the surface colours.
instructions.6: Pour the warm syrup over the basbousa as soon as it leaves the oven and let it soak before cutting.

add-004.title: Meat Samosa
add-004.culturalNotes: Samosa is one of the best-loved Ramadan starters in the Gulf, the Levant and Egypt. They can be shaped and frozen before frying, then fried straight from the freezer.

add-004-i4.name: Salt and sugar for the dough

instructions.1: Mix the flour with salt, sugar and oil, add the water gradually while kneading into a smooth dough, cover and rest 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion and garlic in 2 tbsp oil until soft, then add the meat and stir until it breaks up and cooks.
instructions.3: Add the spices and salt and cook until the meat juices dry up, then stir in the parsley and let the filling cool.
instructions.4: Roll the dough thin and cut into circles; halve each circle, shape each half into a cone, fill it and seal the edges with a little water.
instructions.5: Fry the samosas in medium-hot oil until golden and crisp, then drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.6: You can use ready-made samosa sheets instead of the dough, or brush the pieces with oil and bake at 200°C for about 15 minutes.

add-005.title: Cinnamon Rolls (Cinnabon)
add-005.culturalNotes: Cutting the rolls with thread instead of a knife avoids squashing the dough and keeps the swirls neat. Keep covered for two days and warm a few seconds in the microwave before serving.

add-005-i15.name: Milk and vanilla for the glaze

instructions.1: Activate the yeast in the warm water with the sugar, then add the eggs, butter, milk powder and Chantilly powder.
instructions.2: Add the flour with the baking powder and salt gradually, knead 10 minutes until smooth, cover and leave an hour to rise.
instructions.3: Roll the dough into a thin rectangle, spread with the soft butter and sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
instructions.4: Roll it up tightly from the long side and slice with a piece of thread so the rolls keep their round shape.
instructions.5: Arrange in a greased tray, rest 30 minutes, then bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar, milk and vanilla and spread over the rolls while still warm.

add-006.title: No-Oven Skillet Pizza
add-006.culturalNotes: This pizza needs no kneading or long rising. The secret is very low heat and a tight lid, so the dough cooks through before the base burns.

add-006-i9.name: Garlic powder, dried thyme and dried basil

instructions.1: Mix the tomato paste with the garlic powder, thyme, basil and a little sugar and salt for a quick sauce.
instructions.2: Mix the dry dough ingredients, then add the oil and water and whisk by hand into a smooth, pourable batter.
instructions.3: Oil a frying pan, pour in half the batter and level it.
instructions.4: Spread the sauce, then a layer of cheese, then the vegetables and olives, then the rest of the cheese.
instructions.5: Cover the pan tightly and cook on very low heat for 10-15 minutes until the base is cooked and the cheese melted; repeat with the remaining batter.

add-007.title: Fluffy Raisin Cake
add-007.culturalNotes: Soaking the raisins for ten minutes in rose water or orange juice, then drying them before coating in flour, makes them softer and adds a fresh note.

instructions.1: Toss the raisins with a tablespoon of the flour until coated; this stops them sinking to the bottom of the tin.
instructions.2: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla until doubled and pale, then add the oil, milk and vinegar.
instructions.3: Add the sifted flour with the baking powder and salt gradually and fold gently, finally folding in the raisins with a spoon.
instructions.4: Pour into a greased tin and bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
instructions.5: Let the cake cool completely before slicing so the raisins stay in place.

add-008.title: Libyan Mbakbaka with Lamb
add-008.culturalNotes: Mbakbaka means the dish that 'bubbles' in the pot. It is a Libyan one-pot meal in which the pasta cooks directly in the spicy broth instead of being boiled separately.

add-008-i1.name: Lamb or beef on the bone, cubed

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a deep pot and sauté the onion with the meat until the meat changes colour and the onion browns.
instructions.2: Add the tomato paste, turmeric, hrarat, chilli, coriander and pepper and stir 2 minutes until fragrant.
instructions.3: Add the tomato juice and boiling water, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes until the meat is nearly tender.
instructions.4: Add the potato, chickpeas, garlic and chillies, adjust the salt and cook 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the raw pasta straight into the broth and stir now and then for 10-12 minutes until cooked, absorbing the sauce while it stays thick.
instructions.6: Leave the pot covered for 5 minutes off the heat, then serve hot.

add-009.title: Soft Harissa Semolina Cake with Coconut
add-009.culturalNotes: Levantine harissa is close to Egyptian basbousa, but eggs and flour give it a texture more like a soft cake.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar and water over medium heat, add the lemon juice, simmer 10 minutes on low and leave to cool.
instructions.2: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla until the sugar starts to dissolve, then add the yogurt and oil.
instructions.3: Add the semolina and coconut, then the flour sifted with the baking powder, and mix until smooth.
instructions.4: Pour into a greased 23 cm tin and tap it on the counter to level.
instructions.5: Bake in a preheated oven for 10 minutes at 200°C, then 30-35 minutes at 180°C until golden.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over the harissa as soon as it comes out of the oven, and let it settle before cutting.

add-010.title: Fluffy Yeast Donuts
add-010.culturalNotes: Oil temperature is the secret: above 160°C the donuts burn outside before cooking inside, and below it they soak up oil.

add-010-i10.name: Topping: cinnamon sugar or white and dark chocolate sauce

instructions.1: Put everything except the milk in the mixer bowl, add the milk gradually and knead 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and slightly sticky.
instructions.2: Shape into a ball, place in an oiled bowl, cover and leave to rise for 1 to 1½ hours.
instructions.3: Roll the dough 2 cm thick, cut circles with a glass, cut out the centres with a small cap, and re-roll the scraps.
instructions.4: Set the donuts on baking paper and leave 15 minutes for a second rise.
instructions.5: Fry in plenty of oil at 160°C, turning each side once it browns, until evenly coloured.
instructions.6: Dip while hot in cinnamon sugar, or let cool and dip in white chocolate with thin lines of dark chocolate.

add-011.title: Mini Pizzas
add-011.culturalNotes: Mini pizzas are perfect for lunch boxes and children's parties. The bases can be frozen after a first bake without toppings, then topped and heated when needed.

add-011-i7.name: Tomatoes, onion and garlic for the sauce

instructions.1: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic, then cook in 2 tbsp oil with the ketchup, tomato paste and spices until the liquid evaporates and the sauce thickens.
instructions.2: Activate the yeast in the warm milk with the sugar for 10 minutes, add the flour, salt and oil and knead 8-10 minutes until elastic; rise for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Roll the dough to medium thickness on a floured surface and cut into circles with a glass or cutter.
instructions.4: Arrange the circles on a greased tray, prick with a fork, spread with sauce and top with cheese, peppers, olives and oregano.
instructions.5: Bake at 220°C for 8-10 minutes until the edges brown and the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Without an oven: cook the pizzas in a covered greased pan on low heat for about 7 minutes until the base is done and the cheese melts.

add-012.title: Levantine Meat Sfiha
add-012.culturalNotes: Draining the tomato and onion keeps the dough from going soggy. Pomegranate molasses and tahini give the filling its Aleppo flavour; these pastries are also called 'lahm bi ajeen'.

add-012-i15.name: Cinnamon, mixed spice, salt and black pepper
add-012-i15.standardAmount: 1 tsp cinnamon + 1 spice + 1 salt + ¼ pepper

instructions.1: Mix the dry dough ingredients, add the oil and warm water and knead into a smooth dough that leaves the sides of the bowl; oil it, cover and leave an hour to double.
instructions.2: Squeeze the excess water from the grated onion and tomato, then mix them with the meat, chilli and garlic.
instructions.3: Add the pomegranate molasses, tahini, yogurt, spices and pine nuts and mix until even.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into small balls and roll into thin circles, top with filling and pinch the edges into squares or triangles, or leave open.
instructions.5: Arrange on a greased tray and bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges brown and the meat is cooked.
instructions.6: Serve hot with lemon or yogurt.

add-013.title: Eggless Tiramisu
add-013.culturalNotes: Classic Italian tiramisu relies on raw eggs and mascarpone. This version has no eggs and is set with gelatine and condensed milk, so it is safe and slices cleanly.

instructions.1: Whip the cold cream in a chilled bowl until thick and firm.
instructions.2: Bloom the gelatine in the cold water, melt it for a few seconds in the microwave and mix with 2 tbsp of the cream to temper it.
instructions.3: Beat the cream cheese with the ashta, add the condensed milk, fold in the whipped cream gently, then the gelatine.
instructions.4: Dissolve the coffee in the water, dip the biscuits quickly and arrange a layer in the dish.
instructions.5: Cover with half the cream, then a second layer of biscuits and the rest of the cream, and smooth the top.
instructions.6: Chill the tiramisu 3-4 hours and sift cocoa over the top just before serving.

add-014.title: Crispy Chicken Strips (Musahab)
add-014.culturalNotes: The freezer step gives musahab its straight shape and stops it falling apart. The coated pieces can be frozen and fried straight from the freezer.

add-014-i5.name: Ginger, black pepper and onion powder

instructions.1: Blitz the toast to fine crumbs, then the chicken, and process together with the ketchup, garlic and spices into a smooth paste.
instructions.2: Spread the mixture evenly in a greased tray and freeze for an hour.
instructions.3: Cut into even fingers or rectangles and coat each in flour, then the egg-milk mixture, then the breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Return the coated pieces to the freezer for another hour to set the crust.
instructions.5: Deep-fry in medium-hot oil until golden and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.6: For a lighter version, brush with oil and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, turning once.

add-015.title: Homemade Yogurt (Plain & Strawberry)
add-015.culturalNotes: Milk temperature is everything in homemade yogurt: too hot kills the starter, too cold and it will not set. Keep two spoonfuls from each batch to start the next.

add-015-i3.name: Milk powder (optional, for a firmer set)

instructions.1: Boil the milk, then let it cool until lukewarm (about 40°C) — you can keep a finger in it for ten seconds.
instructions.2: Mix the starter with the milk powder and a little warm milk until smooth, then stir it into the rest of the milk.
instructions.3: Pour the milk into cups or jars and cover.
instructions.4: Set the cups in a tray of warm water inside a switched-off, warm oven for 6-8 hours without moving them until set, then refrigerate.
instructions.5: For strawberry yogurt: cook the strawberries with the sugar and lemon on low heat into a light jam and cool it; put a spoonful in each cup before pouring the milk, or blend it with the milk for an even pink yogurt.

add-016.title: Strawberry Banana Smoothie
add-016.culturalNotes: Using frozen strawberries or banana gives a thick, cold smoothie without ice that dilutes the flavour. Add a spoon of chia seeds or oats for a quick breakfast.

instructions.1: Wash and hull the strawberries and slice the banana.
instructions.2: Put the fruit in the blender with the milk, honey, yogurt and ice.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and creamy, pour into glasses and serve at once.

add-017.title: Herb-Roasted Potatoes with Tahini-Yogurt Sauce
add-017.culturalNotes: Covering the potatoes at first steams them through, then uncovering under the grill gives a crisp crust without much oil.

add-017-i5.name: Paprika, ground coriander and dried thyme

add-017-i10.name: Grated garlic and cumin for the sauce

add-017-i11.name: Parsley or fresh coriander to garnish

instructions.1: Peel the potatoes, cut into medium cubes or wedges and toss in a bowl with the olive oil, garlic, spices and salt until coated.
instructions.2: Spread in a tray side by side, cover with baking paper then foil, and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.
instructions.3: Uncover and brown the potatoes under the grill until golden and crisp.
instructions.4: Mix the tahini, yogurt, water, vinegar, garlic, cumin and salt until creamy.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the potatoes with parsley and serve with the tahini-yogurt sauce.

add-018.title: Basbousa Stuffed with Ashta Cream
add-018.culturalNotes: Cream cheese and labneh with cornflour make a stable ashta that does not run when cut; you can use ready-made fresh ashta if available.

add-018-i5.name: Butter, ghee or a ghee-oil mix

add-018-i11.name: For the ashta: unsalted cream cheese

add-018-i13.name: For the ashta: sugar and vanilla

add-018-i14.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-018-i14.standardAmount: 1 cup sugar + ¾ cup water + lemon slices

instructions.1: Mix the semolina, sugar, coconut and baking powder, add the fat and stir until the semolina is coated; rest 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the canned cream, then the eggs and milk, and fold gently until even.
instructions.3: Spread half the mixture 1 cm thick in a greased tin and bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until the edges brown.
instructions.4: For the ashta: stir the cold milk with the cornflour and sugar over heat until thick, remove, add the vanilla, cream cheese and labneh, mix and let cool 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Spread the ashta over the baked layer and let it set 15 minutes, then spoon the rest of the basbousa mixture over the top.
instructions.6: Return to the oven at 190°C for 15 minutes until the top is golden.
instructions.7: Pour the hot syrup over as soon as it comes out, cover, leave an hour, then chill an hour before cutting.

add-019.title: Egyptian Sobia with Homemade Mix
add-019.culturalNotes: Sobia is a popular Ramadan drink in Egypt, originally made from rice or coconut soaked in milk. The homemade mix makes dozens of glasses and keeps two months in a dry place.

add-019-i9.name: To serve: banana, mango and strawberries

instructions.1: Grind the coconut to a powder in a spice grinder, mix it with the milk powder, Chantilly powder, starch, sugar and vanilla, and store in an airtight jar.
instructions.2: Cut the fruit and divide it among serving glasses.
instructions.3: Blend the cold water with the sugar and 2 tbsp of the mix on high speed for a full minute until very frothy.
instructions.4: Pour the sobia over the fruit and serve ice-cold.
instructions.5: For classic sobia without fruit: blend the mix with cold milk instead of water and serve with a pinch of cinnamon.

add-020.title: No-Bake Cheesecake
add-020.culturalNotes: The gelatine must dissolve completely before it goes in, or the cream will be grainy. The topping can be swapped for strawberry, caramel or Lotus.

add-020-i9.name: Blueberry sauce or jam for the top

instructions.1: Mix the ground biscuits with the butter until like wet sand, press into the base of a springform tin and chill.
instructions.2: Mash the cheese portions, add the cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla and beat until smooth.
instructions.3: Add the liquid cream and keep beating until thick.
instructions.4: Dissolve the gelatine completely in the hot water and add it gradually to the cream while beating.
instructions.5: Pour over the base, smooth and chill for at least 3-4 hours until set.
instructions.6: Spread the sauce or jam on top, release the sides of the tin and serve cold.

add-021.title: Yellow Lentil Koshari (Alexandrian Koshari)
add-021.culturalNotes: Yellow koshari is a popular Alexandrian dish, quicker than classic brown-lentil koshari and sometimes called 'white koshari'. It is usually served with fried fish, pickled lemon or tahini.

add-021-i6.name: Black pepper and salt
add-021-i6.standardAmount: 1 tsp pepper + a pinch of salt

instructions.1: For the sauce: fry the garlic in the oil until pale golden, add the tomato juice, cumin, chilli and salt and simmer until thick.
instructions.2: Mix the rice and lentils, wash well and drain.
instructions.3: Melt the ghee in a pot, dissolve the stock cubes in it, add the rice and lentils with the black pepper and stir 2 minutes to coat.
instructions.4: Add the warm water, adjust the salt, boil on high until the water drops, then cover on very low heat for 20 minutes until cooked.
instructions.5: Fluff gently and serve with the hot sauce and crispy onions.

add-022.title: Homemade Turkish-Style Chicken Mortadella
add-022.culturalNotes: The secret to a firm texture is mincing the chicken to a paste and poaching in water that never boils hard, so the log does not crack. Keeps 4-5 days in the fridge or freeze in slices.

add-022-i11.name: Pitted green olives or whole peppercorns (optional)

instructions.1: Process the chicken in a food processor to a very smooth paste, then add the eggs, cornflour, oil, beetroot water, garlic and spices and process again until even.
instructions.2: Fold in the olives or peppercorns with a spoon.
instructions.3: Place the paste on heat-safe cling film or a cooking bag, roll into a very tight log, tie the ends and wrap in foil.
instructions.4: Poach the log in hot, not boiling, water (about 80°C) for 50-60 minutes, turning occasionally.
instructions.5: Transfer straight to iced water for 10 minutes, then chill at least 4 hours before slicing.

add-023.title: Stovetop Cheese Kunafa
add-023.culturalNotes: Cheese kunafa is famous in the Palestinian city of Nablus. If using akkawi or Nabulsi cheese, soak it in water for several hours, changing the water, to remove the salt.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon, add the vanilla, simmer 10 minutes on low and cool.
instructions.2: Crumble the frozen kunafa by hand or in a processor until fine and rub the melted ghee into it until fully absorbed.
instructions.3: Press half the kunafa into a greased tray, spread the cheese in the middle away from the edges, cover with the rest of the kunafa and press gently.
instructions.4: Set the tray over medium heat and keep turning it until the base browns evenly, about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.5: Invert the kunafa onto a second greased tray and return to the heat until the other side browns and the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa, sprinkle with pistachios and serve at once while the cheese is hot and stretchy.

add-024.title: Sahlab with Mastic
add-024.culturalNotes: Sahlab was originally made from the powdered tubers of an orchid, and is now prepared with starch and rice flour. For a spoonable sahlab, add an extra teaspoon of starch.

add-024-i8.name: Mastic ground with a spoon of sugar

add-024-i10.name: To garnish: cinnamon, toasted nuts and coconut

instructions.1: Mix all the dry ingredients well and store in an airtight jar in a dry place.
instructions.2: For each cup of milk, dissolve 2 tbsp of the mix completely in the cold milk before heating, so it does not form lumps.
instructions.3: Cook on low heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens and starts to boil.
instructions.4: Pour into cups, garnish with cinnamon, coconut and nuts and serve hot.

add-025.title: Kunafa with Mango and Cream
add-025.culturalNotes: The best mangoes for this dessert are ripe, low-fibre varieties such as Owais or Zebdia. Serve cold on the same day so the kunafa stays crisp.

instructions.1: Crumble the kunafa and rub in the ghee and icing sugar until absorbed.
instructions.2: Press into a tray and bake at 180°C until golden and crisp, or toast it crumbled in a pan on low heat, stirring.
instructions.3: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa and let it cool.
instructions.4: Whip the Chantilly powder with the cold milk and ashta until doubled; you can add 2 tbsp purée to the cream.
instructions.5: Spread the cream over the kunafa, then the mango cubes, drizzle the purée on top and chill an hour before serving.
instructions.6: For individual servings: toast the kunafa crumbled and layer it in cups with the cream and mango.

add-026.title: Pumpkin Jam with Orange
add-026.culturalNotes: Pumpkin makes a clear golden jam that tastes rather like apricot. Macerating the pumpkin in sugar first means no water is needed, so the cubes keep their shape.

instructions.1: Mix the pumpkin cubes with the sugar and leave 2 hours until plenty of liquid comes out.
instructions.2: Transfer the pumpkin with its liquid to a pot and add the orange juice, zest, cinnamon and star anise.
instructions.3: Cook on medium heat, stirring now and then, until the liquid reduces and the jam reaches the desired thickness.
instructions.4: Add the lemon juice five minutes before taking it off the heat.
instructions.5: Remove the cinnamon and star anise, pour the hot jam into sterilised jars, seal and refrigerate after opening.

add-027.title: Chicken Fajitas
add-027.culturalNotes: Fajitas come from the Tex-Mex cooking of southern Texas and are traditionally served sizzling in an iron skillet so everyone wraps their own at the table.

add-027-i6.name: Cumin, paprika, ground coriander and chilli

add-027-i9.name: Red and green peppers, in strips

instructions.1: Butterfly the chicken breasts into medium-thick slices.
instructions.2: Mix the oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, coriander, spices, cornflour and salt, toss the chicken in it, cover and chill 2 hours or overnight.
instructions.3: Brown the chicken in a little oil over medium heat, turn, cover and cook through.
instructions.4: Remove the chicken and stir-fry the vegetables in the same pan on high heat until tender but still crisp.
instructions.5: Slice the chicken into strips, return to the vegetables for a minute and serve hot with tortillas, salsa and yogurt.

add-028.title: Arabic-Style Chicken Shawarma Platter
add-028.culturalNotes: Shawarma arabi is a Levantine way of serving: the wrap is toasted, cut into bite-size pieces and served as a full meal with fries and garlic sauce.

add-028-i8.name: Cardamom, turmeric, ginger, curry, cumin and black pepper

add-028-i12.name: Toum, pickled cucumber and fries to serve

instructions.1: Mix all the marinade ingredients until smooth, toss the chicken in it, cover and chill 1-2 hours.
instructions.2: Heat a little oil in a wide pan on high heat, add the chicken and stir constantly until cooked and browned at the edges.
instructions.3: Spread the saj bread with toum, place chicken and pickles along one edge and roll tightly.
instructions.4: Toast the roll on a saj or dry pan on both sides until the bread is crisp.
instructions.5: Cut each roll into slanted pieces ('arabi' style) and serve on a plate with fries, toum and pickles.

add-029.title: Egg Salad with Nabulsi Cheese
add-029.culturalNotes: A Palestinian breakfast salad; Nabulsi cheese, scented with mahlab and mastic, gives it a distinctive flavour. Halloumi or akkawi can be used instead.

instructions.1: Soak the cheese cubes in warm water for 15-20 minutes to reduce the salt, then drain well.
instructions.2: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and cut into medium pieces so the yolks don't crumble.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato, cucumber, spring onion and mint in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the eggs and cheese and toss gently.
instructions.5: Whisk the olive oil, lemon, pepper and nigella seeds, pour over the salad and serve at once, without adding salt.

add-030.title: Indian Chicken Biryani
add-030.culturalNotes: The secret of biryani is 'dum' cooking: half-boiled rice over a thick sauce in a sealed pot, so the rice finishes in the steam and absorbs the spices without clumping.

add-030-i2.name: Whole spices for boiling (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, star anise)
add-030-i2.standardAmount: 3 cardamom + 3 cloves + 1 cinnamon stick + 2 bay leaves + 1 star anise

add-030-i6.name: Turmeric, ground coriander, cumin and red chilli

add-030-i10.name: Saffron soaked in warm milk or rose water

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, ground spices, salt and half the coriander and mint for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Boil the rice in plenty of salted water with the whole spices until only 70% cooked and still firm, then drain.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot, add the chicken with its marinade and cook until half done and the sauce thickens.
instructions.4: Scatter half the fried onion and the rest of the herbs over the chicken, spread the rice on top, and sprinkle with the saffron and remaining onion.
instructions.5: Seal the pot tightly (the lid can be sealed with dough) and cook on very low heat for 25-30 minutes ('dum') until the rice steams through.
instructions.6: Gently lift the biryani from the sides so the white and coloured rice and chicken show, and serve with yogurt raita.

add-031.title: Banana Berry Smoothie
add-031.culturalNotes: Putting the liquid in first helps the blades turn easily with frozen fruit. A very ripe banana means no sugar is needed.

instructions.1: Cut the frozen banana into small pieces so it blends easily.
instructions.2: Put the milk in the blender first, then the yogurt, fruit and honey.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and thick, adding a little milk if too heavy, and serve at once.

add-032.title: Homemade Noodle Dough (No Machine)
add-032.culturalNotes: The stiffer the dough, the chewier the noodles. Air-dry the strips for an hour, then keep two days in the fridge or freeze for a month.

instructions.1: Mix the flour and salt, add the egg, then the water gradually until the dough comes together; it should be slightly stiff, not sticky.
instructions.2: Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, cover and rest 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Roll very thin with a rolling pin on a starch-dusted surface, then fold into layers, dusting starch between them.
instructions.4: Cut into thin, even strips with a knife, then shake them loose and dust with starch so they don't stick.
instructions.5: Boil in water for 3-4 minutes until they float and are cooked, drain, rinse in cold water and use in stir-fries or soups.

add-033.title: Fried Eggs Three Ways
add-033.culturalNotes: Fresh eggs hold their shape in the pan because the white is thicker. Salt after frying, not before, so the yolk doesn't get spotty.

add-033-i4.name: Optional extras: grated cheese, red pepper, spring onion

instructions.1: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with the butter or oil spread across the surface.
instructions.2: Crack each egg into a small bowl first, then slide it gently into the pan so the yolk doesn't break.
instructions.3: Sunny side up: leave the egg without turning until the white is fully set and the yolk runny; covering the pan for a minute sets the top of the white.
instructions.4: Over easy: once the white sets, flip the egg with a spatula for just 30 seconds.
instructions.5: Over hard: leave on the second side 1-2 minutes until the yolk sets.
instructions.6: Season with salt, pepper and extras and serve at once with bread.

add-034.title: Egyptian Layered Feteer Meshaltet
add-034.culturalNotes: Feteer meshaltet is one of the best-known breads of rural Egypt, traditionally baked in a clay oven. The secret is an elastic dough and many ghee-brushed layers that separate after baking.

add-034-i5.name: Butter or liquid ghee for stretching

add-034-i6.name: Oil to cover the dough balls

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, add the water gradually and knead into a very soft, smooth, non-sticky dough, then knead 10 minutes more.
instructions.2: Divide into 6-8 balls, submerge them in a tray of oil, cover and rest 30 minutes until relaxed.
instructions.3: Stretch each ball with your fingertips on a ghee-greased surface until paper-thin and translucent, and brush with ghee.
instructions.4: Fold the sheet into a square envelope, stretch a second ball and place the folded square in its centre and fold over; repeat until a pie of 3-4 balls is formed.
instructions.5: Place the pie in a greased tray, press it out with your fingertips to fill the tray, brush with ghee and bake at 220°C for 30-40 minutes until golden and puffed.
instructions.6: Brush with ghee straight out of the oven and clap the edges between your palms to separate the layers; serve with black honey (molasses) and aged cheese or ashta.

add-035.title: Green Olive Pickle
add-035.culturalNotes: Changing the water daily draws out the olives' bitterness. The traditional salt test: a raw egg should float in the brine with a coin-sized patch showing.

instructions.1: Wash the olives and cut one or two slits in each, or crack lightly with a stone without breaking the pit.
instructions.2: Soak in plain water, changing it daily for 7-10 days until the bitterness is gone (taste one to check).
instructions.3: Boil the water with the salt and let it cool completely to make the brine, then add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pack the olives into a sterilised jar with the lemon, chillies and garlic and cover completely with the brine.
instructions.5: Top with a thin layer of olive oil, close the jar and leave two weeks in a cool place before eating.

add-036.title: Qatayef Asafiri with Ashta
add-036.culturalNotes: They are called 'asafiri' (little birds) for their small size. The bicarbonate goes in at the last moment because it is what opens the holes instantly on the hot griddle.

add-036-i5.name: Baking powder and bicarbonate of soda

add-036-i8.name: Fresh ashta or thick clotted cream

add-036-i11.name: Syrup scented with rose and orange-blossom water

instructions.1: Blend the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and orange-blossom water with the warm water until smooth and pourable like cream.
instructions.2: Leave 15 minutes until bubbles appear, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
instructions.3: Heat a griddle or non-stick pan well without oil and pour small rounds (the size of a child's palm) with a small spoon.
instructions.4: Cook on one side only until full of holes, the top dries and the bottom colours, then lift and cover with a cloth so they don't dry.
instructions.5: Pinch each round halfway closed into a cone, leaving the opening, and press the edges to stick.
instructions.6: Fill the openings with ashta, dip the tips in pistachio, garnish with orange blossom and serve cold with syrup on the side.

add-037.title: Levantine Trotter (Kawareh) Soup
add-037.culturalNotes: Trotters are rich in natural gelatine and give a thick, glossy broth. Cleaning with flour and lemon and blanching first are the secrets to a clean, odour-free broth.

add-037-i2.name: For cleaning: flour, coarse salt, lemon juice and vinegar
add-037-i2.standardAmount: ½ cup flour + 3 tbsp salt + 2 lemons + 3 tbsp vinegar

add-037-i6.name: Bay leaves, cloves and black peppercorns

instructions.1: Scrub the trotters well with the flour, coarse salt, lemon and vinegar, leave 15 minutes, then rinse under running water.
instructions.2: Blanch for 10 minutes in boiling water and discard the water and scum.
instructions.3: Cover with fresh water, add the onion, whole spices and mastic and simmer gently 3-4 hours (or 1½ hours in a pressure cooker) until the meat falls off the bone and the broth is sticky.
instructions.4: Strain the broth, pull the meat and cartilage from the bones, chop and return to the broth, adjusting the salt.
instructions.5: Fry the garlic in the ghee with the coriander until golden, deglaze with the lemon juice and pour over the soup before serving.

add-038.title: Creamy Seafood Soup
add-038.culturalNotes: The seafood goes in last because it cooks in minutes and turns rubbery if left too long on the heat.

add-038-i12.name: Chopped parsley and lemon to serve

instructions.1: Melt the butter and sauté the onion, celery and carrot until soft, then add the garlic for a minute.
instructions.2: Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute until the raw smell is gone.
instructions.3: Add the stock gradually, stirring so it doesn't lump, then the spices and bay leaf, and simmer 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
instructions.4: Add the seafood and cook just 3-5 minutes until the shrimp turn pink and everything is cooked but not rubbery.
instructions.5: Stir in the cream, adjust the salt and pepper, heat without boiling and serve sprinkled with parsley, with lemon.

add-039.title: Kofta Dawood Basha
add-039.culturalNotes: The dish is attributed to Dawood Pasha, an Ottoman governor of Baghdad or Egypt, and is one of the meatballs-in-sauce dishes known across Egypt, the Levant and Iraq.

add-039-i4.name: Seven spice, a pinch of cinnamon and cumin

instructions.1: Knead the meat well with the drained onion, parsley, spices and salt and shape into small walnut-sized balls, pressing a pine nut into each if you like.
instructions.2: Brown the balls in the oil in batches on all sides, then lift out.
instructions.3: Soften the sliced onion in the same oil, add the tomato paste and stir, then the tomato juice, water, pomegranate molasses and salt.
instructions.4: Boil the sauce 10 minutes, return the meatballs and simmer 15-20 minutes until thickened.
instructions.5: You can instead arrange the balls in a tray with potatoes and sauce and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the kofta with vermicelli rice, sprinkled with pine nuts.

add-040.title: Layali Lubnan (Semolina Pudding with Ashta)
add-040.culturalNotes: Layali Lubnan ('Lebanese nights') is a cold Lebanese dessert close to qashtaliya, with a layer of semolina milk pudding and a layer of ashta. It is even better made a day ahead.

instructions.1: Stir the milk, semolina and sugar in a pot over medium heat, adding the mastic ground with a little sugar and the orange-blossom water.
instructions.2: Stir constantly until thick and starting to boil, then keep stirring 3 minutes as it bubbles and remove from the heat.
instructions.3: Pour into a tray about 30 cm and tilt it to level the surface; leave to cool.
instructions.4: Chill 2-3 hours until set.
instructions.5: Spread the ashta over the top, scatter the pistachios and raisins, cut into squares and drizzle with syrup or honey to serve.

add-041.title: Eggless Ammonia Cookies (Baskoot Neshader)
add-041.culturalNotes: Baker's ammonia is the secret of crisp Egyptian Eid cookies; its strong smell evaporates completely during baking. Keep it in a sealed jar because it loses strength in the air.

instructions.1: Blend the sugar, milk, oil, salt and vanilla until the sugar dissolves completely.
instructions.2: Pour into a large bowl, add the custard powder, baking powder, ammonia and vinegar and whisk by hand.
instructions.3: Sift the flour over the mixture and knead by hand a few minutes into a smooth, elastic dough that is easy to shape; cover.
instructions.4: Shape with a cookie press or by hand into fingers and rings and arrange on trays lined with baking paper, spaced apart.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until the bases colour and the edges start to brown, turning on the grill for a minute at the end if you like.
instructions.6: Let the cookies cool completely before storing in airtight tins.

add-042.title: Saudi Lamb Kabsa
add-042.culturalNotes: Adding the salt once the meat has started to cook keeps it tender. Kabsa is usually served with spicy dakkous salsa and laban.

add-042-i1.name: Lamb on the bone, large pieces

add-042-i8.name: Whole spices: pierced dried lime, cinnamon, cardamom, galangal, bay leaf
add-042-i8.standardAmount: 2 limes + 2 cinnamon sticks + 5 cardamom + a piece of galangal + 2 bay leaves

add-042-i9.name: Kabsa spice, black pepper and ground cardamom

add-042-i11.name: Raisins, toasted almonds and lemon slices to garnish

instructions.1: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and sear the meat with the whole spices until it changes colour all over.
instructions.2: Add the onion, then the garlic, and stir until soft, then the tomato paste, tomato and kabsa spice.
instructions.3: Cover the meat with hot water, cover and simmer 60-90 minutes (or 35 minutes in a pressure cooker) until tender, adding the salt in the last half hour.
instructions.4: Lift the meat and brown it under the oven grill; measure the stock to 1½ times the volume of the rice.
instructions.5: Add the drained rice to the boiling stock, cook on high until most is absorbed, then cover on very low heat for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Spread the rice on a platter, arrange the meat on top and garnish with raisins, almonds and lemon slices.

add-043.title: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken Wings
add-043.culturalNotes: Yogurt and milk tenderise the wings, while the citrus and ketchup give a sweet-and-sour taste. They can also be grilled over charcoal.

add-043-i8.name: White or black pepper, paprika and thyme

instructions.1: Wash and dry the wings and cut at the joints if you like.
instructions.2: Mix the yogurt, milk, ketchup, oil, vinegar, lemon, spices and salt, and toss the wings in it well.
instructions.3: Cover and chill at least 2 hours or overnight.
instructions.4: Arrange the wings on a tray lined with baking paper and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes, turning halfway.
instructions.5: Brush with the remaining marinade and brown under the grill 5-10 minutes until crisp.
instructions.6: Serve hot with toum or cheese sauce and fries.

add-044.title: Coleslaw
add-044.culturalNotes: Coleslaw is the classic side for fried chicken and burgers. Chilling before serving softens the cabbage slightly and deepens the dressing.

instructions.1: Shred the cabbage finely and grate the carrot, then mix in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, milk, sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.
instructions.3: Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss until all the cabbage is coated.
instructions.4: Cover and chill at least 30 minutes before serving so the flavours blend.

add-045.title: Homemade Apple Cider Vinegar
add-045.culturalNotes: The jelly-like layer that forms on top is called the 'mother' and shows the fermentation worked; it can be used to start a new batch faster.

add-045-i3.name: Filtered water
add-045-i3.standardAmount: enough to cover the apples (about 1 litre)

instructions.1: Wash and dry the apples and cut into small cubes, skin and seeds included, and place in a wide glass jar.
instructions.2: Dissolve the sugar or honey in the water and pour over the apples to cover completely; a small plate on top keeps them submerged.
instructions.3: Cover the jar with a cotton cloth secured with a rubber band and leave in a warm, dark place, stirring twice a day.
instructions.4: After 2-3 weeks, when the apples sink to the bottom, strain the liquid, return it to the clean jar and cover with the cloth.
instructions.5: Leave another 4-6 weeks until strongly acidic, then bottle and refrigerate.

add-046.title: Quick Crunchy Cucumber Pickles
add-046.culturalNotes: Pouring hot brine over cold cucumbers speeds up the pickling while keeping them crunchy. Choose small, firm cucumbers with few seeds.

add-046-i7.name: Chilli and coriander seeds or dill (optional)

instructions.1: Wash the cucumbers and cut into rounds or spears, or leave whole if very small.
instructions.2: Pack into a sterilised jar with the garlic, chilli and coriander or dill between the layers.
instructions.3: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the boiling water, then add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pour the hot brine over the cucumbers to cover completely and close the jar.
instructions.5: Let cool, then refrigerate; ready after 3-4 hours and best after a day. Keeps chilled for two weeks.

add-047.title: Homemade Paprika Powder
add-047.culturalNotes: The peppers must be completely dry and snap, or the powder will clump and spoil. A kilo of peppers gives only about 100 g of powder.

add-047-i1.name: Red peppers (sweet, hot or a mix)

instructions.1: Wash and dry the peppers well, cut into thin strips and remove all the seeds and white ribs.
instructions.2: Spread the strips apart on a lined tray and dry in the oven at the lowest heat (60-80°C) with the door slightly open for 3-4 hours until completely brittle.
instructions.3: Alternatively dry them in direct sun for 5-7 days covered with muslin, bringing them in at night.
instructions.4: Let the strips cool completely, then grind in a spice grinder to a fine powder and sift.
instructions.5: Store in an airtight glass jar away from light and heat.
instructions.6: For smoked paprika: smoke the dried strips for 20 minutes in a closed pot with a charcoal ember before grinding.

add-048.title: Indian Onion Pakora
add-048.culturalNotes: Pakora (or pakoda) is one of India's most popular street snacks. Chickpea flour gives crunch and authentic flavour, and cold water keeps the batter from turning chewy.

add-048-i4.name: Black pepper, ground coriander and cumin

instructions.1: Separate the onion slices with your fingers, mix with the salt and spices and leave 5 minutes to release their juice.
instructions.2: Add the flour, chilli and coriander, then cold water a spoonful at a time until the onion is coated in a thick, clinging batter.
instructions.3: Heat the oil over medium heat and drop in small amounts of the mixture with a spoon or your fingers.
instructions.4: Turn until golden brown and crisp (2-3 minutes) and lift out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.
instructions.5: Serve hot with tamarind sauce or mint yogurt sauce.

add-049.title: Kunafa with Chocolate Sauce
add-049.culturalNotes: The blender chocolate sauce sets like cream thanks to the oil added slowly, just like making mayonnaise, so it does not run during baking.

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10-15 minutes and leave the syrup to cool.
instructions.2: Blend the milk with the cocoa, sugar and vanilla, then pour in the oil gradually through the lid while blending until the sauce thickens like cream; chill.
instructions.3: Crumble the kunafa and rub in the butter and coconut until absorbed.
instructions.4: Press half the kunafa into a greased tray, spread some of the chocolate sauce, cover with the rest of the kunafa and press.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C until golden underneath and then on top.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over the hot kunafa and decorate with the remaining chocolate sauce to serve.

add-050.title: Semolina Maamoul with Dates
add-050.culturalNotes: Resting the semolina with ghee overnight is what gives maamoul its sandy texture that melts in the mouth. Maamoul is a classic Eid sweet across the Levant.

add-050-i7.name: Mastic ground with a little sugar

add-050-i9.name: Ghee or butter for the filling

instructions.1: Mix the fine and medium semolina and rub the warm ghee in between your palms until fully absorbed; cover and leave 12-24 hours.
instructions.2: Knead the date paste with the ghee and cinnamon or cardamom and roll into small balls.
instructions.3: Add the icing sugar, mahlab and mastic to the semolina, then the warm milk gradually, bringing the dough together lightly without kneading.
instructions.4: Take a piece of dough, hollow it with your finger, insert a date ball and close, then press into a maamoul mould and tap out with a clear pattern.
instructions.5: Arrange on an ungreased tray and bake at 200°C with bottom heat for 15 minutes, then top heat for a few minutes until lightly golden.
instructions.6: Let cool completely in the tray as they are fragile when hot, then dust with icing sugar and store in airtight tins.

add-051.title: Turkish Chicken Döner
add-051.culturalNotes: Turkish döner is traditionally roasted on a rotating vertical spit. At home, cooking in small batches over very high heat caramelises the edges in the same way.

add-051-i1.name: Chicken breast and thigh, very thin slices

add-051-i8.name: Salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, oregano and a pinch of cinnamon
add-051-i8.standardAmount: 1 tsp each + a pinch of cinnamon

add-051-i10.name: To serve: pickled cucumber, tomato and sumac onions

add-051-i11.name: For the garlic sauce: garlic, mayonnaise, yogurt and lemon

instructions.1: Mix the yogurt, tomato paste, pepper paste, oil, lemon, garlic and spices and marinate the chicken at least 4 hours or overnight.
instructions.2: Heat a griddle or wide iron pan on very high heat and cook the chicken in small batches until the edges brown, without stewing in its juices.
instructions.3: Mix the garlic sauce ingredients until creamy.
instructions.4: Wipe the bread with a little of the chicken fat left in the pan and warm it for a few seconds.
instructions.5: Spread the bread with garlic sauce, add the chicken, pickles, tomato and sumac onions, roll and serve hot.

add-052.title: Smoked Herring Salad with Tahini
add-052.culturalNotes: Herring salad is a dish of Egypt's Sham el-Nessim spring festival. Soaking the herring in milk for half an hour before cleaning reduces the salt if it is very salty.

instructions.1: Pass the herring over a direct gas flame for a few seconds on each side until the skin cracks, making it easy to peel and bringing out the smoky aroma.
instructions.2: Remove the skin and bones completely and cut the flesh into small cubes, keeping the roe if there is any.
instructions.3: Mix the tomato, cucumber, onion and peppers in a bowl.
instructions.4: Whisk the tahini with the lemon, vinegar and a little water until creamy, then add the oil.
instructions.5: Add the herring to the vegetables, pour over the tahini dressing, toss gently, garnish with dill and serve with baladi bread.

add-053.title: Crispy Stuffed Mumbar (Sausage Casings with Rice)
add-053.culturalNotes: Mumbar is an Eid al-Adha dish in Egypt. Filling the casings only two-thirds full is the key, because the rice doubles in size as it boils.

add-053-i1.name: Mumbar (casings) cleaned with salt, vinegar and lemon

add-053-i3.name: Chopped or squeezed tomatoes without water

add-053-i5.name: Chopped dill, parsley and fresh coriander

add-053-i7.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin, a pinch of dried mint and cinnamon

add-053-i8.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves and cardamom

instructions.1: Turn the casings inside out and scrub with salt, flour, vinegar and lemon, rinsing several times until the smell is gone, then turn them back.
instructions.2: Mix the raw rice with the onion, tomato, herbs, oil and spices without cooking.
instructions.3: Cut the casings to manageable lengths, knot one end, fill with the stuffing through a funnel only two-thirds full as the rice swells, and knot the other end.
instructions.4: Prick the mumbar with a needle in several places so it doesn't burst while boiling.
instructions.5: Boil in water with the onion, bay leaves and cardamom over medium heat for 30-45 minutes until the rice is cooked, then drain and let dry.
instructions.6: Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, or brush with oil and brown under the oven grill.
instructions.7: Cut into slanted pieces and serve hot with lemon.

add-054.title: Fresh Garden Salad with Lemon Dressing
add-054.culturalNotes: Dressing just before serving keeps the lettuce crisp. For a full meal, add grilled chicken, boiled chickpeas or feta.

instructions.1: Wash the vegetables well and dry them, because leftover water dilutes the dressing.
instructions.2: Cut all the vegetables into similar-sized pieces and put in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Whisk the olive oil, lemon, pomegranate molasses, salt and pepper until combined.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over the salad just before serving, toss gently and sprinkle with sumac.

add-055.title: Chocolate Banana Smoothie
add-055.culturalNotes: Frozen banana gives a milkshake-like texture without ice cream. Adjust the cocoa or honey to taste.

instructions.1: Slice the banana and put it in the blender with the cocoa, milk and honey.
instructions.2: Add the peanut butter or yogurt for extra nutrition, and ice for freshness.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth and velvety, pour and serve at once.

add-056.title: Harissa Chili Paste
add-056.culturalNotes: Harissa is a hot chilli paste from Tunisia and the Maghreb, used with grills, soups and couscous. The layer of oil on top protects it from air so it keeps longer.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the chillies, cut into small pieces, and remove the seeds to reduce the heat if you like.
instructions.2: Blend the chillies, garlic and spices until fine.
instructions.3: Add the salt and lemon, then the olive oil gradually with the blender running until creamy and smooth.
instructions.4: Pack into a sterilised glass jar, cover the top with a layer of olive oil and keep refrigerated for up to a month.

add-057.title: Sautéed Chicken Livers with Onion and Pepper
add-057.culturalNotes: Chicken livers cook quickly and overcooking makes them dry and rubbery. If the centre is light pink they are done.

instructions.1: Wash the livers with water, salt and lemon, trim the membranes and veins, and drain well.
