instructions.2: Heat the oil and brown the onion until golden, then add the garlic and pepper for a minute.
instructions.3: Add the livers on high heat and turn until coloured on all sides.
instructions.4: Add the spices, salt, pepper and pomegranate molasses and cook on low heat just 5 minutes until done but not dry.
instructions.5: Squeeze over the lemon and serve with Arabic bread or rice.

add-058.title: Quick Homemade Roumi-Style Cheese
add-058.culturalNotes: This is a quick home version that resembles roumi cheese in taste and look, but it is not an aged cheese. Keeps wrapped in the fridge for a week.

instructions.1: Blend the oil, egg yolks, vinegar, water, milk powder, cornflour and salt until smooth with no lumps.
instructions.2: Add the cheese triangles and keep blending until they melt completely.
instructions.3: Grease a heatproof metal or glass container with oil and dust with starch; pour in half the mixture, scatter the peppercorns, then add the rest.
instructions.4: Cover with its lid and foil and cook in a water bath (a pot of boiling water halfway up the container) for an hour, topping up the water as it reduces.
instructions.5: Let cool, then chill overnight before unmoulding and slicing.

add-059.title: Syrian Shakriyeh (Lamb in Yogurt Sauce)
add-059.culturalNotes: Shakriyeh is a Damascene dish for special occasions. The secret to yogurt that doesn't split: cornflour and egg, stirring constantly in one direction until it boils, and salting at the end.

add-059-i1.name: Lamb (shanks or pieces on the bone)

add-059-i6.name: For boiling: bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cardamom, whole onion

add-059-i8.name: Ghee and toasted pine nuts or almonds to garnish

instructions.1: Simmer the meat in water with the aromatics, skimming the foam, for 1-1½ hours until tender; drain and keep a cup of the broth.
instructions.2: Sauté the sliced onion in a spoon of ghee until soft and translucent.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt with the cornflour and egg until completely smooth, in the cooking pot itself.
instructions.4: Put the yogurt over medium heat and stir constantly in one direction, without stopping, until it boils, so it doesn't split.
instructions.5: Add the onion, meat, cup of broth and salt and simmer 10 minutes, stirring.
instructions.6: Serve in a deep dish topped with pine nuts toasted in ghee, with vermicelli rice.

add-060.title: Aden-Style Lamb Zurbian
add-060.culturalNotes: Zurbian is one of the best-known dishes of Aden in Yemen. It resembles biryani but relies on plenty of dark fried onion and a long yogurt marinade.

add-060-i1.name: Lamb or beef on the bone

add-060-i8.name: Ground cardamom, black pepper and cinnamon

add-060-i11.name: Whole spices for the rice (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaf)

instructions.1: Marinate the meat with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, ground spices, salt and half the fried onion for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Cook the meat with its marinade in a covered heavy pot on low heat with a little water for 45-60 minutes until nearly tender.
instructions.3: Lightly fry the potatoes and add them to the meat for the last 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Boil the rice in salted water with the whole spices until 70% cooked, then drain.
instructions.5: Spread the rice over the meat in the pot and sprinkle with the saffron, ghee and remaining fried onion.
instructions.6: Cover tightly on very low heat for 25 minutes, then smoke with an ember on a piece of foil with ghee inside the pot for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Turn the zurbian out onto a large platter to show the meat and potatoes and serve with spicy bisbas salsa.

add-061.title: Fig and Strawberry Tart
add-061.culturalNotes: Very cold butter and not kneading are the secret to a crisp shell. The shell is blind-baked first so the cream doesn't make it soggy.

add-061-i9.name: For the cream: cornflour and sugar

instructions.1: Rub the flour, icing sugar and salt with the cold butter until sandy, add the yolk, vanilla and iced water and bring together without kneading; chill 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Roll out and line the tart tin, prick with a fork and chill 15 minutes, then bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes with weights (rice or beans on baking paper) for the first 15 minutes, until golden.
instructions.3: For the cream: heat the milk, whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornflour, add the hot milk gradually, return to the heat stirring until thick, add the vanilla and cover with cling film until cool.
instructions.4: Whip the cold cream, then fold the cold custard into it gently.
instructions.5: Spread the cream into the cooled tart shell and arrange the sliced figs and strawberries on top.
instructions.6: Brush the fruit with the melted apricot jam to glaze and chill the tart an hour before serving.

add-062.title: Bahraini Shrimp Biryani
add-062.culturalNotes: Removing the seeds of the dried lime prevents bitterness. The shrimp are seared quickly at first and finish in the steam with the rice so they stay tender.

add-062-i3.name: Turmeric and biryani or fish spice

add-062-i4.name: Lemon juice and salt for marinating

instructions.1: Marinate the shrimp with the garlic, ginger, turmeric, spice, lemon and salt for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Sear the shrimp in a spoon of oil on high heat for just 2 minutes until they colour, then remove.
instructions.3: Fry the onion in the remaining oil until golden, add the tomatoes, paste, dried lime and chilli and cook until the sauce thickens, then return the shrimp with the coriander.
instructions.4: Boil the rice in salted water until 70% cooked and drain.
instructions.5: Spread the rice over the sauce, sprinkle with saffron and a little ghee, and cover the pot tightly on very low heat for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Fluff the biryani gently and serve with green salad and lemon.

add-063.title: Homemade Coconut Chocolate Bars
add-063.culturalNotes: Chilling the coconut slab before cutting gives clean edges and easy coating. You can press an almond onto each bar before coating.

add-063-i3.name: Melted white chocolate for the filling

instructions.1: Mix the coconut with the condensed milk by hand until absorbed, then add the 2 tbsp white chocolate to bind.
instructions.2: Spread the mixture between two plastic sheets on a tray into an even rectangle (about 1.5 cm thick) and chill 15-20 minutes.
instructions.3: Cut into even bars, or roll into small balls if you prefer.
instructions.4: Dip the pieces with a fork into the dark or white chocolate, let the excess drip, and place on baking paper.
instructions.5: Drizzle with lines of the contrasting chocolate, chill until set and keep refrigerated.

add-064.title: Kunafa Cups with Strawberries and Cream
add-064.culturalNotes: Toasting the kunafa with icing sugar gives it a golden colour and a crunch that lasts longer under the cream. Mango or berries can replace the strawberries.

instructions.1: Crumble the frozen kunafa finely by hand and mix with the ghee and icing sugar.
instructions.2: Toast in a wide pan on low heat, stirring constantly, until golden and crisp, then spread out to cool completely.
instructions.3: Whip the Chantilly powder with the cold milk, sugar and cream cheese until thick.
instructions.4: Build the cups: a layer of kunafa drizzled with a little syrup, then cream, then strawberries, and repeat.
instructions.5: Top with strawberry slices and a sprinkle of kunafa, and serve within a few hours so it stays crisp.

add-065.title: Pink Pickled Turnips
add-065.culturalNotes: Beetroot gives the natural pink colour of Levantine pickled turnips. Coarse salt and a little sugar keep them crunchy.

instructions.1: Wash, peel and cut the turnips into fingers or half-moons, and slice the beetroot.
instructions.2: Pack the turnips into a sterilised jar with beetroot and garlic slices between the layers to spread the colour.
instructions.3: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the cooled water and add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pour the brine to cover the turnips completely and weigh them down with a beetroot slice or small weight so they don't float.
instructions.5: Close the jar and leave in a cool place 3-5 days until pink and tangy, then refrigerate.

add-066.title: Levantine Makdous (Oil-Cured Stuffed Eggplant)
add-066.culturalNotes: Makdous is one of the most important preserves in Syria and Lebanon. Success depends on removing all the water from the eggplant and peppers, as any left will cause mould.

add-066-i3.name: Sweet red peppers, minced and drained

instructions.1: Remove the eggplant stems, leaving the small green cap, and wash.
instructions.2: Boil the eggplants in salted water for 8-10 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain.
instructions.3: Slit each eggplant lengthwise, put a little coarse salt inside, and lay them slit-side down in a colander under a weight for 24-48 hours until all the water is out.
instructions.4: Squeeze the minced red pepper very well and mix with the walnuts, garlic, hot pepper and salt.
instructions.5: Stuff each eggplant with the mixture and press to close.
instructions.6: Pack tightly into sterilised jars, lay the jars on their side for a day to drain any remaining water, then cover completely with olive oil, seal and leave two weeks before eating.

add-067.title: Egyptian Mfatteka (Molasses & Sesame Sweet)
add-067.culturalNotes: Mfatteka is a traditional Egyptian sweet given to nursing mothers in winter because it is full of energy. It keeps in sealed jars outside the fridge for weeks.

instructions.1: Toast the sesame, peanuts and nigella seeds in a cup of the oil over low heat, stirring, until fragrant.
instructions.2: Add the ground fenugreek and stir 2 minutes without burning.
instructions.3: Add the molasses and stir constantly over low heat for 15-20 minutes until it thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
instructions.4: Add the remaining oil and stir, then pour into dishes, garnish with crushed peanuts and leave to cool.

add-068.title: Chicken Drumsticks in Yogurt-Ketchup Marinade
add-068.culturalNotes: Covering the tray at first keeps the chicken juicy, and uncovering at the end gives the skin its glossy red colour.

add-068-i8.name: White or black pepper and paprika

instructions.1: Clean the drumsticks, soak 15 minutes in salted water, rinse and dry, and score deeply so the marinade penetrates.
instructions.2: Mix the remaining ingredients, toss the drumsticks in it and chill 2-4 hours.
instructions.3: Arrange in a tray, cover with foil and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Remove the foil, brush with the remaining marinade and bake another 15 minutes until browned, turning once.
instructions.5: Serve with rice or roast potatoes and salad.

add-069.title: Yemeni Saltah (Sanaa Style)
add-069.culturalNotes: Saltah is the favourite everyday dish of Sanaa, served still boiling in a stone pot called a 'madra'. The whipped fenugreek is its soul.

add-069-i1.name: Hot rich meat or chicken broth

add-069-i8.name: For sahawiq: fresh coriander, garlic, chilli and salt
add-069-i8.standardAmount: a bunch + 2 cloves + 2 chillies + a pinch

instructions.1: Soak the fenugreek in water for at least an hour, pour off the water and whip with a blender or whisk, a little cold water and the sahawiq until it becomes a light white foam.
instructions.2: For the sahawiq: grind the coriander with the garlic, chilli and salt.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion in the oil, then add the tomatoes, paste and chilli and cook down (the kishna), adding the minced meat or egg if using.
instructions.4: Heat a stone pot (madra) or heavy pot until very hot and pour in the broth with the kishna and vegetables until it boils hard.
instructions.5: Spoon the fenugreek foam over the top while it bubbles and serve at once in the pot with malawah or lahoh bread.

add-070.title: Pickled Eggplant with Garlic and Pepper
add-070.culturalNotes: Garlic-pickled eggplant is a popular Egyptian side for ful and taameya. Squeezing out the water after boiling keeps them firm in the brine.

instructions.1: Boil the eggplants whole with their caps in salted water for 8-10 minutes until slightly soft, then drain and cool.
instructions.2: Slit each eggplant lengthwise without separating, press gently to release the water, and leave in a colander for an hour.
instructions.3: Mix the garlic, chillies, coriander, cumin, a little salt and the olive oil and stuff the slits.
instructions.4: Pack the eggplants in a sterilised jar, mix the vinegar, water and salt and pour over to cover.
instructions.5: Close the jar and leave in a cool place 5 days before eating, then refrigerate.

add-071.title: Spicy Gulf Dakkous Salsa
add-071.culturalNotes: Dakkous is the constant companion of Gulf rice dishes because its sharpness cuts the richness of the meat. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

instructions.1: Cut the tomatoes into large pieces and put in the blender with the garlic, chilli and coriander.
instructions.2: Add the lemon, vinegar, tomato paste and salt.
instructions.3: Pulse in short bursts until smooth but still with small pieces, not a juice.
instructions.4: Chill 10 minutes and serve with kabsa, mandi and grills.

add-072.title: Cherry Jam
add-072.culturalNotes: Citric acid adds tartness and helps the jam set and keep. Dark cherries give the most beautiful colour.

instructions.1: Wash the cherries, remove the stems and pit them with a cherry pitter or the end of a straw.
instructions.2: Dissolve the sugar in the water over medium heat, then add the cherries.
instructions.3: Boil over medium heat, skimming and stirring now and then, for 30-40 minutes until thick.
instructions.4: Add the citric acid five minutes before removing from the heat, and test by dropping a little on a cold plate — it should not run.
instructions.5: Pour the hot jam into sterilised jars and seal at once.

add-073.title: Homemade Fresh White Cheese
add-073.culturalNotes: This fresh cheese is close to Egyptian areesh and Indian paneer and needs no rennet. Use the leftover whey in dough or soup.

instructions.1: Heat the milk, stirring, until it starts to boil.
instructions.2: Turn off the heat and add the lemon juice gradually, stirring gently, until the milk separates into white curds and yellow-green whey; leave 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Pour into a sieve lined with cheesecloth and rinse with cold water to remove the lemon taste.
instructions.4: Add the salt and nigella seeds and mix, then gather the cloth and squeeze gently.
instructions.5: Put a weight on the cloth for 2 hours in the fridge until set into a block, then slice; keeps 4 days refrigerated.

add-074.title: Indian Chicken Masala
add-074.culturalNotes: Garam masala is made from spices that are toasted and then ground; the toasting gives its deep aroma. Increase the chilli to taste.

add-074-i12.name: Garam masala (toasted, ground coriander, pepper, cumin, cardamom, cloves)

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, half the ginger, half the garlic, 1 tsp chilli and half the salt for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion in the ghee until golden, then add the remaining garlic and the hot chillies.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes, sugar, masala, remaining chilli and salt, and the vinegar, and simmer until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
instructions.4: Add the chicken with its marinade, stir, cover and cook 10-12 minutes until done.
instructions.5: Stir in the cream for a minute and serve with basmati rice or naan.

add-075.title: Chunky Strawberry Jam
add-075.culturalNotes: Cooking uncovered lets the strawberry juice evaporate and concentrates the flavour. The jam thickens more as it cools, so don't cook it until very stiff.

instructions.1: Hull, wash and drain the strawberries and cut into small or medium cubes.
instructions.2: Put the strawberries and sugar in an uncovered pot over medium heat until plenty of juice comes out, then lower the heat.
instructions.3: Add the cinnamon stick and stir now and then until the liquid reduces and the colour turns deep red.
instructions.4: Add the lemon and raise the heat slightly, stirring constantly so it doesn't catch, and test on a cold plate — it should hold its shape.
instructions.5: Remove the cinnamon and pour the hot jam into sterilised jars and seal.

add-076.title: Karnıyarık (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant)
add-076.culturalNotes: Karnıyarık means 'split belly' in Turkish. This version roasts the eggplant in the oven instead of frying, so it is lighter.

add-076-i8.name: Black pepper, paprika and ground coriander

instructions.1: Soak the halved eggplants in salted water for 15 minutes, dry them and score the white flesh in a crisscross.
instructions.2: Place white side up in a tray, brush with oil, sprinkle with salt and roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until soft and coloured.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, then the garlic and peppers, then add the meat until it breaks up and cooks, then half the tomatoes, the spices and salt until the juices dry.
instructions.4: Press the centre of each eggplant half with the back of a spoon to make a hollow, fill it and top with the remaining tomatoes.
instructions.5: Pour the tomato juice thinned with a little water around the eggplants and return to the oven for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or yogurt.

add-077.title: Homemade Tomato Ketchup
add-077.culturalNotes: Ketchup thickens more as it cools, so take it off the heat when a spoon leaves a clear line on the bottom of the pot. The vinegar and sugar are what preserve it.

instructions.1: Cook the tomatoes and peppers with the water in a covered pot for 15 minutes until completely soft.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth, then pass through a fine sieve to remove the skins and seeds.
instructions.3: Return the juice to the pot with the vinegar, sugar, spices and salt.
instructions.4: Simmer uncovered on low heat for 40-45 minutes, stirring often, until thick like ketchup.
instructions.5: Let cool, then bottle in a sterilised bottle and refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.

add-078.title: Levantine Hummus Fatteh
add-078.culturalNotes: The secret of hummus fatteh is the contrast between hot chickpeas, cold yogurt and crisp bread, so assemble it just before serving.

add-078-i9.name: To garnish: parsley, pomegranate, toasted nuts (pine nuts or almonds) and paprika

add-078-i10.name: Ghee or butter for toasting the nuts

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water, then rinse.
instructions.2: Simmer in fresh water until very tender (60-90 minutes, or 25 minutes in a pressure cooker), keeping a little of the cooking water.
instructions.3: Fry the bread cubes in oil until golden and drain, or brush with oil and toast in the oven.
instructions.4: Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, lemon, garlic, cumin and salt until smooth.
instructions.5: Spread the bread in a deep dish, moisten with a little hot chickpea water, then add the hot chickpeas, then the yogurt sauce.
instructions.6: Toast the nuts in the ghee and pour sizzling over the fatteh; garnish with parsley, pomegranate and a pinch of cumin or paprika and serve at once.

add-079.title: Chocolate Bird's Nest Kunafa
add-079.culturalNotes: Bird's nest is a Levantine kunafa sweet traditionally filled with pistachios. Chocolate is sweet on its own, so a light drizzle of syrup or none at all is enough.

add-079-i6.name: Ground pistachios or icing sugar to garnish

instructions.1: Separate the kunafa strands and brush with ghee, then wrap each thin strand two or three times round your finger into a small nest and tuck the end underneath.
instructions.2: Pack the nests close together in a greased tray and press each centre slightly to make a hollow.
instructions.3: Brush with the remaining ghee and bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.4: Drizzle with a little syrup if you like and let cool slightly.
instructions.5: Fill each nest with a spoon of chocolate spread, top with hazelnuts and sprinkle with pistachios or icing sugar.

add-080.title: Swiss Roll with Jam and Cream
add-080.culturalNotes: Rolling the cake while hot gives it a 'memory' of the rolled shape, so it doesn't crack when filled once cool.

instructions.1: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, vanilla and vinegar for 8-10 minutes until doubled, pale and thick.
instructions.2: Sift the flour with the baking powder and fold in gently with a spatula in batches so it doesn't deflate.
instructions.3: Spread in a rectangular tray lined with greased baking paper and bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until springy.
instructions.4: Turn the cake straight onto a clean towel dusted with icing sugar, peel off the paper and roll up with the towel while hot; leave to cool rolled.
instructions.5: Unroll gently, spread with jam then cream, roll again and chill 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Dust with icing sugar and cut into slanted slices.

add-081.title: Homemade Spreadable Cream Cheese
add-081.culturalNotes: The longer you process it, the smoother it gets. Add dried herbs, garlic or chopped olives for different flavours.

instructions.1: Heat the milk over medium heat until almost boiling.
instructions.2: Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice and stir gently for a short while until the milk separates into white curds and liquid.
instructions.3: Pour into cheesecloth set over a bowl and let the whey drain 1-2 hours until the curds are a little dry.
instructions.4: Process the curds in a food processor with the butter, salt and 2 tbsp of whey until completely smooth and creamy.
instructions.5: Pack into an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days.

add-082.title: Easy Budget Vanilla Cupcakes
add-082.culturalNotes: Vinegar with baking powder gives these cupcakes a good rise with just one egg, and the cornflour makes them softer.

add-082-i6.name: Milk with a spoon of yogurt

instructions.1: Whisk the egg with the vinegar and vanilla until frothy, add the sugar and whisk until dissolved.
instructions.2: Add the oil, then the milk with yogurt, and mix.
instructions.3: Sift the flour, baking powder, cornflour and salt and add gradually, mixing until smooth.
instructions.4: Fill lined cupcake cases two-thirds full and bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
instructions.5: Let cool and decorate with cream or chocolate sauce as you like.

add-083.title: Two-Layer Milk and Orange Mahalabia
add-083.culturalNotes: Waiting for the first layer to set before pouring the second is the secret of clean, separate layers.

instructions.1: Dissolve the starch and sugar in the cold milk, then stir over medium heat until thick and boiling for a minute; add the orange-blossom water.
instructions.2: Divide among cups or a serving dish and leave until cool and the surface sets.
instructions.3: Dissolve the starch and sugar in the cold orange juice with the zest and stir over heat until thick, glossy and clear.
instructions.4: Let it cool a little, then pour gently over the milk layer using the back of a spoon so the layers don't mix.
instructions.5: Chill 3-4 hours and garnish with orange slices or pistachios.

add-084.title: Lentil Soup Fatteh
add-084.culturalNotes: Lentil fatteh is an Egyptian way to turn lentil soup into a full meal; the garlic-vinegar topping gives it the familiar fatta flavour.

add-084-i11.name: Butter, chopped garlic and vinegar for the topping

instructions.1: Put the lentils, vegetables, garlic, stock cubes, spices and water in a pot, bring to the boil and simmer 30 minutes until everything is cooked.
instructions.2: Blend the soup until smooth and adjust the thickness and salt.
instructions.3: Fry the chopped garlic in the butter until golden, then carefully add the vinegar and let it bubble a minute.
instructions.4: Put the toasted bread in deep bowls, pour the hot soup over, then the garlic-vinegar topping, and serve with lemon and spring onion.

add-085.title: Turkish-Style Basbousa (No Eggs, No Butter)
add-085.culturalNotes: Resting the semolina with the milk for an hour gives this basbousa its sandy texture even without butter or eggs, making it much lighter than regular basbousa.

add-085-i6.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-085-i6.standardAmount: 1½ cups sugar + 1¼ cups water + a squeeze of lemon

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes and leave the syrup to cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, sugar and baking powder, add the milk and fold gently without kneading until combined.
instructions.3: Spread in a greased 25 cm tin, level and leave 1-1½ hours for the semolina to absorb the milk.
instructions.4: Cut into squares and place a peanut on each piece.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat until the surface colours.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over as soon as it leaves the oven and let it soak.

add-086.title: Mixed Fruit Jam
add-086.culturalNotes: Apples are rich in natural pectin, helping the jam set without additives, and the mandarin gives it a fresh aroma.

instructions.1: Wash, peel and cut the fruit, removing the mandarin seeds.
instructions.2: Blend the fruit with the cup of water into a purée (or leave some pieces if you like).
instructions.3: Cook the purée with the sugar in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until boiling, then lower the heat.
instructions.4: Cook 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick, adding the lemon before removing from the heat.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-087.title: Egyptian Cooked Hot Chili Sauce
add-087.culturalNotes: This is the chilli sauce served with koshari and ful in Egyptian restaurants. Cooking it with vinegar and oil makes it keep a long time, and the heat depends on how many hot chillies you use.

instructions.1: Cut both kinds of pepper, remove the seeds and mince in a processor with the garlic into a paste.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pot, add the minced peppers and stir over medium heat until the water evaporates.
instructions.3: Add the vinegar, salt and sugar and simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil rises to the top.
instructions.4: Let cool, pack into clean jars with a layer of oil on top and refrigerate for months.

add-088.title: Levantine Fried Kibbeh
add-088.culturalNotes: Iced water on your hands stops the dough sticking and keeps the wall thin without cracking. Kibbeh can be frozen raw and fried straight from frozen.

add-088-i4.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin and a pinch of cinnamon for the dough

add-088-i5.name: Coarse minced meat for the filling

add-088-i6.name: Onions, finely chopped, for the filling

add-088-i8.name: Allspice, salt and pepper for the filling

instructions.1: For the filling: soften the onion, add the coarse meat and stir until it breaks up and cooks, then add the spices and pine nuts and let cool.
instructions.2: For the dough: process the lean meat with the onion and spices into a paste, then add the bulgur in batches and process or knead with hands dipped in iced water until the dough is smooth and holds together.
instructions.3: Take a ball the size of a small egg and hollow it with your index finger, turning it on your palm until the wall is thin and even.
instructions.4: Fill with the stuffing, close and shape into an oval with pointed ends, wetting your hands with iced water.
instructions.5: Deep-fry in hot oil in batches for 4-5 minutes until dark golden and crisp, then drain.
instructions.6: Serve with cucumber yogurt or lemon.

add-089.title: Syrian Maarouk (Sweet Ramadan Bread)
add-089.culturalNotes: Maarouk is a sweet bread tied to Ramadan in Syria and Lebanon, and mahlab is the soul of its flavour. It can be filled with coconut or chocolate or left plain.

add-089-i10.name: Filling: date paste with cinnamon and butter

add-089-i11.name: For the top: egg yolk, milk, sesame and nigella seeds

instructions.1: Mix the dry ingredients with the mahlab and anise, add the milk, yogurt and butter and knead 10 minutes into a soft, fluffy dough.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour or more until doubled.
instructions.3: Knead the date paste with the butter and cinnamon and roll thin between two sheets.
instructions.4: Divide the dough, roll each piece into a rectangle, lay the date paste on it and roll up, then shape into a braid, ring or round as you like.
instructions.5: Leave 30 minutes to rise again, brush with the egg yolk and milk, sprinkle with sesame and nigella and bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes.
instructions.6: Cover with a cloth as soon as they come out so they stay soft.

add-090.title: Cheese-Stuffed Luqmat al-Qadi
add-090.culturalNotes: Freezing the cheese cubes for 15 minutes before filling stops them melting too fast and leaking into the oil. The salty cheese with sweet syrup is what makes this version special.

instructions.1: Mix the dry ingredients, add the oil and warm water gradually and beat by hand into a smooth, sticky batter; cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Heat the oil over medium heat.
instructions.3: Take a little batter in your palm, push a cheese cube into the middle, squeeze a ball out between thumb and index finger so the batter wraps the cheese, and drop it into the oil with a wet spoon.
instructions.4: Turn the balls constantly until golden and crisp all over.
instructions.5: Drain and dip at once in the cold syrup or drizzle with honey, and serve hot with the cheese melted.

add-091.title: Indian Potato Samosa
add-091.culturalNotes: Frying on medium-low heat is the secret to the crisp, blistered crust of authentic Indian samosa.

add-091-i11.name: Turmeric, curry, paprika, ground coriander and cumin

add-091-i14.name: Chutney sauce (mint, coriander, chilli and lemon)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, cumin seeds and salt, rub in the oil until sandy, add the water and knead into a smooth, slightly firm dough; cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion, then the garlic, ginger and chilli, add the spices for a minute, then the potatoes, peas and salt, mashing lightly; add the coriander and lemon and let cool.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into 8 balls, roll each into an oval and cut in half, shape each half into a cone, fill and seal the edge with water.
instructions.4: Fry slowly in medium oil for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp with small bubbles on the crust.
instructions.5: Serve hot with green chutney or tamarind sauce.

add-092.title: Egyptian Sakhina (Bread in Molasses and Ghee)
add-092.culturalNotes: Sakhina is a winter breakfast in rural Egypt that gives warmth and energy. Stale, dry bread works best as it soaks up the molasses without turning mushy.

instructions.1: Mix the molasses with the water and half the ghee in a pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.2: Spread the bread pieces in an oven tray or clay dish.
instructions.3: Pour the hot molasses over the bread until absorbed, then dot the rest of the ghee on top.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for 10-15 minutes until the bread absorbs all the liquid and the top browns slightly.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with sesame and serve hot.

add-093.title: Cheese Stuffed-Crust Pizza
add-093.culturalNotes: Sealing the edge well around the cheese stops it leaking during baking. Cheddar or cheese triangles can replace the mozzarella in the crust.

add-093-i3.name: Warm water to activate the yeast

add-093-i12.name: Green pepper, tomato and olives for the top

instructions.1: Activate the yeast in the warm water with the sugar for 5 minutes, add to the flour, salt, garlic powder, oil and remaining water, knead 10 minutes until smooth and let rise an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Divide the dough in two and roll each into a circle 3 cm larger than the tray on every side.
instructions.3: Lay the cheese sticks around the edge and fold the dough edge over them inwards, pressing firmly to seal.
instructions.4: Prick the base with a fork, spread with sauce and top with grated cheese and vegetables.
instructions.5: Bake in a very hot oven (240°C) for 15-20 minutes until the crust browns and the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Brush the crust with a little garlic-parsley butter and serve hot.

add-094.title: Chicken Ranch Pizza
add-094.culturalNotes: Ranch is a creamy American herb dressing, and dill gives it its signature flavour. It keeps a week in the fridge and is great with salads and potatoes.

add-094-i3.name: For the ranch: garlic powder, onion powder, dried dill and dried parsley

add-094-i4.name: For the ranch: salt and black pepper

add-094-i10.name: Chicken breast cubes, seasoned and sautéed

instructions.1: Mix the ranch ingredients well and chill 30 minutes so the flavours blend.
instructions.2: Knead the dough ingredients with the warm milk until smooth and let rise an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Sauté the chicken seasoned with salt, paprika and garlic until cooked.
instructions.4: Spread the dough in two greased trays and spread with a layer of ranch instead of tomato sauce.
instructions.5: Scatter the cheese, chicken and vegetables, then a final sprinkle of cheese.
instructions.6: Bake at 230°C for 15-20 minutes and drizzle with lines of ranch after baking.

add-095.title: Frothy Lemon Mint Lemonade
add-095.culturalNotes: Blending peeled lemons briefly prevents bitterness, and the two spoons of milk give the pale colour and thick froth known from juice shops.

add-095-i4.name: Very cold water or sparkling water

instructions.1: Peel the lemons and remove all the seeds and as much of the thick white pith as possible so the juice isn't bitter.
instructions.2: Blend the lemons, mint, sugar, half the water and the ice for only 30 seconds.
instructions.3: Strain through a fine sieve, return to the blender with the remaining water and the milk and blend a few seconds until frothy.
instructions.4: Pour at once over ice and garnish with mint leaves and a lemon slice.

add-096.title: Fluffy Potato Ojja with Vegetables
add-096.culturalNotes: Baking powder is the secret of a fluffy, light ojja, and the mashed potato keeps it soft and firm so it doesn't break when flipped.

add-096-i3.name: Green and red bell pepper, small dice

add-096-i9.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin, ground coriander and a pinch of chilli

instructions.1: Whisk the eggs with the spices, then add the flour and baking powder and whisk until no lumps remain.
instructions.2: Add the mashed potato, onion, peppers and parsley and mix until even.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee and oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the mixture and level it, then cover on low heat for 8-10 minutes until the base sets and browns.
instructions.4: Flip the ojja onto a plate and slide it back into the pan on the other side for 5 minutes until cooked.
instructions.5: You can pour the mixture into a greased tray and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes, or fry spoonfuls as small patties.
instructions.6: Cut into wedges and serve with tahini or green salad.

add-097.title: Homemade Pomegranate Molasses
add-097.culturalNotes: Pomegranate molasses is essential in Levantine cooking for salads, muhammara and sfiha. Sour or sweet-sour pomegranates give the best balance.

instructions.1: Seed the pomegranates, pulse the seeds briefly in a blender and strain through a fine sieve.
instructions.2: Mix the juice, sugar and lemon in a wide pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.3: Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 1-1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until reduced to a quarter and syrupy.
instructions.4: Let cool completely (it thickens as it cools), bottle and refrigerate.

add-098.title: Fresh Orange Juice (with Optional Carrot)
add-098.culturalNotes: Drink orange juice as soon as it is squeezed, as it loses vitamins and turns bitter with time. Local juicing oranges give more juice than navels.

add-098-i3.name: Boiled carrot (optional, for a thicker juice)

instructions.1: Wash the oranges, halve and squeeze with a juicer, or peel and blend then strain.
instructions.2: For the carrot version: blend the boiled carrot with a cup of the juice until smooth, then add to the rest.
instructions.3: Sweeten to taste and serve at once over ice.

add-099.title: Palestinian Musakhan Rolls
add-099.culturalNotes: Musakhan is a Palestinian dish traditionally served on taboon bread with a whole chicken. The rolls are a modern way to serve it as a starter; sumac and olive oil are its soul.

add-099-i5.name: Salt, black pepper and a pinch of cumin

add-099-i6.name: Saj or shrak bread, cut into triangles

instructions.1: Cook the onion in the olive oil over low heat for 15-20 minutes until completely soft and sweet without burning.
instructions.2: Add the sumac and spices, then the shredded chicken, and stir 5 minutes to absorb the flavour; add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Put a little filling on the edge of each bread triangle, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
instructions.4: Arrange in a tray, brush with the olive oil left from the onion and bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp.
instructions.5: Serve hot with yogurt or pomegranate molasses.

add-100.title: Tuna Salad with Corn
add-100.culturalNotes: Lemon and mustard soften the strong tuna smell. For a light version, replace all the mayonnaise with yogurt.

instructions.1: Drain the tuna well of oil or water and flake with a fork.
instructions.2: Add the corn, pepper, onion, parsley and pickles.
instructions.3: Mix the mayonnaise with the mustard, lemon and pepper and fold into the salad.
instructions.4: Chill 15 minutes and serve on toast, in lettuce leaves or as a sandwich filling.

add-101.title: Eggplant Fatteh with Yogurt
add-101.culturalNotes: Salting the eggplant before frying greatly reduces the oil it absorbs. Tahini in the yogurt stops it splitting and gives it a velvety texture.

add-101-i2.name: Arabic bread, cubed, toasted or fried

add-101-i3.name: Minced meat sautéed with onion and spices (optional)

add-101-i7.name: Lemon juice and salt
add-101-i7.standardAmount: juice of ½ lemon + a pinch

add-101-i9.name: Ghee and pine nuts or almonds to garnish

instructions.1: Sprinkle the eggplant cubes with salt and leave in a colander 20 minutes to release their water, then dry.
instructions.2: Fry the eggplant until golden, or brush with oil and roast in the oven, and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon and salt until smooth.
instructions.4: Spread the bread in a serving dish, then the eggplant, then the minced meat if using, then cover with the yogurt sauce.
instructions.5: Toast the pine nuts in the ghee and pour sizzling over the yogurt, garnish with pomegranate and parsley and serve at once.

add-102.title: Homemade Greek Yogurt
add-102.culturalNotes: Greek yogurt is simply regular yogurt strained of its whey, so it is higher in protein and thicker. The longer it strains, the closer it gets to labneh.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling, then let it cool until lukewarm (about 43°C).
instructions.2: Mix the starter with a little of the warm milk, then return it to the rest of the milk and stir.
instructions.3: Cover the container and wrap it in a blanket or place in a switched-off warm oven for 8 hours without moving it until set.
instructions.4: Pour the yogurt into a cheesecloth-lined sieve over a bowl and leave in the fridge 3-4 hours until the whey drains and it is very thick.
instructions.5: Stir until smooth and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for a week.

add-103.title: Pepperoni Pizza
add-103.culturalNotes: Putting the pepperoni on top of the cheese rather than under it lets the edges crisp and curl into little cups, with their spiced fat running into the cheese.

instructions.1: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth and elastic and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Roll the dough thin in a greased tray, leaving a slightly thicker edge.
instructions.3: Spread with the sauce and sprinkle with oregano, then the cheese, then lay the pepperoni slices on top.
instructions.4: Bake at the highest heat (240-250°C) for 12-15 minutes until the edges brown and the pepperoni edges crisp.
instructions.5: Leave 2 minutes before slicing so the cheese sets.

add-104.title: Basil Pesto
add-104.culturalNotes: Pesto comes from Genoa in Italy. A layer of oil on top and a little lemon keep it green. Toss with hot pasta and two spoonfuls of its cooking water.

instructions.1: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until lightly coloured and let cool.
instructions.2: Put the basil, cheese, pine nuts and garlic in a food processor and chop until combined.
instructions.3: Add the olive oil gradually with the processor running until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Adjust the salt and pepper, add the lemon, and store in a jar covered with a layer of oil in the fridge for a week.

add-105.title: French Onion Soup
add-105.culturalNotes: Slowly caramelising the onions is the whole secret of this French soup; rushing it on high heat burns them and makes them bitter instead of sweet.

instructions.1: Melt the butter with the oil, add the onions and stir until soft, then add the sugar and salt.
instructions.2: Cook the onions on low heat for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until caramelised to a deep golden brown.
instructions.3: Sprinkle in the flour and stir a minute, then add the stock, thyme and bay leaf and simmer 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, top each with a slice of bread and then the cheese.
instructions.5: Grill until the cheese melts and browns, and serve at once.

add-106.title: Pineapple Coconut Smoothie
add-106.culturalNotes: A tropical smoothie close to a piña colada without alcohol. Frozen pineapple gives it a thick, icy texture.

instructions.1: Put the coconut milk and yogurt in the blender first, then the pineapple, banana, honey and ice.
instructions.2: Blend until completely smooth, pour into two glasses and garnish with a pineapple slice or a sprinkle of coconut.

add-107.title: Egyptian Liver and Orzo Tagine
add-107.culturalNotes: This tagine is a favourite of Egypt's liver shops. Searing the liver quickly on very high heat keeps it tender, and it finishes cooking in the oven.

add-107-i10.name: Cumin, black pepper and chilli
add-107-i10.standardAmount: 1 tsp cumin + ½ pepper + a pinch of chilli

instructions.1: Toast the orzo in the ghee until golden, then add the stock and salt and cook until half the liquid is absorbed.
instructions.2: Sear the liver in the oil on very high heat for just 2 minutes until it changes colour, then remove.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, then the garlic and peppers, add the tomato paste, tomato juice and spices and cook 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Mix the half-cooked orzo with the liver and sauce in a clay tagine.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until the orzo absorbs the sauce and the top browns.
instructions.6: Squeeze over the lemon and serve hot in the tagine.

add-108.title: Jalapeño Cheddar Bites
add-108.culturalNotes: The double breadcrumb coating and freezing before frying stop the cheese leaking into the oil.

instructions.1: Mix the cheddar, cream cheese, jalapeño and spices until the mixture holds together.
instructions.2: Shape into walnut-sized balls, set on a tray and freeze 20 minutes.
instructions.3: Coat in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, then egg and breadcrumbs again for a double layer.
instructions.4: Return to the freezer for 10 minutes to set the crust.
instructions.5: Fry in hot oil at 180°C for 2 minutes until golden and drain.
instructions.6: Serve at once with ranch or sweet chilli sauce.

add-109.title: Harissa Stuffed with Ashta and Walnuts
add-109.culturalNotes: Tahini on the base of the tray is a Levantine tradition that gives the harissa a crisp golden bottom and a subtle distinctive flavour.

add-109-i12.name: Syrup: sugar, water, lemon and orange-blossom water
add-109-i12.standardAmount: 2 cups sugar + 1½ cups water + a squeeze of lemon + 1 tbsp orange-blossom water

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes, add the orange-blossom water and let cool.
instructions.2: Rub the semolina with the ghee until absorbed, add the sugar, coconut and baking powder, then the yogurt and milk, mix until even and rest 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Grease the tray with the tahini, spread half the mixture and level with a wet hand.
instructions.4: Mix the walnuts with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp of syrup; spread the ashta over the base, then the walnuts.
instructions.5: Carefully spread the rest of the mixture over the filling, level it, cut into squares and put a walnut on each.
instructions.6: Bake at 190°C with bottom heat for 30 minutes, then top heat until coloured.
instructions.7: Pour over the cold syrup as soon as it comes out and leave an hour before serving.

add-110.title: Emirati Harees (Wheat and Lamb Porridge)
add-110.culturalNotes: Harees is the dish of celebrations, Ramadan and weddings in the Emirates and the Gulf, traditionally cooked overnight in a pot over embers until the meat melts into the wheat.

instructions.1: Wash the wheat well, soak overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Simmer the meat in the water, skimming, for an hour until it starts to cook.
instructions.3: Add the wheat and salt and cook on very low heat for 3-4 hours, stirring now and then and adding boiling water as it dries, until the meat falls apart and the wheat is fully cooked.
instructions.4: Remove the bones and beat the mixture with the wooden masher (midhrab) or a stick blender until smooth, even and stretchy, adding the cardamom and cinnamon.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish, make a well in the centre, fill with hot ghee and serve hot.

add-111.title: Turkish Basbousa with Peanuts
add-111.culturalNotes: Turkish basbousa (revani) needs no butter or oil, and the peanuts roasting in the oven give it a special flavour.

add-111-i6.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-111-i6.standardAmount: 2 cups sugar + 1½ cups water + a squeeze of lemon

instructions.1: Make the syrup by boiling the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes and let it cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, sugar and baking powder, add the milk and fold gently until even without kneading.
instructions.3: Spread in a greased tray and rest 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds and put half a peanut on each.
instructions.4: Bake at 190°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat for a few minutes until the surface colours.
instructions.5: Pour the cold syrup over while hot and let it soak before serving.

add-112.title: Date Jam (Fresh Red or Ripe Dates)
add-112.culturalNotes: Date jam is a traditional preserve in Egypt and the Gulf. Lemon juice is essential to stop the sugar crystallising in storage.

add-112-i1.name: Red or ripe dates, peeled and pitted

instructions.1: Peel the dates and remove the stones carefully to keep their shape; an almond or clove can go in place of each stone.
instructions.2: Boil the sugar and water until the sugar dissolves, then add the dates and cloves.
instructions.3: Simmer on low heat for 40 minutes without much stirring until the dates turn translucent and the syrup is thick like honey.
instructions.4: Add the lemon five minutes before removing from the heat to stop crystallisation.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-113.title: Crispy Mozzarella Sticks
add-113.culturalNotes: The cheese must be frozen when fried, and frying must be quick and hot, so the crust crisps before the cheese melts and leaks.

add-113-i3.name: Eggs beaten with a spoon of milk

add-113-i4.name: Breadcrumbs with oregano, garlic powder and paprika

add-113-i6.name: Marinara sauce or ketchup to serve

instructions.1: Cut the cheese into sticks 1.5 cm thick and freeze 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Coat in flour, then egg, then seasoned breadcrumbs, then egg and breadcrumbs a second time.
instructions.3: Freeze the coated sticks at least another 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil at 180°C for only 1-1½ minutes until golden, before the cheese runs.
instructions.5: Drain and serve at once with marinara sauce.

add-114.title: Sawabe' Zeinab (Crispy Fried Fingers in Syrup)
add-114.culturalNotes: Sawabe' Zeinab ('Zeinab's fingers') is an Egyptian Ramadan sweet. The grater pattern isn't just for looks: it adds crunch and helps the syrup seep inside.

add-114-i7.name: Baking powder and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Mix the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and salt and rub in the oil until absorbed.
instructions.2: Add the yogurt, then the water gradually, and bring into a smooth, firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Take small pieces and shape into fingers, pressing each on the back of a grater or sieve to take the pattern and rolling it on itself so it is hollow.
instructions.4: Fry in medium oil in batches, turning, until puffed, golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Dip while hot in the cold syrup for a minute, lift out and garnish with pistachios or coconut.

add-115.title: Brined Lupini Beans (Termes)
add-115.culturalNotes: Termes is a popular snack for Sham el-Nessim and festivals in Egypt. The bitterness goes with changing the water, and ready-sweetened lupini need fewer days.

add-115-i4.name: To serve: cumin, lemon and chilli

instructions.1: Wash the lupini and soak in plenty of water for 24 hours.
instructions.2: Boil in fresh water for about an hour until tender but not mushy, then drain.
instructions.3: Soak in cold water, changing it twice a day for 5-7 days until the bitterness is completely gone (taste to check).
instructions.4: Make salted water (1 tbsp salt per litre) and keep the lupini in it in the fridge.
instructions.5: Serve in paper cones or bowls with a pinch of cumin, a squeeze of lemon and chilli.

add-116.title: Dynamite Shrimp
add-116.culturalNotes: Toss the shrimp in the sauce at the last moment so they keep their crunch. Adjust the heat with the amount of sriracha.

add-116-i2.name: Salt, white pepper and garlic powder

add-116-i8.name: For the sauce: sweet chilli sauce

add-116-i9.name: For the sauce: sriracha or chilli sauce

add-116-i10.name: For the sauce: honey and lemon juice

add-116-i11.name: Chopped spring onion and sesame to garnish

instructions.1: Season the shrimp with salt, pepper and garlic, then toss in the egg white.
instructions.2: Mix the cornflour and flour, toss the shrimp in it until fully coated and shake off the excess.
instructions.3: Fry in hot oil in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
instructions.4: Mix the sauce ingredients in a large bowl until smooth.
instructions.5: Toss the hot shrimp in the sauce just before serving and garnish with spring onion and sesame on lettuce.

add-117.title: Crispy Chinese-Style Coated Nuts
add-117.culturalNotes: The secret is repeating the moisten-and-coat step several times to build the thick crunchy shell. You can deep-fry them instead for a taste closer to the shop-bought kind.

add-117-i4.name: Salted water (1 tsp salt in ½ cup water)

add-117-i6.name: Paprika, garlic powder, curry and chilli

instructions.1: Mix the flour, cornflour and spices in a wide bowl.
instructions.2: Moisten the peanuts with a little of the salted water and soy sauce, toss in the flour mix until coated, and repeat the moistening and coating 3-4 times to build a thick shell.
instructions.3: Sift off the excess flour and toss the nuts with the oil.
instructions.4: Spread on a lined tray and bake at 170°C for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 7 minutes, until golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Let cool completely so they crisp up further, and store in an airtight jar.

add-118.title: Date, Cocoa and Walnut Energy Balls
add-118.culturalNotes: A healthy snack with no added sugar, relying on the natural sweetness of dates. Almonds or cashews can replace the walnuts.

add-118-i6.name: Vanilla and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: If the dates are dry, soak in hot water for 10 minutes and drain well.
instructions.2: Pulse the walnuts and oats coarsely in a food processor, then add the dates, cocoa, peanut butter, vanilla and salt and process until it holds together like dough.
instructions.3: Roll into walnut-sized balls and coat in coconut or cocoa.
instructions.4: Chill 30 minutes until firm and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for two weeks.

add-119.title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Rice Cakes
add-119.culturalNotes: A pinch of flaky salt brings out the chocolate and peanut butter. A quick crunchy snack lighter than biscuits.

add-119-i5.name: Flaky salt or crushed peanuts to garnish

instructions.1: Spread each rice cake with a thin layer of peanut butter and chill 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in the microwave in short bursts until smooth.
instructions.3: Dip the spread side in the chocolate or pour it over and spread with a spoon.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with crushed peanuts or a pinch of flaky salt, chill until the chocolate sets and keep in the fridge.

add-120.title: Puffed Potato Balloons
add-120.culturalNotes: Thin dough and partial drying are the secret of the puff: steam trapped inside the thin piece separates its two surfaces in the hot oil.

instructions.1: Mash the boiled potatoes while hot until completely smooth, add the starch and salt gradually and knead into a smooth, non-sticky dough.
instructions.2: Roll the dough very thin (1-2 mm) between two sheets of baking paper and cut into small squares or circles.
instructions.3: Leave the pieces to air-dry for 2 hours until the surface is dry (or dry in a barely warm oven).
instructions.4: Fry in medium oil, pressing gently with a slotted spoon, until they puff up like balloons and turn golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Drain and sprinkle with salt and paprika while hot.

add-121.title: Yemeni Sahawiq with Cheese
add-121.culturalNotes: Sahawiq is the essential hot relish of the Yemeni table, and adding cheese softens its heat and gives it a creamy texture.

add-121-i5.name: Cheese triangles or soft white cheese

instructions.1: Pound the chillies, garlic and salt in a mortar (mirhak) or chop in a processor.
instructions.2: Add the coriander and pound, then the chopped tomatoes and pound until broken down but still with some texture.
instructions.3: Add the cheese, cumin and lemon and mix until creamy.
instructions.4: Serve at once with rice, mandi and bread.

add-122.title: Egyptian Vermicelli Milk Pudding with Ashta
add-122.culturalNotes: Toasting the vermicelli well in ghee gives this Egyptian pudding its toasty flavour and sets it apart from rice pudding.

add-122-i7.name: Nuts, raisins and coconut to garnish

instructions.1: Toast the vermicelli in the ghee, stirring constantly, until deep golden.
instructions.2: Add the hot milk, sugar and vanilla and simmer 10 minutes until the vermicelli is cooked and slightly thickened.
instructions.3: Pour into a clay dish or oven tray and spread the ashta over the top.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until the top browns.
instructions.5: Garnish with nuts, raisins and coconut and serve hot or cold.

add-123.title: Flaky Chocolate Croissants
add-123.culturalNotes: The secret of flaky croissants is keeping the butter cold and solid between the dough layers, so it turns to steam in the oven and separates them.

add-123-i9.name: Chocolate batons or chopped dark chocolate

instructions.1: Knead everything except the cold butter and chocolate into a smooth dough, wrap and chill an hour.
instructions.2: Roll the cold butter into a thin square between two sheets of baking paper; roll the dough into a rectangle twice its size, place the butter in the middle and enclose it.
instructions.3: Roll the dough into a long rectangle and fold in three like a letter, chill 30 minutes, and repeat the rolling, folding and chilling three times.
instructions.4: Roll the dough 4 mm thick and cut into triangles; place a piece of chocolate at the base of each and roll towards the tip.
instructions.5: Leave an hour until puffed, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Quick method: use ready-made puff pastry, cut, fill and bake straight away.

add-124.title: Chicken Caesar Salad
add-124.culturalNotes: Caesar salad was created in Mexico in the 1920s. The lettuce must be completely dry for the creamy dressing to cling to it.

add-124-i4.name: Olive oil and garlic powder for the croutons

add-124-i8.name: For the dressing: lemon juice and mustard

add-124-i9.name: For the dressing: Worcestershire sauce or anchovy fillet (optional)

add-124-i10.name: For the dressing: Parmesan and black pepper

instructions.1: Toss the bread cubes with the olive oil and garlic powder and toast at 190°C for 10 minutes until crisp.
instructions.2: Mix the dressing ingredients until smooth, thinning with a spoon of water if thick.
instructions.3: Tear the lettuce into large pieces after washing and drying it well.
instructions.4: Toss the lettuce with the dressing, add the chicken and croutons, sprinkle with Parmesan and black pepper and serve at once.

add-125.title: Homemade Chocolate Wafers
add-125.culturalNotes: Thin sheets are the secret of the crunch. Keep unfilled sheets in an airtight tin and fill shortly before serving so they don't soften.

add-125-i7.name: For the filling: chocolate spread or thick ganache

instructions.1: Whisk the flour, icing sugar, butter, egg white and vanilla with the water added gradually until a smooth, pourable batter like thin crêpe batter; rest 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat a wafer iron or flat non-stick pan, pour a very thin amount of batter and spread it, and cook until dry and pale golden on both sides.
instructions.3: Lift the sheet onto a flat surface to cool and crisp; repeat with the rest.
instructions.4: Beat the chocolate with the soft butter until smooth.
instructions.5: Spread a sheet with filling and top with another, repeating for 3-4 layers, press under a light weight for 5 minutes and cut into rectangles with a sharp knife.

add-126.title: Safflower Lemon Pickle
add-126.culturalNotes: Boiling the lemons briefly speeds up the pickling and removes bitterness from the skin. Safflower gives the golden colour of Egyptian lemon pickle.

instructions.1: Boil the whole lemons for 5-7 minutes until the skin softens slightly, then cool in iced water.
instructions.2: Cut four slits lengthwise in each lemon without separating it at the base.
instructions.3: Mix the safflower, nigella, salt, sugar and chilli and stuff the lemons with it.
instructions.4: Pack the lemons in a sterilised jar with the garlic and chillies, press well and pour over the lemon juice and the rest of the mix.
instructions.5: Cover the top with olive oil, seal and leave in a warm place for 15-20 days, shaking every two days, until the skin softens.

add-127.title: Homemade Pressed Sesame Oil
add-127.culturalNotes: Warm water breaks the oil's bond with the sesame fibres so it separates. The leftover paste can be used like tahini in sweets.

instructions.1: Lightly toast the sesame in a dry pan (optional, for a stronger flavour) and let cool.
instructions.2: Grind the sesame in a powerful grinder or food processor into a smooth paste like tahini.
instructions.3: Add a spoon of warm water and knead and rub the paste hard with a wooden spoon in one direction, then another spoon, until the oil starts to separate from the fibres.
instructions.4: Keep rubbing until the golden oil floats, then tilt the bowl, collect the oil with a spoon and squeeze the paste in cheesecloth to extract the rest.
instructions.5: Let the oil rest an hour so any sediment settles, then strain into a dark bottle and keep in a cool place.

add-128.title: Homemade Creamy Cheese Cups (Gibna Kasat)
add-128.culturalNotes: This soft creamy cheese is like the ready-made Egyptian cup cheese. Processing the curds while warm gives a much smoother texture.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling, add the vinegar and stir gently until it separates into curds and whey; leave 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Strain through cheesecloth, keeping a cup of whey, and let the curds drain 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Process the warm curds with the butter, cream, cheese and salt, adding whey a spoon at a time until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Pack into cups or jars and chill until set; keeps a week in the fridge.

add-129.title: Alexandrian Hegazeya (Semolina Cinnamon Slice)
add-129.culturalNotes: Hegazeya is a popular Alexandrian sweet, set apart by its semolina and cinnamon filling. The ghee-oil mix gives it crunch with softness.

instructions.1: Rub the semolina and flour with the ghee and oil, add the yeast, sugar and warm water gradually and gather the dough lightly; rest 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the filling ingredients until like wet sand.
instructions.3: Divide the dough in two; press the first half into the base of a greased tray and spread and press the filling on it.
instructions.4: Press the second half over the top, level and cut into squares or diamonds.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until the top browns.
instructions.6: Pour the warm syrup over while hot and let cool before serving.

add-130.title: Jameed Sauce for Mansaf
add-130.culturalNotes: Jameed is dried salted yogurt shaped into discs, and the finest comes from Karak. It is the heart of Jordanian mansaf, and stirring in one direction keeps it from splitting.

instructions.1: Break the jameed disc into small pieces and soak in the warm water overnight until soft.
instructions.2: Rub the jameed by hand or blend with its soaking water until completely dissolved, then strain out any grit.
instructions.3: Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction until it boils, so it doesn't split.
instructions.4: Add the lamb stock gradually with the laban and turmeric and simmer 15 minutes, stirring.
instructions.5: Use the sauce at once to cook the boiled mansaf meat in and pour over the rice, adding no salt since the jameed is salty.

add-131.title: Garlic Lemon Baked Salmon
add-131.culturalNotes: Salmon dries quickly if left too long in the oven. When it flakes in the centre and is still slightly glossy, it is perfectly cooked.

instructions.1: Take the salmon out of the fridge 15 minutes before baking and pat dry.
instructions.2: Mix the butter, garlic, lemon juice, zest and spices.
instructions.3: Place the salmon on a tray lined with baking paper, brush with the mixture and arrange lemon slices around.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for just 12-15 minutes until pale pink and flaking easily with a fork.
instructions.5: Spoon over the pan juices and serve with rice or sautéed vegetables.

add-132.title: Duck Soup with Carrots and Potatoes
add-132.culturalNotes: Duck stock is very rich, so skimming the fat once it has cooled a little gives a lighter, clearer soup. Mastic and cardamom soften the duck's strong aroma.

add-132-i6.name: Whole spices: bay leaf, cardamom, mastic, cinnamon stick

instructions.1: Simmer the duck in water to cover with the whole onion and spices, skimming, for 1½ hours until cooked.
instructions.2: Lift out the duck, strain the stock and let it sit a little so the excess fat can be skimmed off.
instructions.3: Sauté the chopped onion in the ghee until soft, add the carrots and potatoes and stir 2 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the strained stock and cook until the vegetables are tender, adding the orzo for the last 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Season and serve the soup hot, and brown the duck in the oven to serve as a main course.

add-133.title: Apricot Jam
add-133.culturalNotes: Apricot jam is one of the quickest jams because apricots are rich in pectin, and skimming the foam gives a clear, glossy jam.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the apricots, open them, remove the stones and cut into pieces as you like.
instructions.2: Put the apricots and sugar in a large pot over medium-high heat and stir until the sugar dissolves and the fruit releases its juice.
instructions.3: When it boils, lower to medium and skim the foam after 10 minutes.
instructions.4: After another 10 minutes add the lemon and cook, stirring, until it reaches the desired thickness.
instructions.5: Pour at once into dry sterilised jars and refrigerate after opening.

add-134.title: Arabic Seven-Spice Blend (Baharat)
add-134.culturalNotes: Seven spice is the base of Levantine cooking for stuffed vegetables, meats and kibbeh. Light toasting before grinding releases the aromatic oils; over-toasting makes it bitter.

instructions.1: Toast the whole spices except the nutmeg in a dry pan over low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not darkened.
instructions.2: Spread on a plate to cool completely.
instructions.3: Grind in a spice grinder to a fine powder and grate the nutmeg over it.
instructions.4: Sift and store in an airtight glass jar away from light; it stays fragrant 3-4 months.

add-135.title: Homemade Garlic and Onion Powder
add-135.culturalNotes: Low heat matters: if it's too high the slices brown and the powder turns bitter. White onions dry better because they contain less sugar.

instructions.1: Slice the garlic thinly and the onions into thin even slices.
instructions.2: Spread the slices on lined trays without overlapping and dry in the oven at 60-70°C with the door slightly open for 3-5 hours, turning every hour, until completely brittle.
instructions.3: Let cool completely, then grind each separately in a spice grinder to a fine powder and sift.
instructions.4: Store each in an airtight jar with a little starch to absorb moisture.

add-136.title: Japanese Cotton Cheesecake
add-136.culturalNotes: The whites must reach soft, not stiff, peaks or the cake will crack. The water bath and low heat are the secret of its wobbly, cotton-like texture.

add-136-i9.name: Cream of tartar or lemon juice

instructions.1: Melt the cream cheese, butter and milk over a water bath, stirring until smooth, and let cool slightly.
instructions.2: Add the yolks one at a time, then the vanilla, then sift in the flour and cornflour and whisk until smooth.
instructions.3: Whisk the whites with the cream of tartar until foamy, then add the sugar gradually until soft, curling peaks form (not stiff).
instructions.4: Fold the whites into the cheese mixture in three additions, pour into a lined tin and tap out the bubbles.
instructions.5: Set the tin in a tray of warm water 2 cm deep and bake at 150°C for 60-70 minutes until risen and golden.
instructions.6: Turn off the oven and leave the door ajar 15-20 minutes before taking it out so it doesn't sink, then cool.

add-137.title: Red Grape Jam
add-137.culturalNotes: Citric acid preserves the jam and stops it crystallising. Red grapes give a beautiful colour with no need for colouring.

add-137-i4.name: Citric acid (or juice of 1 large lemon)

instructions.1: Pick the grapes off the bunches, wash well and discard any shrivelled ones.
instructions.2: Put the grapes, sugar, water and citric acid in a heavy-based pot and stir gently.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, then simmer about 40 minutes until the grapes are cooked and the syrup thickens, skimming the foam.
instructions.4: Test with a spoonful on a cold plate; if it holds its shape it is done.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-138.title: Jordanian Shrak Bread
add-138.culturalNotes: Shrak is the bedouin bread of Jordan and Palestine and is served under the rice in mansaf. The simple yeast-free dough and a very hot saj are the secret of its thinness.

add-138-i1.name: White flour (or 2 cups white + 1 cup wholemeal)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, add the water gradually and knead 8-10 minutes into a smooth, supple dough that doesn't stick.
instructions.2: Divide into orange-sized balls, brush with oil, cover and rest an hour until relaxed.
instructions.3: Roll each ball with a rolling pin, then stretch it over the backs of your hands, tossing between them until very thin and translucent.
instructions.4: Heat the domed saj (or the back of a large upturned wok) well, drape the loaf over it and leave a few seconds until bubbles appear, then flip for a few seconds more.
instructions.5: Fold the loaves and stack them under a cloth so they stay soft.

add-139.title: Fresh Peach Juice
add-139.culturalNotes: Lemon stops the juice browning and brings out the peach flavour. Very ripe peaches need little sugar.

instructions.1: Peel the peaches (easy after 30 seconds in boiling water then iced water) and cut them up.
instructions.2: Blend with the water, sugar and lemon until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Strain for a light juice, or leave it thick.
instructions.4: Serve chilled with mint leaves.

add-140.title: Arayes (Meat-Stuffed Grilled Pita)
add-140.culturalNotes: The meat layer must be thin so it cooks at the same time as the bread crisps, and draining the onion and tomato stops the bread going soggy.

add-140-i1.name: Minced meat with a little fat

add-140-i3.name: Onion, very finely chopped and drained

add-140-i8.name: Olive oil with paprika for brushing the bread

instructions.1: Knead the meat with the onion, tomato, parsley, pomegranate molasses and spices until even.
instructions.2: Open each loaf at one edge like a pocket and spread a thin, even layer of meat inside right to the edges, pressing it flat.
instructions.3: Brush the outside of the bread with the paprika olive oil and cut each loaf into quarters or halves.
instructions.4: Arrange in a tray and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes, then flip and bake 8-10 minutes until crisp and the meat is cooked.
instructions.5: They can also be grilled over charcoal or in an electric grill until crisp on both sides.
instructions.6: Serve hot with tahini and pickles.

add-141.title: Kazandibi (Turkish Caramelized Milk Pudding)
add-141.culturalNotes: Kazandibi means 'bottom of the pot' in Turkish, as the base is deliberately scorched. Mastic is the authentic Ottoman flavour.

add-141-i7.name: Mastic ground with a little sugar

instructions.1: Grease a rectangular metal tray with the butter and sprinkle the sugar evenly over the base.
instructions.2: Whisk the milk, sugar, rice flour and flour cold, then stir constantly over medium heat until thick and boiling for 2 minutes; add the mastic and vanilla.
instructions.3: Set the empty tray directly on the heat until the sugar caramelises and turns brown, then pour the pudding over it at once.
instructions.4: Move the tray over the heat so the whole base browns evenly (1-2 minutes) without burning.
instructions.5: Let cool, then chill 4 hours, cut into rectangles and roll each piece so the caramelised side faces up.

add-142.title: Turkish Trileçe (Three-Milk Caramel Cake)
add-142.culturalNotes: Trileçe is the Balkan-Turkish version of Latin American tres leches cake, set apart by its glossy caramel topping.

add-142-i4.name: Baking powder and a pinch of salt

add-142-i11.name: For the caramel: butter and warm cream

instructions.1: Whisk the whites until firm and the yolks with the sugar and vanilla until pale, fold in the whites gently, then sift in the flour and baking powder and fold lightly.
instructions.2: Pour into a greased tray and bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden; let it cool to warm.
instructions.3: Mix the milk, cream and condensed milk, prick the warm cake with a fork and pour the mixture over gradually until absorbed; chill overnight.
instructions.4: For the caramel: melt the sugar in a pan until amber, then carefully add the butter and warm cream, stirring until smooth, and let cool.
instructions.5: Spread the whipped cream over the cake, pour the caramel sauce on top and cut into cold squares.

add-143.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
add-143.culturalNotes: Brown sugar gives the cookies softness and a caramel flavour, and taking them out while the centre is soft makes them chewy inside and crisp at the edges.

instructions.1: Cream the butter with both sugars until light and pale, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, soda and salt and mix just until no flour shows, then fold in the chocolate chips.
instructions.3: Chill the dough 30 minutes, then scoop tablespoon-sized balls onto a lined tray, spaced apart.
instructions.4: Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until the edges colour and the centres are still soft.
instructions.5: Leave on the tray 5 minutes to firm up, then move to a rack to cool.

add-144.title: Muhammara (Red Pepper and Walnut Dip)
add-144.culturalNotes: Muhammara is an Aleppo mezze, and pomegranate molasses gives it a balanced sweet-sour taste. Its flavour improves if left an hour before serving.

instructions.1: Roast the peppers over a direct flame or under the grill until blackened, cover 10 minutes, then peel and seed.
instructions.2: Lightly toast the walnuts in a dry pan.
instructions.3: Chop the walnuts coarsely in a processor, then add the peppers, garlic, pepper paste, pomegranate molasses, spices and lemon and process.
instructions.4: Add the breadcrumbs and olive oil and process until creamy with some texture.
instructions.5: Serve in a dish drizzled with olive oil and walnuts, or spread on manakish dough before baking.

add-145.title: Za'atar Manakish
add-145.culturalNotes: Manakish is the most famous morning breakfast in Lebanon and the Levant. The fingertip dimples hold the za'atar oil so it doesn't run off the dough.

instructions.1: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and oil with the warm water into a smooth dough, cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Mix the za'atar with the olive oil into a runny paste.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into 8 balls, roll each into a thin round and press with your fingertips to make small dimples.
instructions.4: Spread the za'atar mixture over the top, leaving a small border.
instructions.5: Bake on a saj or tray in an oven preheated to the highest heat for 7-10 minutes until the edges brown.
instructions.6: Serve hot with tomato, cucumber, mint and labneh.

add-146.title: Chicken Maqalqal
add-146.culturalNotes: Maqalqal is a quick Gulf and Yemeni dish in which the meat is cut very small and stirred over high heat until the sauce dries and clings to the pieces.

instructions.1: Heat the oil on high heat, add the chicken and stir quickly until it changes colour all over.
instructions.2: Add the onion, garlic and pepper and stir until the onion softens.
instructions.3: Add the tomato, tomato paste, spices and salt and stir over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until the sauce almost dries.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with bread or rice.

add-147.title: Lamb Maqalqal
add-147.culturalNotes: Cutting the meat into very small pieces lets it cook quickly and stay tender in this Gulf dish.

add-147-i1.name: Lamb or beef, very small cubes

add-147-i7.name: Cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, ground cardamom and black pepper

instructions.1: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot on high heat and brown the meat in batches.
instructions.2: Return all the meat, add the onion, garlic, peppers and spices and stir 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and cook on low heat 15-20 minutes until the meat is tender in its own juices, adding a little water if needed.
instructions.4: Uncover and stir on high heat until the sauce dries and caramelises onto the meat.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with coriander and serve with bread and sahawiq.

add-148.title: Homemade Saj Bread
add-148.culturalNotes: The thinner the loaf and the hotter the saj, the softer and lighter the bread. Freeze extra loaves and warm for a few seconds.

instructions.1: Knead the ingredients with the warm water added gradually into a soft, supple dough; cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Divide into medium balls, roll each very thin with a rolling pin, then stretch over the backs of your hands until translucent.
instructions.3: Heat a saj or the back of a large upturned pan on high heat and drape the bread over it.
instructions.4: Flip after 30-40 seconds when bubbles and brown spots appear, and leave a few seconds on the other side.
instructions.5: Fold the loaves and cover with a cloth; use for shawarma, sandwiches and manakish.

add-149.title: Yemeni Lahsa with Cheese
add-149.culturalNotes: Lahsa is a quick Yemeni breakfast, named because it is scooped up ('licked') with bread. The melted cheese makes it creamy.

instructions.1: Sauté the onion and chilli in the ghee until soft, then add the tomatoes and stir until they soften and cook down.
instructions.2: Crack the eggs over the mixture and stir quickly with the spices until they start to set.
instructions.3: Add the cheese and stir until it melts into the eggs and the texture is soft and creamy.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with malawah or baladi bread.

add-150.title: Sheikh al-Mahshi (Stuffed Zucchini in Yogurt)
add-150.culturalNotes: It is called 'sheikh of the stuffed vegetables' because it is filled only with meat and no rice. Stirring the yogurt constantly until it boils stops it splitting.

add-150-i10.name: Crushed garlic and dried mint fried in ghee

instructions.1: Core the zucchini with a corer, wash and dry, and fry them in oil until lightly coloured if you like, then drain.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion, add the meat and spices and cook through, then add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Stuff the zucchini with the meat and arrange in a pot.
instructions.4: Add a little water to cover and cook 15 minutes until tender.
instructions.5: Whisk the yogurt with the egg, starch and salt and cook over medium heat stirring in one direction until it boils, then pour over the zucchini and simmer 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Fry the garlic and dried mint in ghee and pour over the top; serve with vermicelli rice.

add-151.title: Yemeni Malawah (Flaky Salted Bread)
add-151.culturalNotes: Malawah is a flaky Yemeni bread traditionally baked in a tannour; its many layers resemble Egyptian feteer. It is served with saltah, honey and fenugreek.

instructions.1: Knead the flour and salt with the water added gradually into a very soft, smooth dough; divide into balls, brush with butter and cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Stretch each ball on a greased surface until paper-thin, brush with butter and sprinkle with nigella seeds.
instructions.3: Roll the sheet into a rope, then coil it like a snail and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Press the coil with your palms into a disc 1 cm thick.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot oven at 220°C for 15-20 minutes until golden, or cook on a greased griddle over medium heat, flipping.
instructions.6: Clap between your palms after baking to separate the layers, and serve with honey or saltah.

add-152.title: Peach Jam
add-152.culturalNotes: Peaches have less pectin than apricots, so they need lemon and a little longer to set.

instructions.1: Peel the peaches by dipping them a few seconds in boiling water then cold water, stone them and cut into cubes.
instructions.2: Mix the peaches with the sugar and leave an hour to release their juice.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, skimming, then simmer on low heat, stirring, for 30-40 minutes until thick.
instructions.4: Add the lemon five minutes before removing from the heat and test on a cold plate.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-153.title: Apple Cinnamon Jam
add-153.culturalNotes: Apples are very rich in pectin so the jam sets easily. Green apples give a tarter taste and paler colour.

add-153-i1.name: Apples, peeled, grated or small cubes

instructions.1: Peel the apples and grate coarsely or cut into small cubes, sprinkling with lemon juice so they don't brown.
instructions.2: Put the apples with the sugar, water and cinnamon in a pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.3: Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring, until the apples are translucent golden and the jam thickens.
