instructions.4: Remove the cinnamon and pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-154.title: Mixed Berry Jam
add-154.culturalNotes: You can press half the batch through a fine sieve to remove seeds for a smoother jam. Frozen berries give excellent results and are available year-round.

add-154-i1.name: Mixed berries (raspberry, blueberry, blackberry), fresh or frozen

instructions.1: Wash and drain the berries and lightly crush half of them with a fork.
instructions.2: Cook the berries and sugar in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and it boils.
instructions.3: Boil 20-25 minutes, skimming and stirring, until thick, adding the lemon in the last 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Test on a cold plate and pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-155.title: Damask Rose Petal Jam
add-155.culturalNotes: Rose jam is a preserve of Damascene homes. Use fragrant, unsprayed roses; the citric acid is what restores their pink colour.

add-155-i4.name: Citric acid or juice of 1 lemon

instructions.1: Separate the petals and trim off their bitter white base, rinse gently and drain.
instructions.2: Rub the petals with ½ cup of the sugar until they wilt and release their colour; cover and leave overnight.
instructions.3: Boil the remaining sugar with the water until dissolved, add the petals and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the citric acid, which turns the colour bright pink, and cook 5 more minutes until thick.
instructions.5: Pour into small sterilised jars and serve with cheese and Middle Eastern sweets.

add-156.title: Msabbaha (Warm Chickpeas in Tahini)
add-156.culturalNotes: Msabbaha is hummus with tahini made with whole chickpeas instead of puréed ones, served warm at Levantine and Palestinian breakfasts.

add-156-i8.name: Olive oil, parsley and paprika to serve

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight with the bicarbonate, then rinse.
instructions.2: Boil in fresh water until very tender (about an hour), keeping a cup of the cooking water.
instructions.3: Whisk the tahini with the lemon, garlic, cumin, salt and a little cooking water into a creamy sauce.
instructions.4: Lightly crush a quarter of the chickpeas and mix all the hot chickpeas with the sauce.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish and top with the chilli-lemon dressing, olive oil, parsley and paprika; serve warm.

add-157.title: Orange Marmalade
add-157.culturalNotes: The peel must be fully tender before the sugar goes in, as it won't soften afterwards. Orange seeds are a natural pectin source that helps it set.

instructions.1: Wash the oranges well, halve and squeeze, keeping the juice and the seeds (tie the seeds in a cloth; they are rich in pectin).
instructions.2: Cut the peel into very thin strips and soak with the juice, water and seed bag overnight.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil, then simmer 40 minutes until the peel is completely tender.
instructions.4: Remove the seed bag, add the sugar and lemon juice and boil hard 15-20 minutes, stirring, until it reaches setting point on a cold plate.
instructions.5: Leave 10 minutes so the peel spreads evenly, then pour into sterilised jars.

add-158.title: Fig Jam
add-158.culturalNotes: Fig jam with sesame and anise is a traditional Levantine preserve, served at breakfast with white cheese.

instructions.1: Wash the figs and remove the stems; quarter them or leave whole if small.
instructions.2: Mix with the sugar and leave 2 hours to release their juice.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil over medium heat, then simmer on low heat 35-40 minutes, stirring, until thick and darker.
instructions.4: Add the lemon and anise or mastic five minutes before removing, then the sesame or walnuts.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars.

add-159.title: Burger Sauce
add-159.culturalNotes: Chopped pickles and pickle juice are the secret of the sweet-tangy taste that resembles famous burger chains' sauce.

add-159-i8.name: Sugar and a pinch of black pepper

instructions.1: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl until smooth.
instructions.2: Cover and chill at least 30 minutes so the flavours blend; keeps 5 days in the fridge.

add-160.title: Beef Fajitas
add-160.culturalNotes: Slicing the beef against the grain and cooking it quickly over very high heat gives tender, not chewy, strips.

add-160-i1.name: Beef steak, thin slices against the grain

add-160-i6.name: Cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and chilli

add-160-i10.name: Tortillas, sour cream and salsa to serve

instructions.1: Marinate the beef with the oil, lemon, garlic, soy sauce and spices, cover and chill at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Heat an iron pan on very high heat and sear the beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned outside and still tender, then remove.
instructions.3: Stir-fry the vegetables in the same pan on high heat until slightly softened but still crisp.
instructions.4: Return the beef to the vegetables for a minute and serve at once with warm tortillas, sour cream and salsa.

add-161.title: Homemade Chili Flakes
add-161.culturalNotes: Wear gloves when handling hot chillies and avoid touching your eyes. Toasting the flakes a minute in a dry pan before use makes them more fragrant.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the chillies well and split them lengthwise (keep the seeds for more heat or remove them for less).
instructions.2: Arrange on a tray and dry in the oven at 60-70°C with the door slightly open for 3-4 hours until brittle, or in the sun for several days.
instructions.3: Let cool completely, then pulse briefly in a grinder for coarse flakes, or grind fine for chilli powder.
instructions.4: Store in an airtight jar away from light.

add-162.title: Braised Beef with Eggplant
add-162.culturalNotes: Frying or roasting the eggplant before adding it keeps its shape so it doesn't fall apart in the sauce, and deepens the flavour.

add-162-i8.name: Mixed spice, cinnamon and a pinch of black pepper

instructions.1: Sprinkle the eggplant with salt and leave 20 minutes, then dry and fry until golden, or brush with oil and roast in the oven.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, add the meat and stir until it changes colour, then the garlic and spices.
instructions.3: Add the tomato paste, tomatoes and water, cover and simmer an hour until the meat is tender.
instructions.4: Add the eggplant and pepper and cook 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
instructions.5: Serve with white rice.

add-163.title: Lime-Cured Black Olives
add-163.culturalNotes: Lime speeds up removing the bitterness of olives instead of soaking for weeks, but use only the clear water and rinse the olives well afterwards.

add-163-i3.name: Water
add-163-i3.standardAmount: 2 litres for the lime + for the brine

instructions.1: Wash and drain the olives; mix the lime with 2 litres of water and leave until it settles.
instructions.2: Pour only the clear water (not the sediment) over the olives and leave 24 hours, stirring every 5 hours.
instructions.3: Drain the olives and rinse several times, then soak in plain water changed twice a day for 3-4 days until the bitterness is gone.
instructions.4: Make a brine of water and salt (a cup of salt per 2 litres), pack the olives in jars with the chillies and lemon and cover with brine.
instructions.5: Top with a layer of olive oil, seal and leave a week before eating.

add-164.title: Kunafa Mabrouma (Rolled Kunafa Fingers)
add-164.culturalNotes: Mabrouma is a Levantine kunafa sweet traditionally filled with Aleppo pistachios. Tight rolling keeps the fingers from coming apart after baking.

add-164-i1.name: Fresh shredded kunafa dough at room temperature

instructions.1: Cut a long strip of kunafa about 20 cm and lay it flat.
instructions.2: Brush with melted ghee and lay a line of nuts along one end.
instructions.3: Roll the strip from that end into a tight finger and trim the excess.
instructions.4: Pack the fingers tightly in a ghee-greased tray and brush with the remaining ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with top and bottom heat for 25 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Pour the syrup over as soon as it comes out, then cut and garnish with pistachios.

add-165.title: Egyptian Linza (Coconut Cake with Custard)
add-165.culturalNotes: Linza is a popular Egyptian bakery sweet; the custard layer in the middle sets it apart from ordinary coconut cake.

instructions.1: Mix the milk, cornflour, cream powder and vanilla cold, then stir over heat until thick; cover until cool.
instructions.2: Cream the butter with the icing sugar, then add the eggs one at a time.
instructions.3: Add the flour, coconut, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk until smooth.
instructions.4: Spread two-thirds of the batter in a greased tray, then the cold custard, then spoon the rest of the batter on top.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until the top colours.
instructions.6: Let cool completely, brush the top with jam if you like and cut into squares.

add-166.title: Soft 'Soufflé' Dough for Savory Pastries
add-166.culturalNotes: The dough is called 'soufflé' for its cotton-like lightness. The egg white and milk keep it soft until the next day.

add-166-i8.name: Egg yolk with a little milk for brushing

add-166-i9.name: Fillings as you like (cheese, chicken, sausage)

instructions.1: Mix the yeast and sugar with the warm milk, then add the oil and egg white.
instructions.2: Add the flour and salt gradually and knead until very soft and smooth and not sticky; cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into small balls, roll out, fill with your favourite filling and shape into fingers, triangles or rounds.
instructions.4: Leave 20 minutes to rise again and brush with the yolk and milk.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until golden.

add-167.title: Levantine Ouzi (Spiced Rice and Lamb Parcels)
add-167.culturalNotes: Ouzi is originally a whole lamb stuffed with rice; the filo parcels are a home way of serving it as elegant individual portions.

instructions.1: Brown the meat in 2 tbsp ghee, cover with hot water, add the bay leaves, spices and salt and cook an hour until tender, keeping the stock.
instructions.2: Stir the rice in a spoon of ghee, add stock to just cover it and the salt and cook until absorbed, then add the peas.
instructions.3: Mix the rice with the meat and half the nuts.
instructions.4: Brush two filo sheets with ghee and stack them in a small bowl; add a few nuts, then rice, gather the edges into a parcel and turn it out onto a tray.
instructions.5: Brush the parcels with ghee and bake at 190°C for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Serve with yogurt or cucumber-yogurt salad.

add-168.title: Orange Semolina Basbousa
add-168.culturalNotes: Zest in the batter and juice in the syrup give a clear, fresh orange flavour that lightens the sweetness of the basbousa.

add-168-i11.name: Syrup: sugar, water and orange juice
add-168-i11.standardAmount: 1½ cups sugar + 1 cup water + ½ cup juice

instructions.1: Boil the sugar and water, add the orange juice and simmer 5 minutes; let the syrup cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, flour, coconut and baking powder.
instructions.3: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and zest, then add the orange juice, yogurt and oil.
instructions.4: Add the wet mix to the dry and stir in one direction until smooth, then pour into a greased tin.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat until coloured.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over while hot.

add-169.title: Dry Tahini Powder and Instant Tahini Sauce
add-169.culturalNotes: A dry powder that keeps for months and turns into tahini sauce in a minute; handy for trips and small kitchens.

add-169-i7.name: For the sauce: lemon juice and vinegar

instructions.1: Toast the flour in a dry pan on low heat, stirring, until light beige, and toast the sesame separately until golden.
instructions.2: Grind the sesame fine, mix with the toasted flour and salt, sift and store in an airtight jar.
instructions.3: For the sauce: mix 2 tbsp of the powder with the oil, then the water, lemon, vinegar and cumin, and whisk until creamy.
instructions.4: Serve the sauce at once with falafel, shawarma and grills.

add-170.title: Oven Tandoori Chicken
add-170.culturalNotes: Kashmiri chilli gives the signature red colour without fierce heat. Marinating in two stages, lemon first then yogurt, makes the chicken very tender.

instructions.1: Score the thighs deeply and marinate with the lemon, half the garlic and ginger, half the chilli and the salt for 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the yogurt with the remaining garlic, ginger and chilli, the masala, pepper and mustard, coat the chicken well and chill 4 hours or overnight.
instructions.3: Place the chicken on a rack over a tray and bake at 220°C for 35 minutes, turning once.
instructions.4: Baste with butter and grill 5 minutes until the edges char slightly.
instructions.5: Serve with sliced onion, lemon and mint yogurt sauce.

add-171.title: Pressure-Cooker Lamb Mandi
add-171.culturalNotes: A pressure cooker cuts the cooking of lamb to under an hour, and smoking with an ember at the end gives the tannour flavour without an oven.

add-171-i7.name: Cinnamon stick, coriander seeds, cardamom, bay leaves and peppercorns
add-171-i7.standardAmount: 1 stick + ½ tsp + 7 pods + 2 leaves + ½ tsp

instructions.1: Season the meat with the salt, pepper, turmeric and half the saffron.
instructions.2: Put the meat in the pressure cooker with the whole spices and water to cover and cook 35-40 minutes until tender, then lift out and strain the stock.
instructions.3: Brown the meat under the oven grill or in a pan until coloured.
instructions.4: Stir the rice in the oil for 2 minutes, add the stock (1½ times the rice volume) and salt, cook until absorbed, then cover on low heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the remaining saffron, lay the meat on the rice, smoke with the ember inside the closed pot for 10 minutes and garnish with raisins.

add-172.title: Roast Duck à l'Orange
add-172.culturalNotes: Pricking the duck skin lets the thick layer of fat melt and drain, so the skin crisps and the meat isn't greasy.

add-172-i7.name: Cinnamon sticks, bay leaves and cardamom

instructions.1: Dry the duck well and prick the skin with a fork without reaching the meat; season inside and out with salt, pepper and orange zest.
instructions.2: Stuff with the onion, half an orange and the whole spices.
instructions.3: Place on a rack over a tray with a cup of water, cover and roast at 180°C for 1½ hours, pouring off the fat that collects.
instructions.4: Mix the orange juice, honey, soy sauce and butter.
instructions.5: Uncover and baste the duck with the mixture every 10 minutes for 30-40 minutes until the skin is glossy brown and crisp.
instructions.6: Boil the remaining mixture with the pan juices and cornflour until thick, rest the duck 15 minutes before carving and serve with the sauce.

add-173.title: Hummus el-Sham (Hot Spiced Chickpea Drink)
add-173.culturalNotes: Hummus el-Sham is an Egyptian winter drink sold from street carts, drunk very hot with chilli and lemon.

add-173-i5.name: Onion powder, garlic powder and cumin

add-173-i8.name: Chilli dressing: chickpea water and chilli

add-173-i9.name: Cumin dressing: chickpea water, cumin and lemon

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas 10-12 hours, then rinse.
instructions.2: Boil in plenty of water until fully cooked (about an hour).
instructions.3: Add the tomato juice, garlic, spices, stock cube and salt to the chickpeas with their water and boil 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Prepare the chilli and cumin-lemon dressings, each in a small bowl with chickpea water.
instructions.5: Serve the chickpeas with their broth piping hot in cups, adding a spoon of your favourite dressing to each.

add-174.title: Baked New York Cheesecake
add-174.culturalNotes: Low-speed mixing, a water bath and gradual cooling prevent cracks and give the famous dense, smooth texture.

add-174-i11.name: Strawberry or berry sauce to serve

instructions.1: Mix the biscuits and butter, press into a lined springform tin and bake 10 minutes at 170°C.
instructions.2: Beat the cream cheese with the sugar on low speed until smooth, then add the starch, sour cream, cream, lemon and vanilla.
instructions.3: Add the eggs one at a time, mixing lightly just until incorporated, without adding air.
instructions.4: Wrap the outside of the tin in foil, pour in the filling, set in a tray of hot water and bake at 160°C for 60-70 minutes until the edges set and the centre still wobbles slightly.
instructions.5: Turn off the oven and leave the cheesecake inside for an hour with the door ajar, then chill overnight.
instructions.6: Release the tin and serve with strawberry or berry sauce.

add-175.title: Damascene Madlouka with Ashta and Pistachio
add-175.culturalNotes: Madlouka is a Damascene sweet known for the green layer of pistachio covering the ashta. Toasting the semolina well in ghee is the secret of its flavour.

instructions.1: Toast the semolina in the ghee on low heat, stirring, until pale golden and fragrant.
instructions.2: Add the hot milk with the sugar, orange-blossom and rose water gradually, stirring constantly, until the semolina absorbs the liquid and becomes a smooth dough that leaves the pan.
instructions.3: Spread the hot dough in a serving dish 1-2 cm thick and smooth with a ghee-greased spoon.
instructions.4: Spread the ashta over it while warm or once cooled, and cover the whole top with crushed pistachios.
instructions.5: Cut into squares and serve with syrup on the side.

add-176.title: Swiss Meringue Buttercream
add-176.culturalNotes: The golden ratio: one part egg white to twice as much sugar to three times as much butter. It is less sweet and smoother than regular buttercream, ideal for covering and decorating cakes.

add-176-i3.name: Unsalted butter, soft but slightly cool

instructions.1: Put the whites and sugar in the mixer bowl over a pan of gently simmering water and stir constantly until the sugar dissolves completely and the mixture reaches 70°C (no grains felt between your fingers).
instructions.2: Move the bowl to the mixer and whisk on high speed for 10 minutes until a glossy, thick meringue forms and the bowl is completely cool.
instructions.3: Add the butter a cube at a time on medium speed; it may look curdled halfway, then turns smooth again.
instructions.4: Add the vanilla and salt and mix on the lowest speed for 3-5 minutes to knock out air bubbles.
instructions.5: If it turns runny, chill 15 minutes and whisk again; if it curdles, warm part of the bowl from the outside and whisk.

add-177.title: Levantine Chicken Sfiha
add-177.culturalNotes: Yogurt and tahini keep minced chicken moist, since it dries out faster than meat, and pomegranate molasses gives the familiar Levantine tang.

add-177-i8.name: Onion, very finely chopped and drained

instructions.1: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Mix the chicken with the drained onion, garlic, yogurt, tahini, pomegranate molasses, tomato and spices.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into small balls, roll into rounds, add the filling and pinch the edges into squares or triangles.
instructions.4: Arrange on a greased tray and bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges brown.
instructions.5: Serve hot with lemon or yogurt.

add-178.title: Rocket and Pomegranate Salad
add-178.culturalNotes: The peppery rocket is balanced by sweet pomegranate and tangy molasses. Serve alongside kibbeh and grills.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the rocket well and tear roughly or leave whole.
instructions.2: Whisk the olive oil, pomegranate molasses, lemon, sumac and salt.
instructions.3: Toss the rocket and onion in a dish, pour over the dressing just before serving and scatter the pomegranate and walnuts on top.

add-179.title: Homemade Bully Beef
add-179.culturalNotes: Bully beef is a canned pressed meat; this preservative-free home version keeps two days in the fridge or 2-3 months frozen.

add-179-i3.name: Crushed soy, soaked in a cup of water

instructions.1: Soak the soy in the water until it absorbs it and softens.
instructions.2: Process the meat, suet, soy, spices and starch together into a very smooth paste.
instructions.3: Pack into a greased metal tin or heatproof jar with no gaps and cover tightly with foil.
instructions.4: Cook in a water bath (a pot of gently simmering water halfway up the tin) for a full hour.
instructions.5: Let cool, chill overnight, then unmould and slice for sandwiches.

add-180.title: Saudi Cardamom Coffee (Gahwa)
add-180.culturalNotes: Putting the cardamom in the thermos rather than the dallah keeps its aroma fresh. Saudi coffee is served with the right hand, filling only a third of the cup.

instructions.1: Bring the water to a strong boil in the dallah.
instructions.2: Add the coffee and simmer on low heat 10-12 minutes until coloured and the foaming settles, watching so it doesn't boil over.
instructions.3: Put the cardamom, cloves and saffron in the bottom of the thermos (mattara), not in the dallah.
instructions.4: Take the dallah off the heat for a minute so the grounds settle, then gently pour the coffee over the cardamom in the thermos.
instructions.5: Leave 5 minutes to take on the cardamom aroma and serve in small cups with dates.

add-181.title: Baby Eggplant Jam
add-181.culturalNotes: Eggplant jam is a luxury Levantine preserve. Soaking the eggplants in salt overnight firms their fibres so they hold their shape without needing lime.

instructions.1: Peel the eggplants leaving the cap, prick all over with a fork, soak overnight in salted water and rinse well.
instructions.2: Boil in water for 5 minutes until slightly soft, drain and squeeze gently.
instructions.3: Boil the sugar and water until dissolved, then add the eggplants, cloves and cinnamon.
instructions.4: Simmer on very low heat for 1-1½ hours until the eggplants are dark, glossy and translucent and the syrup is thick, adding the lemon at the end.
instructions.5: Pack the eggplants with their syrup into sterilised jars.

add-182.title: Crispy Chicken Salad
add-182.culturalNotes: A complete meal of protein and vegetables. Adding the chicken and dressing at the last moment keeps it crisp.

add-182-i2.name: Chopped garlic and onion for marinating

add-182-i3.name: Black pepper, paprika and ground coriander

add-182-i5.name: Breadcrumbs with a spoon of starch

add-182-i9.name: Grated carrot, bell pepper and corn

add-182-i10.name: Dressing: mayonnaise, honey, mustard and lemon

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the garlic, onion, spices, vinegar and yogurt for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Coat the fingers in the breadcrumbs mixed with starch, pressing well.
instructions.3: Fry in medium oil until golden, crisp and cooked, drain and cut into pieces.
instructions.4: Mix the vegetables in a large bowl and whisk the dressing ingredients.
instructions.5: Arrange the crispy chicken over the vegetables and pour over the dressing just before serving.

add-183.title: Budget Yogurt Cheesecake
add-183.culturalNotes: Milk powder thickens the yogurt to a firm texture with no gelatine or whipping cream, making this version economical and lighter.

instructions.1: Mix the biscuits with the butter and milk, press into the base of the tin and chill.
instructions.2: Beat the yogurt with the cream cheese, milk powder, sugar and vanilla until thick and smooth.
instructions.3: Pour over the base and smooth the top.
instructions.4: Chill 4-5 hours until set, then decorate with fresh fruit and ground biscuit.

add-184.title: Lebanese Tabbouleh
add-184.culturalNotes: Lebanese tabbouleh is essentially a parsley salad with very little bulgur. Chopping with a sharp knife rather than a processor keeps the parsley from bruising and darkening.

add-184-i5.name: Spring onions or white onion, finely chopped

add-184-i8.name: Salt and seven spice (or black pepper)

add-184-i9.name: Lettuce or cabbage leaves to serve

instructions.1: Rinse the bulgur and soak in the lemon juice with a little tomato juice for 15 minutes until soft.
instructions.2: Wash and dry the parsley and mint completely, then chop very finely with a knife without crushing.
instructions.3: Cut the tomatoes into tiny dice and chop the onion, rubbing it with the salt and spice.
instructions.4: Combine the parsley, mint, tomatoes, onion and bulgur, add the olive oil and salt, toss gently and serve at once with lettuce leaves.

add-185.title: No-Bake Lotus Biscoff Cheesecake
add-185.culturalNotes: Lotus spread gives the caramel-cinnamon flavour and helps the cream set, so this version needs no gelatine.

add-185-i7.name: Melted Lotus spread for the top

instructions.1: Mix the ground biscuits with the butter, press into a springform tin and chill.
instructions.2: Beat the cream cheese with the cup of Lotus spread and the icing sugar until smooth.
instructions.3: Whip the cold cream until firm and fold gently into the cheese mixture.
instructions.4: Pour over the base, smooth and chill 4-5 hours.
instructions.5: Warm the Lotus spread a few seconds in the microwave and pour over the top, sprinkle with crushed biscuits, release the tin and serve cold.

add-186.title: No-Bake Chocolate Oreo Cheesecake
add-186.culturalNotes: The melted dark chocolate is what sets the filling when cold, so it must be lukewarm when added or the cream cheese will seize.

instructions.1: Mix the ground Oreos with the butter, press into a tin and chill.
instructions.2: Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar and salt until smooth, then add the lukewarm melted chocolate.
instructions.3: Whip the cream until firm and fold gently into the chocolate mixture; pour over the base and chill 3 hours.
instructions.4: For the ganache: pour the hot milk over the chopped chocolate, leave a minute, then stir until glossy.
instructions.5: Pour the lukewarm ganache over the set top, chill 2 hours and decorate with strawberries.

add-187.title: Baked Lemon Cheesecake with Lemon Glaze
add-187.culturalNotes: The zest carries strong lemon flavour without too much acidity, and the glaze on top adds freshness and tang.

add-187-i9.name: For the glaze: sugar, water, lemon juice and starch

instructions.1: Mix the biscuits and butter, press into the tin and bake 10 minutes at 170°C.
instructions.2: Beat the cheese and sugar on low speed, then add the sour cream, zest, juice and vanilla, then the eggs one at a time.
instructions.3: Pour in the filling and bake in a water bath at 160°C for 45-50 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the centre; leave in the switched-off oven for an hour.
instructions.4: For the glaze: dissolve the starch in the water, add the sugar and lemon juice and stir over heat until thick and glossy; let cool.
instructions.5: Chill the cheesecake overnight and pour the lemon glaze over the top before serving.

add-188.title: No-Bake Chocolate Biscuit Cake
add-188.culturalNotes: A quick no-bake sweet known as 'lazy cake'. The spoon of oil in the chocolate gives a shop-style shine and stops it cracking when cut.

instructions.1: Heat the milk with the cocoa and butter, remove from the heat and add the dark chocolate, stirring until melted and glossy.
instructions.2: Fold in the broken biscuits and nuts until all are coated.
instructions.3: Press into a rectangular tin lined with baking paper, or roll into small balls, and chill 2 hours.
instructions.4: Melt the milk chocolate with the spoon of oil and pour over the top or dip the balls in it.
instructions.5: Chill until completely set and cut into slices or squares.

add-189.title: Crispy Cheesy Potato Balls
add-189.culturalNotes: The potatoes must be dry and well mashed; too much moisture makes the balls crack in the oil.

add-189-i8.name: For coating: eggs beaten with milk

instructions.1: Mix the mashed potato with the yolk, butter, spices, cornflour, coriander and salt.
instructions.2: Take a ball, flatten it in your palm, put a cube of cheese in the centre and seal well.
instructions.3: Coat the balls in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, and chill 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp and drain.
instructions.5: Serve hot with the cheese stretchy inside, with ketchup or toum.

add-190.title: Strawberry Jam Pasta Frolla Tart
add-190.culturalNotes: Pasta frolla is a crumbly Italian shortcrust; chilling it before rolling makes it easy to handle and stops the butter melting.

add-190-i6.name: Baking powder and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Cream the butter with the icing sugar, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, baking powder and salt and bring the dough together without long kneading; wrap and chill 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Press two-thirds of the dough into the base and sides of a greased rectangular or round tin.
instructions.4: Mix the jam with the lemon and spread over the dough.
instructions.5: Roll the remaining dough, cut into strips and lay them over the jam in a lattice, or grate the frozen dough over the top.
instructions.6: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the edges brown and let cool before cutting.

add-191.title: Algerian Qalb el-Louz
add-191.culturalNotes: Qalb el-louz is a Ramadan sweet in Algeria. The secret is soaking it slowly with plenty of hot syrup so it becomes soft and melting.

add-191-i9.name: For the filling (optional): ground almonds, sugar and orange-blossom water

add-191-i10.name: Syrup with orange-blossom water and honey

instructions.1: Mix the semolina, sugar, vanilla and baking powder, add the milk, oil and orange-blossom water and fold gently without kneading until absorbed.
instructions.2: Cover and rest an hour.
instructions.3: Spread half the mixture in a greased tray, spread the almond filling if using, then the rest of the mixture and level without pressing.
instructions.4: Cut into diamonds and place an almond on each.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until deep golden.
instructions.6: Pour the hot syrup gradually over the hot cake until fully absorbed and leave several hours before cutting.

add-192.title: Spiced Minced Meat Pizza
add-192.culturalNotes: Cooking the meat until its juices dry before putting it on the dough stops the pizza going soggy in the middle.

instructions.1: Knead the dough ingredients until elastic and smooth and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, add the meat and spices and cook until done and the juices dry, then the pepper for a minute.
instructions.3: Spread the dough in two greased trays and spread with the sauce.
instructions.4: Scatter the meat, then the cheese and olives and sprinkle with oregano.
instructions.5: Bake at 230°C for 15-20 minutes until the edges brown and the cheese melts.

add-193.title: Syrian Chicken Shawarma Fatteh
add-193.culturalNotes: Shawarma fatteh is a Syrian dish combining yellow rice, shawarma and yogurt-tahini sauce. The crisp bread goes on top at the end so it stays crunchy.

add-193-i3.name: Turmeric and ghee for the rice

add-193-i5.name: Yogurt and lemon juice for marinating

add-193-i7.name: Black pepper, cardamom, paprika, ground coriander and mastic
add-193-i7.standardAmount: ½ tsp each + a pinch of mastic

add-193-i8.name: Lebanese bread squares, fried or toasted

add-193-i9.name: For the sauce: yogurt, tahini, vinegar, cumin and garlic
add-193-i9.standardAmount: 1 cup + 3 tbsp + 1 tbsp + a pinch + 1 clove

add-193-i10.name: Parsley and pickled cucumber to garnish

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, lemon, garlic, onion and spices for an hour.
instructions.2: Stir the rice in the ghee with the turmeric, add the stock and cook until done.
instructions.3: Sear the chicken in a very hot pan until cooked and browned.
instructions.4: Whisk the yogurt-tahini sauce ingredients until smooth, thinning with warm water if thick.
instructions.5: Spread half the bread in a dish, then the rice, then the shawarma, then the sauce, and top with the rest of the bread, parsley and pickles.

add-194.title: Minced Meat and Ruqaq Fatta
add-194.culturalNotes: Toasted ruqaq gives this fatta a different texture from baladi bread; it absorbs the stock while staying slightly firm.

add-194-i6.name: Black pepper, ground cardamom and paprika

instructions.1: Cook the rice in a spoon of ghee with the stock and salt until done.
instructions.2: Soften the onion in ghee, add the meat and spices and cook until done and crumbly.
instructions.3: Break the ruqaq into pieces and toast in the oven with a spoon of ghee until golden, then moisten with hot stock.
instructions.4: For the sauce: fry half the garlic in ghee, add the tomato juice and salt and cook down. For the dressing: fry the remaining garlic in ghee and add the vinegar.
instructions.5: Spread the moistened ruqaq in a dish, sprinkle with the garlic-vinegar dressing, then the rice, then the minced meat, then the sauce.

add-195.title: Aleppo Ghazl el-Banat (Pistachio Phyllo Layers)
add-195.culturalNotes: Low heat and long baking are needed so the inner layers cook and crisp without the top burning. Clarified butter gives the characteristic Aleppo aroma.

add-195-i4.name: Sugar and orange-blossom water for the filling

add-195-i6.name: Syrup: lemon juice and rose water

instructions.1: Boil the sugar and water, add the lemon and simmer 10 minutes, then the rose water; let the syrup cool.
instructions.2: Mix the pistachios with the sugar and orange-blossom water.
instructions.3: Grease a tray with ghee and layer 10-12 filo sheets, brushing each with ghee.
instructions.4: Spread the pistachios evenly, then layer 10-12 more sheets, brushing each, and brush the top well.
instructions.5: Cut the tray into diamonds or squares with a sharp knife right to the bottom before baking.
instructions.6: Bake in a gentle oven at 160°C for about an hour until pale golden and crisp inside.
instructions.7: Pour the cold syrup over as soon as it comes out and leave several hours before serving.

add-196.title: Shanklish Salad
add-196.culturalNotes: Shanklish is a sharp aged Syrian-Lebanese cheese; generous olive oil and tomatoes tame its sharpness. No salt is needed.

instructions.1: Crumble the shanklish with a fork into small, uneven pieces.
instructions.2: Mix the tomatoes, onion, pepper and parsley in a bowl.
instructions.3: Add the shanklish, toss gently, pour over plenty of olive oil and serve with Arabic bread.

add-197.title: Grilled Kibbeh Discs (Kibbeh Mishwiyeh)
add-197.culturalNotes: The tail fat in the filling melts during grilling so the kibbeh stays juicy inside. It is a prized dish of Aleppo and the Syrian Jazira.

add-197-i3.name: Small onion, salt, allspice and cinnamon for the dough

add-197-i8.name: Red chilli, salt and allspice for the filling

instructions.1: Make the kibbeh dough: process the lean meat with the onion and spices, then add the bulgur and knead with hands dipped in iced water until it holds together.
instructions.2: For the raw filling: mix the minced meat with the tail fat, walnuts, pomegranate molasses, chilli and spices.
instructions.3: Roll a ball of dough between two plastic sheets into a thin disc, spread with filling, cover with a second disc and seal the edges well.
instructions.4: Brush the discs with olive oil and grill over medium charcoal for 6-7 minutes each side until the filling is cooked and the crust browned.
instructions.5: Serve hot with yogurt and salad.

add-198.title: Yemeni Fahsa (Shredded Lamb Stew)
add-198.culturalNotes: Fahsa is saltah's sister, but made with mashed meat instead of broth, and served bubbling in a stone pot.

add-198-i6.name: Cumin, turmeric, black pepper and broth spice (hawaij)

instructions.1: Boil the meat with a little onion and spice until fully cooked and falling off the bone (about 1½ hours), keeping the broth.
instructions.2: Shred the meat and remove the bones.
instructions.3: For the kishna: soften the onion in the ghee, then the garlic, chilli, tomatoes and paste until cooked down.
instructions.4: Add the shredded meat and a cup of broth to the kishna and mash with a wooden spoon until blended and fully shredded (tafhees).
instructions.5: Whip the soaked fenugreek with the sahawiq into a foam.
instructions.6: Heat the fahsa in a stone madra or heavy pot until bubbling hard, top with the fenugreek and serve at once with malawah bread.

add-199.title: Iraqi Dolma (Mixed Stuffed Vegetables)
add-199.culturalNotes: Iraqi dolma cooks many vegetables together, and the 'hakka' is the crisp browned layer of meat or bread at the bottom of the pot that everyone competes for.

add-199-i2.name: Coarse minced meat with tail fat

add-199-i10.name: Eggplant, zucchini, peppers and small tomatoes to hollow

add-199-i11.name: Lamb ribs or bone-in meat for the base of the pot (hakka)

instructions.1: Core the vegetables, boil the large onions 5 minutes and separate the layers, and blanch the grape leaves 2 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the rice with the meat, onion, garlic, pomegranate molasses, tomato paste, spices and oil.
instructions.3: Fill the vegetables three-quarters full and roll the grape leaves and onion layers around the stuffing.
instructions.4: Brown the meat in the base of a heavy pot, pack the stuffed vegetables tightly on top and place an upturned plate over them.
instructions.5: Add hot water mixed with pomegranate molasses and salt to cover and cook over medium then low heat for 60-90 minutes until the rice is cooked and the water absorbed.
instructions.6: Invert the pot onto a large platter so the browned hakka sits on top and serve hot.

add-200.title: Egg-Stuffed Taameya (Falafel)
add-200.culturalNotes: Drying the eggs well before wrapping stops the mix sliding off. Medium heat is needed because the layer is thick and takes time to cook.

instructions.1: Add the ground coriander and bicarbonate to the mix just before frying and stir well.
instructions.2: Peel the boiled eggs and dry them well.
instructions.3: Flatten a portion of the mix in your palm, set an egg in the centre and wrap it fully in an even layer, pressing to hold together.
instructions.4: Roll in sesame.
instructions.5: Fry in medium oil, turning, until deep golden and crisp and the mix is cooked through to the egg, 6-8 minutes.
instructions.6: Cut in half and serve with tahini and salad.

add-201.title: Chilled Hibiscus (Karkadeh) Drink
add-201.culturalNotes: Cold soaking gives a more ruby colour and less bitterness than boiling. Karkadeh is a Ramadan drink and the wedding drink of Egypt and Sudan.

instructions.1: Rinse the hibiscus quickly in cold water to remove dust.
instructions.2: Soak in lukewarm water for 4 hours or overnight in the fridge (for cold), or boil for just 2 minutes then let cool (for quick preparation).
instructions.3: Strain well, dissolve the sugar in it and add the orange-blossom water.
instructions.4: Serve chilled with lemon slices and mint, or hot in winter.

add-202.title: Mahalabia Cups with Strawberry Jelly
add-202.culturalNotes: The jelly must be completely cool before pouring, or it will melt the top of the mahalabia and the layers will mix.

instructions.1: Dissolve the starch and sugar in the cold milk and stir over medium heat until thick and boiling, then add the vanilla.
instructions.2: Divide among the cups and leave to cool, then chill an hour until the surface sets.
instructions.3: Dissolve the jelly in the boiling water, add the cold water and leave until completely cool and just starting to set.
instructions.4: Scatter strawberries over the mahalabia, pour the jelly gently over the back of a spoon and chill 3-4 hours until set.

add-203.title: Qidra Khalili (Hebron Rice with Lamb and Chickpeas)
add-203.culturalNotes: Qidra is the dish of Hebron in Palestine, traditionally cooked in a clay jar in communal ovens. The whole garlic cloves turn soft and sweet and are essential.

add-203-i6.name: Turmeric and qidra spices (cumin, cardamom, mixed spice)

add-203-i7.name: Onion, bay leaves and cinnamon for boiling

add-203-i10.name: Toasted almonds and pine nuts to garnish

instructions.1: Boil the meat with the onion, bay leaves and cinnamon for 1½ hours until cooked, keeping the stock.
instructions.2: Brown the meat in a spoon of ghee with the turmeric and spices.
instructions.3: Mix the soaked rice with the chickpeas, garlic cloves, ghee, spices and salt.
instructions.4: Lay the meat in the bottom of a clay or copper qidra pot, put the rice mixture on top and pour in hot stock to 2 cm above the rice.
instructions.5: Cover tightly and bake at 180°C for an hour until the rice is cooked and the stock absorbed.
instructions.6: Invert the qidra onto a large platter in front of the guests and garnish with the nuts.

add-204.title: Jordanian Mansaf
add-204.culturalNotes: Mansaf is Jordan's national dish and a symbol of generosity, traditionally eaten with the right hand. Shaneena softens the sharpness and saltiness of the jameed.

add-204-i2.name: Soaked, rubbed Karaki jameed (or liquid jameed)

add-204-i6.name: Onion, cardamom, bay leaves and cinnamon for boiling

add-204-i9.name: Almonds and pine nuts toasted in ghee

instructions.1: Boil the meat with the onion and whole spices, skimming, until 70% cooked (about an hour), keeping the stock.
instructions.2: Cook the rubbed jameed with the shaneena over medium heat, stirring in one direction until it boils, then gradually add two cups of the meat stock.
instructions.3: Move the meat into the jameed sauce and simmer 45 minutes until fully tender and soaked in the sauce.
instructions.4: Stir the rice in a spoon of ghee with the turmeric and cook with the meat stock until done.
instructions.5: Spread the shrak on a large platter and moisten with a little jameed, heap the rice on top and arrange the meat on the summit.
instructions.6: Pour over jameed, garnish with nuts and parsley and serve with the rest of the hot jameed in a side bowl.

add-205.title: Tunisian Slata Mechouia
add-205.culturalNotes: Mechouia is one of Tunisia's best-known salads, with a smoky flavour from charcoal grilling. Tabil and karwiya are the core Tunisian spice blend.

add-205-i6.name: Tabil and karwiya (ground coriander and caraway)

add-205-i8.name: Tuna, boiled egg and olives to garnish

instructions.1: Grill the peppers, tomatoes, onion and garlic over charcoal, a direct flame or under the grill until the skins blacken and they soften.
instructions.2: Put the hot vegetables in a sealed plastic bag for 5 minutes to make peeling easy.
instructions.3: Peel the vegetables, seed the peppers and chop coarsely with a knife or pound in a mortar.
instructions.4: Add the olive oil, tabil, karwiya, salt and lemon and mix.
instructions.5: Serve garnished with tuna, boiled egg and olives, with bread.

add-206.title: Oxtail Tagine with Caramelized Onions
add-206.culturalNotes: Oxtail needs long cooking until the collagen melts and the meat falls off the bone. Add salt only at the end.

add-206-i1.name: Oxtail, cut into rings and cleaned

add-206-i6.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and mastic

instructions.1: Boil the oxtail in water with the aromatics until 70% cooked (about 2 hours in a regular pot or 40 minutes in a pressure cooker), keeping the stock.
instructions.2: Cook the onions in the ghee on low heat for 20-25 minutes until caramelised golden brown.
instructions.3: Add the garlic, peppers and spices and stir, then 1½ cups of the stock.
instructions.4: Arrange the oxtail in a clay tagine, pour the onions and their sauce over and adjust the salt.
instructions.5: Cover with foil and bake at 200°C for 45 minutes, then uncover for the last 10 minutes so the top browns.
instructions.6: Serve hot with white rice or baladi bread.

add-207.title: Fresh Strawberry Juice
add-207.culturalNotes: Lemon keeps the bright red colour, and a small piece of beetroot deepens it without any taste showing.

add-207-i5.name: Small piece of boiled beetroot (optional, for colour)

instructions.1: Wash, hull and chop the strawberries.
instructions.2: Blend with the sugar, water, lemon and beetroot until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Pour over ice and garnish the rim of the glass with a whole strawberry.
instructions.4: For a strawberry milkshake, use cold milk instead of water and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

add-208.title: Baked Sardine Tray with Lemon and Vegetables
add-208.culturalNotes: Sardines are rich in omega-3 and economical. The layer of onion underneath stops the fish sticking and sweetens the sauce.

add-208-i9.name: Crushed garlic, cumin and ground coriander

instructions.1: Clean the sardines, removing the heads and guts, wash with vinegar and lemon and drain.
instructions.2: Mix the lemon juice, oil, garlic, spices and salt and marinate the sardines 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Lay the onion rings in the tray, then the sardines, then the tomatoes, peppers and lemon slices, and pour over the rest of the marinade.
instructions.4: Cover with foil and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, then uncover for 10 minutes until the top browns.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with parsley and serve with rice or bread.

add-209.title: Jerusalem Sesame Kaak
add-209.culturalNotes: Jerusalem kaak is the famous street bread of Jerusalem with its long oval shape. Water sweetened with molasses gives it its darker colour and holds the sesame.

add-209-i9.name: Water sweetened with sugar or molasses to hold the sesame

instructions.1: Knead the dough ingredients with the warm water for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic and leave an hour to double.
instructions.2: Divide into 10 balls, roll each into a long rope and join into an elongated oval ring.
instructions.3: Dip each ring in the sweetened water, then roll in sesame on all sides.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray and rest 15 minutes to rise again.
instructions.5: Bake in a hot oven at 230°C for 12-15 minutes until deep golden.
instructions.6: Serve with za'atar, falafel, eggs or cheese.

add-210.title: Freekeh and Beef Tagine
add-210.culturalNotes: Freekeh is smoked green wheat, and cooking it in a clay tagine gives a fluffy texture and rich smoky flavour; it is a dish of rural Egypt.

instructions.1: Sear the meat in a spoon of ghee with the pepper until coloured, then add a little water and cook until 70% done.
instructions.2: Fry the onion in the remaining ghee until golden, add the freekeh and stir 2 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the tomato juice, spices and salt and stir, then the stock, and boil 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Put the meat in a clay tagine and pour the freekeh with its liquid over it.
instructions.5: Cover and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes until the freekeh is cooked and the stock absorbed, then uncover to brown the top.
instructions.6: Serve hot in the tagine.

add-211.title: Grape Leaf Fatteh with Minced Meat
add-211.culturalNotes: A creative way to turn leftover stuffed grape leaves into a new, festive dish.

add-211-i1.name: Cooked chopped grape leaves (or leftover stuffed grape leaves)

add-211-i5.name: Salt, pepper, cinnamon and pomegranate molasses

add-211-i10.name: Toasted pine nuts and ghee to garnish

instructions.1: Soften the onion, then cook the meat with the spices and pomegranate molasses until done and crumbly.
instructions.2: Mix the rice with the chopped grape leaves and half the meat and warm through.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon and salt.
instructions.4: Spread the bread in the base of the dish, then the rice and grape-leaf mixture, then the yogurt sauce.
instructions.5: Scatter the rest of the meat and the pine nuts toasted in ghee on top and serve at once.

add-212.title: Chocolate-Coated Halawa (Rahash) Balls
add-212.culturalNotes: Rahash (tahini halawa) with chocolate is a quick three-ingredient sweet; freezing before dipping is the secret of a neat finish.

instructions.1: Crumble the halawa and mix with the ashta and nuts until it holds together like dough.
instructions.2: Roll into small balls and freeze 20 minutes so they don't melt when dipped.
instructions.3: Melt the chocolate with the oil over a water bath or in the microwave until fluid.
instructions.4: Dip the balls with a fork in the chocolate, set on baking paper, decorate with nuts and chill until set.

add-213.title: Halawa (Rahash) Roll with Pistachio
add-213.culturalNotes: Liquid tahini softens the halawa so it can be shaped, and pistachios inside and out make an elegant sweet to serve with coffee.

instructions.1: Knead the crumbled halawa with the tahini and cardamom into a firm, rollable dough.
instructions.2: Roll into a rectangle ½ cm thick between two sheets of baking paper.
instructions.3: Sprinkle half the pistachios over the top, press in, then roll up tightly.
instructions.4: Roll the log in the remaining pistachios to coat.
instructions.5: Wrap in baking paper, chill an hour, then cut into round slices.

add-214.title: Tamriya (Date Slice with Sesame and Tahini)
add-214.culturalNotes: Tamriya is served with Arabic coffee in the Gulf, and the slightly bitter tahini balances the sweetness of the dates.

instructions.1: Warm the dates with the butter over low heat, stirring and mashing until soft and smooth.
instructions.2: Add the biscuit crumbs, cardamom, cinnamon and half the sesame and knead well.
instructions.3: Press into a tray lined with baking paper 1.5 cm thick and level.
instructions.4: Spread the tahini over the top, sprinkle with the rest of the sesame, chill an hour and cut into squares.

add-215.title: Date and Nut Balls
add-215.culturalNotes: A healthy alternative to processed sweets and a quick energy source; you can press a whole almond into each ball.

add-215-i2.name: Baladi ghee, butter or coconut oil

instructions.1: If the dates are firm, warm them with the ghee over very low heat, stirring, until soft.
instructions.2: Mix the dates with the nuts, cinnamon and cardamom until evenly spread.
instructions.3: Roll into walnut-sized balls with ghee-greased hands.
instructions.4: Roll in coconut or sesame and keep in an airtight container.

add-216.title: Sudanese Helo-Mur (Abreh) Drink
add-216.prepTime: a week to sprout the sorghum
add-216.culturalNotes: Helo-mur is Sudan's most famous Ramadan drink, and making its flakes is a communal ritual weeks before the month. Ready-made flakes are sold in Sudanese shops, cutting the work to soaking.

add-216-i3.name: Helo-mur spices: cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, black cumin, fenugreek

add-216-i6.name: To serve: sugar and cold water

instructions.1: Zariaa: soak the sorghum a day, spread on a damp cloth and cover until it sprouts (5-7 days), then sun-dry and grind.
instructions.2: Mix the sprouted flour with the sorghum flour, ground spices and soaked dates, add water into a batter and leave two days to ferment.
instructions.3: Spread the mixture very thin on a hot griddle until dry, browned and crisp flakes form, then break and store them.
instructions.4: To serve: soak the flakes in cold water for 2-3 hours until their flavour and colour dissolve.
instructions.5: Strain, sweeten with sugar and serve ice-cold at iftar.

add-217.title: Dates with Milk (Balah bel Laban)
add-217.culturalNotes: Dates with milk is the Ramadan iftar drink in Egypt, giving quick energy after fasting. Soaking the dates first gives a velvety texture with no bits.

add-217-i4.name: Crushed nuts and coconut to garnish

instructions.1: Wash and pit the dates and soak in a cup of the milk for an hour until soft.
instructions.2: Blend the dates with the soaking milk until completely smooth, then add the rest of the milk and blend a minute.
instructions.3: Serve cold or warm with a sprinkle of nuts, or leave the dates in pieces in the milk without blending, as you prefer.

add-218.title: Creamy Cheddar Cheese Sauce
add-218.culturalNotes: Grating the cheddar yourself rather than using pre-grated makes it melt smoothly, since pre-grated contains anti-caking starch. Don't let the sauce boil after adding the cheese or it turns grainy.

instructions.1: Melt the butter, add the flour and stir a minute without colouring.
instructions.2: Whisk in the milk gradually so it doesn't lump, and cook until slightly thickened.
instructions.3: Lower the heat right down and add the cheddar in batches, stirring until completely melted, then the mustard and paprika.
instructions.4: Serve warm with nachos, fries and burgers, thinning with a little milk if it thickens.

add-219.title: Baked Potato Kibbeh Tray
add-219.culturalNotes: Potato kibbeh is an easier and cheaper version of traditional kibbeh, and the bulgur gives it the firmness and familiar kibbeh texture.

instructions.1: Knead the potato with the bulgur, egg and spices, adding flour if soft, until the dough holds together.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat with the spices, and add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Spread half the potato dough in a greased tray, spread the filling, then cover with the rest of the dough and smooth with a wet hand.
instructions.4: Score the top in a crisscross with a knife and brush with ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes until the top is golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Serve with yogurt and green salad.

add-220.title: Lebanese Bayaz (Onion, Parsley and Sumac Salad)
add-220.culturalNotes: Rubbing the onion with salt and sumac takes away its sharpness and makes it soft and tangy; it is the classic partner of grills in Lebanese restaurants.

instructions.1: Rub the sliced onion with the salt and sumac between your fingers for a minute until it softens and turns purple.
instructions.2: Add the parsley and toss.
instructions.3: Drizzle with olive oil and lemon if you like and serve at once with grills, kofta and shawarma.

add-221.title: Seasoned Baked Potato Wedges
add-221.culturalNotes: Soaking to remove starch, then drying well, is the secret of crisp oven wedges without frying.

instructions.1: Scrub the potatoes well, halve each lengthwise, then cut each half into 3-4 thick wedges.
instructions.2: Soak in cold water for 15 minutes to remove the starch, then dry completely.
instructions.3: Toss with the oil, spices and salt until coated.
instructions.4: Spread skin-side down on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with Parmesan while hot and serve with garlic sauce or ketchup.

add-222.title: Cheesy Garlic Bread
add-222.culturalNotes: Wrapping the bread in foil first lets the garlic butter soak in, and opening it at the end gives the crunch.

add-222-i6.name: A pinch of salt and oregano

instructions.1: Mix the soft butter with the garlic, parsley, salt and oregano.
instructions.2: Slice the bread diagonally without cutting all the way through, or split lengthwise.
instructions.3: Spread the garlic butter inside the slices and top with the cheese.
instructions.4: Wrap in foil and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, then open the foil and bake 3-4 minutes until the cheese melts and the bread crisps.
instructions.5: Serve hot with pasta or soup.

add-223.title: Slow-Simmered Bone Broth
add-223.culturalNotes: Vinegar helps extract minerals and collagen from the bones, and a successful broth turns to jelly when chilled.

add-223-i1.name: Beef, lamb or chicken bones (with marrow and joints)

add-223-i6.name: Garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns and cinnamon stick

add-223-i7.name: Water
add-223-i7.standardAmount: to cover the bones by 5 cm

instructions.1: Roast the bones at 220°C for 30 minutes until browned (optional, for a darker, richer broth).
instructions.2: Put the bones in a large pot, cover with water, add the vinegar and leave 30 minutes before heating.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil and skim the foam, then add the vegetables and spices.
instructions.4: Simmer on the lowest possible heat for 8-12 hours (4 hours for chicken), topping up with water if needed.
instructions.5: Strain, cool, skim the fat and keep in the fridge 5 days or freeze; salt when using.

add-224.title: Iced Mocha
add-224.culturalNotes: Mocha is a mix of coffee and chocolate. Freezing coffee into ice cubes instead of plain ice stops the drink from getting diluted.

instructions.1: Dissolve the coffee and sugar in the warm water and let cool slightly.
instructions.2: Drizzle lines of chocolate sauce inside the glass.
instructions.3: Whisk or blend the coffee with the milk and a spoon of chocolate sauce until frothy.
instructions.4: Fill the glass with ice, pour the mocha over and top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cocoa.

add-225.title: Homemade Dessert Ashta (Clotted-Style Cream)
add-225.culturalNotes: A stable ashta that doesn't run in the oven or when cut, with little sugar because Middle Eastern sweets are soaked in syrup.

instructions.1: Dissolve the cornflour, cream powder and sugar in the cold milk, then stir constantly over medium heat until very thick.
instructions.2: Remove from the heat, add the orange-blossom water and let it cool to lukewarm, stirring now and then.
instructions.3: Add the canned cream and whisk until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Cover with cling film touching the surface and chill; use to fill qatayef, kunafa and basbousa and to decorate desserts.

add-226.title: Indian Chapati
add-226.culturalNotes: Chapati is an everyday bread in India, East Africa and Yemen. Rolling it with ghee then rolling out again gives soft layers.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and oil, add the water gradually and knead into a smooth, soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Divide into 10 balls, roll each into a thin round, brush with ghee, fold, coil into a spiral and roll out again (for layers).
instructions.3: Heat an iron or non-stick pan and cook each bread until bubbles appear, then flip, brush with ghee and press with a spatula until it puffs and spots golden.
instructions.4: Stack the breads under a cloth and serve with curry and masala.

add-227.title: Karak Chai
add-227.culturalNotes: Karak is the favourite street drink of the Gulf, originally from Indian chai. Letting it boil up several times gives its creamy body and concentrated flavour.

add-227-i2.name: Loose black tea or tea granules

instructions.1: Boil the water with the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon for 3 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the tea and sugar and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until strong and dark.
instructions.3: Add the evaporated milk and saffron and let it rise, then lower the heat and let it rise two or three more times.
instructions.4: Strain and serve hot in small cups.

add-228.title: Egyptian Savory Qaraqeesh (Salted Eid Kaak)
add-228.culturalNotes: Savory qaraqeesh are baked alongside Eid kahk in Egypt and served with tea; fennel and anise give them their distinctive aroma.

instructions.1: Rub the flour with the ghee until fully absorbed.
instructions.2: Add the yeast, sesame, fennel, anise, nigella, sugar and salt, then the warm water gradually, and bring together lightly.
instructions.3: Cover and rest 30-45 minutes until doubled.
instructions.4: Roll part of the dough into a long strip and cut diagonally into fingers, or shape small rings; arrange on trays and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C until the bases colour, then turn on the grill to lightly brown the tops.
instructions.6: Let cool completely to crisp up and store in airtight tins.

add-229.title: Crispy Orange Cookies
add-229.culturalNotes: Economical Eid cookies; the zest carries more flavour than the juice because the aromatic oils are in the peel.

add-229-i8.name: Vanilla and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Cream the butter with the icing sugar and zest, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the orange juice into a smooth dough.
instructions.3: Shape with a cookie press or piping bag, or roll and cut with cutters, onto lined trays.
instructions.4: Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges colour.
instructions.5: Let cool completely to crisp and store in airtight tins.

add-230.title: Hijazi Almond 'Coffee' (Milk and Almond Drink)
add-230.culturalNotes: Almond 'coffee' is a winter drink from the Hijaz, called coffee although it contains none. It is served to guests on cold winter nights.

instructions.1: Blanch the almonds for 2 minutes, peel and crush coarsely.
instructions.2: Dissolve the rice flour and sugar in the cold milk, then heat over medium heat, stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Add the almonds and cardamom and simmer on low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
instructions.4: Add the saffron or rose water and serve hot in cups with almond pieces.

add-231.title: Three-Cheese Mint Samosa
add-231.culturalNotes: Feta gives saltiness, mozzarella the stretch and cheddar a strong flavour, while mint adds freshness to balance the richness.

add-231-i1.name: Feta or salty white cheese, crumbled

add-231-i4.name: Dried mint (or ½ cup fresh, chopped)

add-231-i8.name: Flour and water paste to seal

instructions.1: Mix the three cheeses with the mint, nigella seeds and egg until combined.
instructions.2: Put a spoonful of filling on the edge of each sheet and fold into successive triangles to the end.
instructions.3: Seal the end with the flour paste.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.5: Serve hot with the cheese stretchy.

add-232.title: Chicken, Corn and Mayo Samosa
add-232.culturalNotes: A creative filling children love; samosas can be made and frozen before frying for the Ramadan table.

add-232-i1.name: Boiled chicken breast, finely chopped or shredded

add-232-i6.name: Garlic powder, paprika, salt and black pepper

instructions.1: Mix the chicken with the corn, mayonnaise, cheese, parsley and spices into a creamy filling that holds together.
instructions.2: Fill the sheets and fold into triangles, sealing the end with a flour-and-water paste.
instructions.3: Fry in hot oil until golden, or brush with oil and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

add-233.title: Classic French Chocolate Mousse
add-233.culturalNotes: Classic French mousse uses raw eggs, so use very fresh or pasteurised eggs. Folding gently keeps it light.

add-233-i2.name: Large eggs, separated, at room temperature

add-233-i6.name: Chocolate shavings or berries to decorate

instructions.1: Melt the chocolate over a water bath and let it cool to lukewarm.
instructions.2: Stir the yolks one at a time into the lukewarm chocolate, then the vanilla.
instructions.3: Whip the cream to soft peaks, and whisk the whites with the icing sugar until firm.
instructions.4: Fold the cream into the chocolate gently, then the whites in two additions with a folding motion so the air isn't lost.
instructions.5: Divide into glasses and chill at least 4 hours; decorate before serving.

add-234.title: Fresh Mango Juice
add-234.culturalNotes: Very ripe mangoes provide most of the sweetness. The best varieties for juice are Owais, Zebdia and Fass.

instructions.1: Peel the mangoes and cut the flesh away from the stone.
instructions.2: Blend with the water, sugar and lemon until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Strain if you prefer a light juice and serve chilled at once.
instructions.4: For mango with milk, use cold milk instead of water and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

add-235.title: Watermelon Mint Juice
add-235.culturalNotes: Watermelon needs no water because it is almost all water. Freezing watermelon cubes to use instead of ice keeps the flavour concentrated.

instructions.1: Cut the watermelon into cubes and remove the seeds.
instructions.2: Blend with the lemon, mint and sugar for a few seconds until liquid.
instructions.3: Strain if you like and serve at once over ice.

add-236.title: Classic Vanilla Custard
add-236.culturalNotes: Pouring the hot milk onto the yolks gradually (tempering) stops the eggs curdling. Homemade custard with yolks is far richer than custard powder.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling.
instructions.2: Whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornflour until pale and smooth.
instructions.3: Pour a third of the hot milk gradually onto the yolks, whisking, then return the mixture to the pan.
instructions.4: Stir constantly over medium heat until thick and boiling for a minute, then remove and add the vanilla and butter.
instructions.5: Pour into serving dishes, cover with cling film touching the surface so no skin forms, chill and serve with fruit.

add-237.title: Stovetop Popcorn
add-237.culturalNotes: Leaving a gap for steam makes the popcorn crisp rather than chewy, and removing it as soon as the popping slows stops the bottom burning.

add-237-i5.name: Extras: cheese powder, caramel or paprika

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat with 3 test kernels.
instructions.2: When the three pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover leaving a small gap for steam, and shake the pot now and then.
instructions.3: When the popping slows to two seconds between pops, take the pot off the heat at once.
instructions.4: Tip the popcorn into a large bowl and toss with the salt, butter and extras.

add-238.title: Grilled Corn on the Cob
add-238.culturalNotes: Charcoal-grilled corn is the classic summer snack of the Nile Corniche and Alexandria. Rubbing the cob with a lemon slice dipped in salt and chilli is a popular touch.

instructions.1: Remove the husks and silk, and boil the cobs 5 minutes beforehand if you want to shorten the grilling.
instructions.2: Grill over charcoal, a direct gas flame or a hot grill, turning constantly, until the kernels brown with a few black spots, 10-15 minutes.
instructions.3: Brush with butter while hot, sprinkle with salt, squeeze over lemon and add a pinch of chilli.

add-239.title: Chicken and Vegetable Crêpes
add-239.culturalNotes: Resting the batter before cooking makes the crêpes softer and less likely to tear. Crêpes can be made ahead and frozen between sheets of baking paper.

add-239-i11.name: White sauce or mayonnaise and mustard

add-239-i12.name: Paprika, garlic powder and black pepper

instructions.1: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and oil into a smooth, lump-free batter and rest 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat a lightly greased non-stick pan, pour in a ladleful and swirl to cover the base, cooking a minute each side.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, peppers and mushrooms, add the chicken and spices, then the sauce, and stir.
instructions.4: Put the filling in the middle of each crêpe, sprinkle with cheese and fold into a roll or triangle.
instructions.5: Return to the pan or oven for a few minutes until the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Serve hot with cheese sauce or ketchup.

add-240.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
add-240.culturalNotes: A hot oven and short time are the secret: the crust sets and the centre stays molten. The ramekins can be filled and chilled until baking, adding two minutes.

add-240-i7.name: A pinch of salt and vanilla

add-240-i8.name: Cocoa and butter for the moulds

instructions.1: Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa.
instructions.2: Melt the chocolate with the butter over a water bath until smooth.
instructions.3: Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until pale, add the melted chocolate, then fold in the flour, salt and vanilla gently.
instructions.4: Divide among the ramekins and bake in an oven preheated to 220°C for 10-12 minutes until the edges set and the centre still wobbles.
instructions.5: Leave just one minute, then turn out onto a plate and serve at once with ice cream.

add-241.title: Buttered Corn Cups
add-241.culturalNotes: A light street snack loved by children; frozen corn gives excellent results all year.

add-241-i4.name: Extras: grated cheese, mayonnaise, paprika, chilli, lemon

instructions.1: Boil the corn in salted water for 5 minutes or heat in the microwave, then drain.
instructions.2: Toss with the butter and salt over the heat for a minute until coated.
instructions.3: Divide into cups and add the extras you like (Mexican street style: mayonnaise, cheese, paprika and lemon).

add-242.title: Homemade Shanklish Cheese
add-242.culturalNotes: Traditional shanklish is aged for weeks until a beneficial mould forms; this is a quick, milder home version eaten after a few days.

instructions.1: Strain the yogurt in a clean cloth hung over a bowl in the fridge for 24 hours until it becomes very dry labneh.
instructions.2: Mix with the salt, chilli and spices.
instructions.3: Shape into balls the size of a small orange with oiled hands.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray lined with baking paper in a dry, cool, airy place for 3-4 days until the outside dries.
instructions.5: Roll the balls in dried thyme or chilli and keep in a jar covered with olive oil or in the fridge.

add-243.title: Mint Yogurt Sauce
add-243.culturalNotes: A refreshing Indian-style sauce; the little sugar balances the heat of the chilli and lemon. Without yogurt it becomes a green chutney that keeps longer.

instructions.1: Grind the mint, coriander, garlic, chilli, lemon, sugar and salt in a processor into a paste.
instructions.2: Add the olive oil gradually with the processor running.
instructions.3: Mix the paste with the yogurt and serve cold with grills, samosa and pakora; keeps two days in the fridge.

add-244.title: Fruit and Avocado Salad
add-244.culturalNotes: Avocado adds a creamy texture and healthy fats that make the salad more filling; it goes in last so it isn't mashed.

instructions.1: Cube the avocado and sprinkle at once with lemon juice so it doesn't brown.
instructions.2: Cut the rest of the fruit and toss gently with the avocado in a bowl.
instructions.3: Mix the honey with the orange and lemon juice.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over the fruit, sprinkle with mint and serve cold at once.

add-245.title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
add-245.culturalNotes: Browning the mushrooms until their water evaporates before adding stock gives the soup a deep flavour instead of a boiled-mushroom taste.

instructions.1: Soften the onion in the butter, then the garlic for a minute.
instructions.2: Add the mushrooms and stir on high heat until they release their water, it evaporates and they brown slightly; set a handful aside to garnish.
instructions.3: Sprinkle in the flour and stir a minute, then add the stock gradually and the thyme and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Blend the soup smooth with a stick blender, or leave it chunky.
instructions.5: Add the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper, heat without boiling and serve garnished with the browned mushrooms and parsley.

add-246.title: Egyptian-Style Everyday Pasta with Meat Sauce
add-246.culturalNotes: Everyday pasta is the quick weeknight meal of the Egyptian home. The pasta water binds the sauce to the pasta and makes it glossy.

add-246-i8.name: Mixed spice, black pepper and salt

instructions.1: Boil the pasta in salted water until cooked and drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat, garlic and spices until done.
instructions.3: Add the tomato paste, then the tomato juice, and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Toss the pasta in the sauce with a little of the cooking water and serve sprinkled with roumi cheese.

add-247.title: Soft Homemade Burger Buns
add-247.culturalNotes: Milk, butter and egg give burger buns their familiar softness, and shaping tight balls makes them rise evenly.

instructions.1: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the milk and egg, then add the butter and knead 10 minutes until smooth and glossy.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 equal pieces, shape into tight balls, arrange on a lined tray and press lightly.
instructions.4: Leave 45 minutes until puffed, brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame.
instructions.5: Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Cover with a cloth as soon as they come out so they stay soft.

add-248.title: Berry Yogurt Smoothie
add-248.culturalNotes: Yogurt adds protein and good bacteria, and oats make it a filling breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk and yogurt in the blender first, then the berries, honey and oats.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once.

add-249.title: Egyptian Fino (Samoli) Bread Rolls
add-249.culturalNotes: Fino is Egypt's favourite sandwich bread. Steam in the oven gives it a thin, glossy, crisp crust.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt, sugar and yeast, add the warm water and knead, then add the oil and knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 pieces, roll each into a rectangle, then roll up tightly and shape into a long roll with tapered ends.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray and leave 45 minutes until puffed, then slash lengthwise with a sharp blade.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes with a tray of water at the bottom of the oven for steam, until golden.
instructions.6: Cool on a rack.

add-250.title: Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie
add-250.culturalNotes: A protein- and energy-rich smoothie, good after exercise or as a quick breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk in the blender first, then the banana, peanut butter, honey and extras.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once with a pinch of cinnamon.

add-251.title: Breaded Fried Liver
add-251.culturalNotes: Liver toughens if overcooked or salted too early, so fry it quickly over high heat to keep it tender inside.

instructions.1: Pound the liver slices gently to make them thin and even and remove the membranes.
instructions.2: Marinate with the garlic, lemon, cumin and pepper for 30 minutes, adding the salt just before coating.
instructions.3: Coat each slice in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil for 1½-2 minutes per side until just golden.
instructions.5: Drain and serve at once with lemon, tahini and fries.

add-252.title: Spiced Sausage (Sujuk) Skillet
add-252.culturalNotes: Oriental sausage (Alexandrian sausage or maqaniq) cooks in its own fat, so little oil is needed. Pomegranate molasses gives a tangy Levantine taste.

instructions.1: Cut the sausage into pieces or rings.
instructions.2: Brown the sausage in the oil until coloured and releasing its fat, then lift out.
instructions.3: Soften the onion, garlic and peppers in the same oil.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes and spices and stir until soft, then return the sausage and toss with the pomegranate molasses for 2 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve hot in bread or with fried eggs.

add-253.title: Spicy Egyptian Feshah (Sautéed Lungs)
add-253.culturalNotes: Feshah is a popular Eid al-Adha dish in Egypt; boiling it well first with vinegar and spices removes its smell and tenderises it.

add-253-i2.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and vinegar

add-253-i7.name: Cumin, chilli, mixed spice and black pepper

instructions.1: Wash the lungs well with water and vinegar and cut into large pieces.
instructions.2: Boil with the onion, bay leaves and cardamom for 45 minutes until cooked, skimming, then drain and cut into small cubes.
instructions.3: Brown the onion in the ghee, then the garlic and peppers.
instructions.4: Add the lungs and stir on high heat until the edges brown, then the tomatoes, paste and spices, stirring until cooked down and dry.
instructions.5: Squeeze over lemon and serve hot with baladi bread.

add-254.title: Egyptian Tripe (Kersha) with Chickpeas
add-254.culturalNotes: Tripe needs careful cleaning and long cooking; a pressure cooker saves a lot of time. The garlic and vinegar dressing is the soul of this Egyptian dish.

add-254-i2.name: For cleaning: coarse salt, vinegar, lemon and flour

add-254-i3.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and mastic

instructions.1: Scrub the tripe with coarse salt, flour, vinegar and lemon, scrape and rinse several times until white and odour-free.
instructions.2: Blanch 10 minutes and discard the water, then boil in fresh water with the aromatics for 2-3 hours (or an hour in a pressure cooker) until completely tender.
instructions.3: Cut the tripe into small squares, keeping a cup of the broth.
instructions.4: Soften the onion in the ghee, then the garlic, deglaze with the vinegar, then add the tomato juice, spices and broth.
instructions.5: Add the tripe and chickpeas and simmer 20 minutes until thickened.
instructions.6: Serve hot in deep bowls with lemon and bread.

add-255.title: White Bean Salad
add-255.culturalNotes: A salad rich in protein and fibre that makes a light full meal. It improves after an hour in the fridge.

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, then boil in fresh water until tender but not mushy; drain and let cool.
instructions.2: Mix the beans with the cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley.
instructions.3: Whisk the lemon, oil, garlic and spices.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over, toss and leave 15 minutes to absorb the flavours before serving.

add-256.title: Qashtouta (Phyllo Nut Bombs with Ashta)
add-256.culturalNotes: Qashtouta is a modern Egyptian sweet that spread in Ramadan, combining crisp filo with soft ashta and nuts in one bite.

add-256-i4.name: Mixed crushed nuts (pistachio, almond, walnut, hazelnut)

add-256-i6.name: Sugar and cinnamon for the nuts

instructions.1: Mix the nuts with the coconut, sugar and cinnamon.
instructions.2: Cut the filo into large squares and brush 3 layers with ghee, stacking them.
instructions.3: Put a spoon of ashta and a spoon of nuts in the centre, gather the edges up into a parcel (the 'bomb') and press.
instructions.4: Pack the parcels tightly in a greased tray and brush with ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Pour over the cold syrup as soon as they come out and garnish with pistachios.

add-257.title: Harrak Osbao (Lentils with Pasta, Tamarind and Pomegranate)
add-257.culturalNotes: Harrak osbao is a Damascene Lenten dish whose name means 'he burned his finger', because people rush to eat it before it cools. The tang of pomegranate molasses and tamarind sets it apart.

add-257-i2.name: Dough (flour, water, salt) cut into small squares, or small pasta

instructions.1: Boil the lentils in plenty of water until cooked but still holding their shape.
instructions.2: Knead a stiff dough of flour, water and salt, roll thin and cut into small squares; fry half until crisp and keep for garnish.
instructions.3: Add the other half of the dough to the lentils and cook until done and thickened, then add the pomegranate molasses, tamarind, cumin and salt.
instructions.4: Fry half the onions, sliced, in olive oil until brown and crisp; chop the rest and sauté with the garlic and coriander, then add to the lentils.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish, let it cool slightly, and garnish with the crispy onion, fried dough, toasted bread and coriander; serve warm or cold.
